body:
💡 **What:** Introduced an in-memory variable `cachedValidatableGames` in `backend/server.js` for the `/api/games/validatable` endpoint to cache parsed and mapped data from `data_cekid.json`.
🎯 **Why:** The endpoint previously executed a synchronous `fs.readFile` and `JSON.parse` on every request. For a relatively static 1,300-line configuration file, this creates unnecessary disk I/O and CPU overhead under load. Caching the data prevents these repeated expensive operations.
📊 **Impact:** Significantly reduces the response time for the endpoint by avoiding file system reads and synchronous JSON parsing blockages for all subsequent requests after the first.
🔬 **Measurement:** Verify the optimization by checking endpoint execution time locally and observing reduced disk reads and CPU overhead under load. All unit tests for routing and endpoints pass.

author: spareilleux
body:
## Summary

Two follow-up bug fixes on top of #307 (Tonal Orbit v1):

1. **Wheel / pinch zoom now persists** — was snapping back every frame because the focus-transition lerp ran unconditionally.
2. **Responsive HUD layout** — bottom-row FOCUS pill and title chip no longer collide on phones; breadcrumb no longer collides with CastButton on narrow viewports.

## Bug 1 — Zoom snaps back

The animation loop ran `camera.position.lerp(cameraTargetPos, ease)` on every frame, so any user wheel-zoom or pinch was immediately overwritten by the lerp back to the previous focus-target position.

**Fix:** gate the lerp behind a `cameraAnimating` flag.
- Set true by `updateCameraTarget()` when a focus transition is armed (i.e. user tapped a body).
- Cleared either when the lerp converges (within `CAMERA_SETTLE_EPS = 0.05`) **or** when the user grabs OrbitControls, wired via `controls.addEventListener('start', …)` which fires on any wheel / pinch / drag-rotate.

Result: tap-to-focus still flies the camera smoothly, but once the camera settles (or the user takes control mid-flight) OrbitControls owns the camera and the user's zoom persists.

**Manually verified** with a `?test=zoom` harness that simulates a user drag at +1.5s and reads back the camera distance immediately and 1s later. Before the fix the lerp would pull the camera back to its home position within 1s; after the fix the distance changed (e.g. 44.27 → 8.00) and stayed at 8.00 a second later.

## Bug 2 — Layout

### Before (live demo, mobile 414px)
- App header (`← Back / Home / Test / Tonal Orbit / Demos (Por…`) overflows right
- FOCUS pill + title chip (`TONAL ORBIT · v1 · perf=…`) collide; \"perf\" gets cut off
- Tap targets near right edge unreliable

### Before (any viewport)
- `height: 100vh` Container overflowed `.mainContent` (which is `flex: 1` of a `min-height: 100vh` flex column with a sticky breadcrumb), clipping the bottom of the canvas

### Fixes in `TonalOrbitTest.tsx`
- Container: `height: 100vh` → `height: 100%` so it fills its flex parent exactly
- Breadcrumb pill: `maxWidth: 'calc(100% - 32px)'` → `'calc(100% - 160px)'` + `overflowX: 'auto'` so it never collides with the top-right CastButton on narrow viewports
- FOCUS pill: dropped fixed `minWidth: 260`, switched to responsive `maxWidth: { xs: 'calc(100% - 40px)', sm: 'calc(100% - 260px)' }`
- Title chip: `display: { xs: 'none', sm: 'block' }` — hidden below sm so the FOCUS pill can take the full bottom row on phones

### Fix in `TonalOrbit.tsx`
- Added `ResizeObserver(container)` next to the existing `window.resize` listener — MUI styles can settle a few frames after mount, so the initial `clientHeight` could be undersized. The observer also fires on parent flex layout changes that don't trigger a window resize.
- Wrapped renderer-resize in a `W < 1 || H < 1` guard to skip transient zero-size measurements during mount/unmount.

## Test harness (kept for regression)

Added a `?test=zoom` opt-in URL param that:
1. Tags the canvas with `data-test=zoom`
2. Simulates a user drag at +1.5s
3. Writes `data-zoom-test=\"initial=… afterAction=… afterWait1s=…\"` to the body

The TonalOrbit render loop only writes camera state to DOM attrs when that tag is present, so production renders pay **zero** cost. The harness is useful for CI / headless verification that future changes don't reintroduce the snap-back bug.

## Visual proof

| viewport | before (live #307) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| desktop 1920×1080 | `live-desktop.png` — white strip bottom | `final-desktop.png` — clean canvas fill |
| tablet 768×1024 | (not previously captured) | `final-tablet.png` — pill + chip both visible, no overlap |
| mobile 414×896 | `live-mobile.png` — chip overlaps pill, \"perf\" clipped | `final-mobile.png` — chip hidden, pill stretches to full width |

(Screenshots captured locally with headless Chrome during development; deployed at `https://demos.guitaralchemist.com/test/tonal-orbit` after merge.)

## Test plan

- [ ] On desktop: load `/test/tonal-orbit`, scroll-wheel zoom in — camera distance changes and stays.
- [ ] On desktop: tap a pitch planet — camera flies in. Mid-flight, scroll-wheel — wheel wins, ease releases.
- [ ] On mobile (375–414px): visit `/test/tonal-orbit?perf=low` — confirm FOCUS pill stretches, title chip hidden, breadcrumb doesn't overlap Cast button.
- [ ] Tablet (~768px): both pill and chip visible side-by-side with breathing room.
- [ ] Regression: `/test/tonal-orbit?tour=auto` still cycles the camera (opt-in only; nothing in `?test=zoom` interferes).
- [ ] Typecheck baseline unchanged (185).

Cleanup PR (delete old `Sunburst3D.tsx` files) is still on hold — user wants longer A/B comparison window.

## Summary
Replaces the placeholder Results page with a **live-generating founder playbook** across four dimensions, each completing in 5–7 seconds. All four tabs are clickable at any time. README rewritten for hackathon judges naming Gemini 3.5 Flash, RocketRide Pipeline, and GMI Inference.

| **Traction** | Streaming table of 18 curated dev/AI events (logos, fit badge, date, location, custom "why this one", RSVP CTA, city filter). |
| **Funding** | Streaming table of 25 VCs (stage chips, check size, why-this-fits). Click any row → Gmail-style cold-email panel with subject + body personalized per partner from their published thesis; Send (mailto), Copy, partner picker, LinkedIn links. |
| **Advise** | Three video tiles: clip 1 reveals after ~1.5s, clip 2 after ~6.5s, the third has an idle Generate CTA that simulates rendering on click. |

body:
### Motivation
- Fix the Phase‑1 QR/menu checkout bugs where the Payment step showed amount 0 after submit and the unpaid order could not be reopened or restored after closing or refresh. 
- Ensure the payment step uses the submitted order snapshot/pending backend summary instead of the possibly-cleared cart total. 
- Prevent public order creation from fatal errors when the CashDrawerService autoload/class is missing so orders do not fail for tenants without configured cash drawer hardware.

### Description
- Frontend: `frontend/app/menu/page.tsx` — added `initialSubmittedOrder` prop to `PaymentModal`, hydrate-on-open logic, and a `payableTotal` memo that selects `submittedSnapshot.total`, `pendingSummary.remainingAmount`, or falls back to cart `finalTotal` when computing amounts passed to payment providers.  
- Frontend: `frontend/app/menu/page.tsx` — persist submitted unpaid order snapshot into localStorage under key `pmd_open_order:{tenant}:{tableKey}` and use `pmd_guest_session_id` for guest session stability; snapshot includes `orderId`, `status`, `paymentStatus`, `total`, `currency`, `submittedItems`, `createdAt`. 
- Frontend: `frontend/app/menu/page.tsx` — restore local unpaid order on page load, expose `My Order / Pay` chip safely inside `MenuContent` (component scope) and pass restored snapshot into `PaymentModal` so reopening after close/refresh shows the correct unpaid order and amount. 
- Backend/helper: `app/Helpers/CashDrawerHelper.php` — added a defensive `class_exists(\Admin\Services\CashDrawerService\CashDrawerService::class)` guard and a warning log so public order creation will skip drawer open when the service class is unavailable instead of throwing a fatal error.

### Testing
- Ran PHP syntax check with `php -l app/Helpers/CashDrawerHelper.php` and it passed without syntax errors. 
- Attempted frontend build with `cd frontend && npm run build` but the Next.js build failed in this environment due to Google Fonts fetch/connectivity during the Turbopack step (external fetch), which is unrelated to the payment logic changes. 
- Manual/behavioural validation performed in code: submit flow now records backend `order_id` and prefers `(response as any)?.total` for the snapshot, and payment UI reads `submittedSnapshot.total` or `pendingSummary.remainingAmount` first so payment amount no longer becomes 0 after cart clear.

author: niklasrosenstein
body:
## Summary

- Consolidates dev environment bootstrap into a single `./scripts/dev-setup.sh` that works on macOS as well as Linux. Drops the previous `mise setup:hosts` / `mise setup:docker` tasks and the inline shell in `minikube:up` / `k3s:up` -- replaced by `mise setup` (script wrapper). No more `depends` chains that swallowed sudo's TTY.
- macOS portability: writes to `~/.docker/daemon.json` (Docker Desktop) instead of the missing `/etc/docker/daemon.json`; uses portable field-based `awk` for `/etc/hosts` / `.env` edits (BSD `awk` silently ignored the previous word-boundary syntax); host IP via `route -n get` + `ifconfig | awk` (more reliable than `ipconfig getifaddr`, which returns empty for cellular/tether/utun interfaces); explicit Docker Desktop restart (`stop` then wait for processes then `open -b com.docker.docker` then poll up to 180s), since `docker desktop restart` was observed to report success while leaving the engine dead.
- Idempotency: `setup_docker` short-circuits when `daemon.json` already has rise registries. `setup_minikube` reuses an existing cluster (kubectl-context probe -- `minikube status` breaks on multi-network setups), always points `kubectl current-context` at `minikube`, skips the ingress port-forward when :8080 is already in use, and prompts `[keep/recreate/skip]` when a cluster is already running.
- `/etc/hosts` is now a managed block bracketed by marker lines -- re-runs cleanly replace the block (no accumulating entries) and `hosts-clear` fully undoes it. The block opportunistically enumerates `*.rise.local` ingress hostnames from the current cluster.
- Symmetric teardown: `./scripts/dev-setup.sh down` (or `mise down`) walks setup in reverse with one confirmation -- kill port-forward, cluster delete, strip `.env` block, remove rise registries from `daemon.json`, strip `/etc/hosts` block.
- Standalone ingress port-forward control via `mise setup pf` / `mise setup pf-down` (idempotent background start/stop).
- `mise dev` preflight checks (hosts, Docker, k8s) are inlined into the task and prompt `Continue anyway? [y/N]` on failure rather than hard-exiting -- removing the now-redundant `check:hosts`, `check:docker`, `check:k8s` tasks.
- `sqlx:check` moved from `rust-quality` CI job (no DB) to `unit-tests-linux` (has Postgres), fixing the `sqlx-cli 0.9` breakage where `prepare --check` now always needs a live database.

## Test plan

- [x] On macOS: `mise setup` succeeds end-to-end (hosts, daemon.json, optional Docker Desktop restart, minikube cluster, ingress port-forward, `.env` written).
- [x] Re-running `mise setup` is idempotent: no duplicate `/etc/hosts` lines, no duplicate `daemon.json` entries, no needless Docker Desktop restart prompt, existing minikube cluster kept and prompted as `[keep/recreate/skip]`.
- [x] `./scripts/dev-setup.sh pf` after `minikube` brings up port-forward; `pf-down` kills it; `lsof -i :8080` reflects state correctly.
- [x] `./scripts/dev-setup.sh hosts` after deploying a project picks up the new `*.rise.local` ingress hostname.
- [ ] `mise down` cleanly undoes everything (port-forward, cluster, .env block, daemon.json registries, /etc/hosts block) with one prompt.
- [ ] `./scripts/dev-setup.sh preflight` runs only hosts + docker and exits.
- [ ] `./scripts/dev-setup.sh k3s` on macOS errors out cleanly; `k3s-down` does the same.
- [ ] On Linux: `mise setup` configures `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, restarts docker via systemctl, brings up the chosen cluster.
- [ ] `mise dev` with a missing preflight condition lists issues and prompts to continue; answering `y` proceeds, anything else exits.

## Summary
Adds Hypothesis-based property tests for the canonical own-column resolver `_own_table_column` (shared by SEC005, SEC018, SEC030, PERF003). Pure tests-only PR: a new test module + adding `hypothesis>=6.0` to the `dev` optional-deps.

Where example-based tests pin specific shapes we've thought to enumerate, the property tests cover the **combinatorial space** — random tuples of random strings against tables with random `schema`/`name`. The six properties:

| Property | What it asserts |
| --- | --- |
| 1-tuple → returns the col | Unqualified refs are always treated as own-table |
| 2-tuple matching qualifier | Returns the col when qualifier == table.name |
| 2-tuple non-matching | Returns None when qualifier != table.name |
| 3-tuple matching | Returns the col when both schema and table match |
| 4+-part tuple → None | Cross-database refs are uniformly unresolved |
| Never raises | Total-function contract — no AssertionError, KeyError, etc., for any input |

**All 6 pass on the current implementation.** No bugs surfaced — that's the expected outcome for mature code. Their value is as regression guards: if a future refactor inadvertently narrows the input domain (an `isinstance` check that rejects empty strings; a tighter type annotation), Hypothesis will catch the contract narrowing at the property level rather than waiting for someone to hit the gap with a real policy.

Hypothesis added to `dev` only — not to the `testing` extra, since it's a contributor tool, not something downstream consumers of `pgrls.testing` need.

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check tests/test_property_resolvers.py` — clean
- [x] `pytest tests/test_property_resolvers.py` — 6 passed
- [x] No source changes; no version bump
- [ ] CI green on PG 15 / 16 / 17 (the Hypothesis tests are pure-Python, don't need PG; the existing 1846 tests are unaffected)

author: ericlevine
body:
## Summary

- When a model response carries multiple tool_uses and at least one needs approval, hold the whole turn under one coalesced approval. A single user yes/no releases or denies every held call together — preserving the model's original turn order so dependent sequences (Bash producing output a following WebFetch consumes) still execute in order on release.
- Mixed turns also coalesce: an auto-allow Bash alongside a review-flagged WebFetch are held together and run in one batch at release. Inline-task and hard-deny turns fall back to the legacy per-tool path unchanged.
- Audit emits one `lite_proxy.approval.release` row per release event with per-tool detail under `params.held_tools[]`, avoiding the `UNIQUE(user_id, request_id, COALESCE(task_id, ''))` canonical dedup index that would otherwise silently collapse N rows.

## How it works

Pass 1 runs the existing per-tool eval with buffered `PendingApprovals` and audit wrappers — no per-tool state is committed to the underlying cache or audit store until the coalesce decision is made. After pass 1:

- **Coalesce mode** (≥2 tool_uses, ≥1 needs approval, no inline-task hold, no hard deny): commit one coalesced hold and emit `coalesced_approval_pending` audit rows; re-run the rewriter with a coalesced eval producing one combined approval prompt.
- **Legacy mode** (everything else): replay the buffered per-tool holds atomically. Any single Hold failure rolls back the batch and surfaces `SkippedReason` so the handler emits 502 — matching the pre-change inline "approval unavailable" semantic.

Release synthesizes a multi-tool response (Anthropic JSON+SSE, OpenAI Chat+Responses) so the harness executes every approved call from one user gesture. `rewriteApprovedToolUses` re-evaluates each held tool_use against current state and fails closed for the whole batch if any single re-eval refuses (decision changed, fingerprint diverged, boundary failed, nonce mint failed) — no half-executed turns.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI `go build ./...` green
- [ ] CI `go vet ./...` green
- [ ] CI `go test ./...` green (passes locally; new coverage in `coalesce_test.go` for: coalesced hold creation, mixed turns, single-tool legacy preservation, turn order preservation through release, coalesced hold failure fallback, bounded cache eviction safety, legacy replay failure fail-closed, partial replay rollback, configured TTL preservation, sibling metadata preservation, audit dedup avoidance)
- [ ] Multi-tool turn UX: send a model response with 2+ tool_uses that hit a `review` rule; verify ONE prompt is rendered (not N) and `yes` releases every call in original order
- [ ] Mixed turn: review-flagged WebFetch + auto-allow Bash in one response; verify both held and both run on `yes`
- [ ] Inline-task path: existing `task` verb flow still works for single-tool reviews
- [ ] Audit: confirm `lite_proxy.approval.release` rows carry `held_tools` array for coalesced releases and that single-tool holds remain shape-compatible with dashboards

## Summary
Diagnostic continued. After #33, server logs show no `from=<mobile>` lines at all after the user accepts on the phone — but we also don't see any `_send skipped` / `send_json failed`, so we can't tell whether:
- mobile WS is wedged (no sends at all reach the server, but TCP still open so `application_state == CONNECTED`)
- mobile webrtcService.endCall / joinCall isn't actually calling `wsService.send`

This logs every inbound WS message (`[ws][in] user=N event=X`) except pings. Run a call test and look at lines for the mobile user_id during the call — that tells us exactly which side of the wire is broken.

## Test plan
- [ ] Make a desktop→mobile call, accept on phone, wait 30s
- [ ] Inspect server logs for `[ws][in] user=<mobile_id> event=...` lines
- [ ] Zero events at all → mobile WS is wedged
- [ ] Pings only (which we skip — so look for nothing OR run with the skip removed) → silent send-side bug

Easy to revert.

## Summary

This PR adds full support for running the seats.aero MCP server as a remote HTTP service so it can be used with **Grok** (via xAI's Remote MCP connectors) while keeping full backward compatibility with local stdio usage.

### Key Changes

- **Remote MCP over Streamable HTTP** (`src/server/http.ts`)
  - Stateless `StreamableHTTPServerTransport`
  - Simple bearer token auth via `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` (protects your seats.aero quota)
  - Dual-mode binary (`MCP_TRANSPORT=http` or `PORT` → HTTP mode)
  - `/healthz` endpoint for hosting platforms

- **New `get_trips` tool**
  - Returns full segments, taxes, and **booking links** from an availability ID
  - Essential for actually booking Aeroplan awards

- **Schema & API completeness**
  - Support for `sources` (e.g. `"aeroplan"`), `cabins`, `minify_trips`, etc.
  - Updated source list (now includes finnair, lufthansa, frontier, spirit)
  - Fixed several small validation bugs

- **Comprehensive test suite** (19 tests)
  - Schema, tool logic, and full HTTP integration tests (including auth)

- **Documentation & DX**
  - Major README refresh with remote Grok usage instructions
  - New `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  - CI with build + tests + Docker validation
  - Dependabot + PR template

### Commits

- `feat`: Core remote transport + get_trips
- `test`: Full test coverage
- `docs`: README + CONTRIBUTING
- `ci`: GitHub Actions, Dependabot, PR template

### Verification

- All tests pass (`pnpm test:run`)

body:
Implemented the MT-LiveExecutor, a procedural MQL5 script that enables real-time execution of trading strategies described in natural language (Portuguese). 

Key features:
- **NLP Parser:** Converts Portuguese text segments into actionable trading rules.
- **Rule Engine:** Evaluates technical indicators (MA, RSI, Stochastic, Bollinger Bands) and micro-structure data (Aggression Delta, Volume).

- The popup is created once during map initialization and reused for all hover interactions, reducing DOM churn

## Impeccable Design Audit — thread-impeccable-audit

Full three-phase design audit: PRODUCT.md creation, site-wide audit, bill detail UX critique. Seven fixes applied.

### Fixes Applied

**F1 — `--text-secondary` undefined (HIGH)**
`bill/[id]/page.js` referenced `var(--text-secondary)` in three places — the AI summary body text, the summary textarea, and the timeline "Show all" button. `--text-secondary` is not defined in globals.css. Fixed:
- Summary body text: `var(--text-secondary)` → `var(--text-mid)` (correct reading weight)
- Summary textarea: `var(--text-secondary)` → `var(--text-primary)` (user-typed content should be primary)
- Timeline button: `var(--text-secondary)` → `var(--text-muted)` (correct tertiary weight)

**F2 — `--text-faint` green-tinted (MEDIUM)**
`globals.css`: `--text-faint: #3d4d42` had a Shorepine-legacy green cast (G channel dominant). Changed to `#3d4050` — same luminance, neutral/blue-leaning, no green contamination.

**F3 — Score formula hides dominant number on no-multiplier bills (HIGH)**
`bill/[id]/page.js`: The 32px brass score number only rendered inside the `xfMult !== 1` conditional. Bills without a momentum multiplier showed only "BASE 45" in 13px muted text — no dominant number. Restructured: 32px score now always visible; the BASE × multiplier = formula prefix only shows when a multiplier exists.

**F4 — Duplicate bill title in Playfair Display (MEDIUM)**
`bill/[id]/page.js`: Bill title rendered twice — compact identity header (Playfair 15px, above score) and BILL IDENTITY block (Playfair 18px, below AI summary). Suppressed the title line from the BILL IDENTITY block. That block now opens directly with the companion pill, RCW cites, and political context — which is its actual job.

**F5 — "SHOREPINE" comment in CSS root (LOW)**
`globals.css` line 4 comment updated: "SHOREPINE DARK INTELLIGENCE THEME" → "VECTOR | WA DARK INTELLIGENCE THEME".

**F6 — Score block gradient top anchor (LOW)**
`bill/[id]/page.js` (×2): Score formula block background changed from `linear-gradient(135deg, #0e1014 …)` to `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--bg) …)` so the top of the gradient follows the design token.

**F7 — Refresh button near-invisible (LOW)**
`page.js` (home): Refresh button opacity changed from `refreshing ? 0.3 : 0.5` to `refreshing ? 0.4 : 0.7`. The control was barely visible at rest.

author: shoaibrain
body:
## Summary

Hotfix for PR #170's failed second deploy attempt. CFN auto-rolled back; prod state unchanged. This PR fixes the underlying issue + adds a CLAUDE.md rule so the cross-stack export trap can't repeat.

**TL;DR:** PR #170's explicit Lambda function name triggered replacement → ARN changed → `TenantApiAuthorizerArn` Output value changed → CFN blocks because analytics-stack actively imports it. Fix: drop the explicit function name (CDK auto-name stays, no replacement); use `\${stageVariables.authorizerFn}` in the function-name slot of authorizerUri (per AWS docs, this slot supports stage vars; region/account still must be literal which we already do).

## What broke + why my review missed it

Deploy error:
```text
Cannot update export TenantApiAuthorizerArn as it is in use by analytics-stack.
```

My Layer 1 cdk diff review listed the Output deltas visibly (`AvailabilityZones`, `ApiGatewayUrl`, `ApiGateway/TenantApi/Endpoint`) and the resource diffs (Lambda replace, Permission replace). I classified the Output template changes as "behaviorally identical resolved values" without auditing for cross-stack importers. The cdk diff format doesn't tell you which Outputs are imported by other stacks — that information has to be cross-referenced explicitly with `aws cloudformation list-imports`.

## Architect subagent review

Spawned a `general-purpose` subagent for an architect-level second opinion. Key findings:

- Diagnosis correct
- Option A' (pin functionName to existing CDK-auto-generated name) won't work: CFN treats "FunctionName property was unset, now is set" as a property change regardless of value → still triggers replacement. **Confirmed empirically via cdk synth on the pinning attempt.**
- Cross-stack import audit on at-risk exports: only `TenantApiAuthorizerArn` has a consumer (analytics-stack). `AvailabilityZones`, `ApiGatewayUrl`, `ApiGateway/TenantApi/Endpoint` have no importers → safe to mutate.
- Recommended Option A: stage-var in function-name slot only; keep CDK auto-name; no replacement
- Future architectural endpoint: Option C (SSM Parameter migration) decouples cross-stack ARN handoff from CFN exports — queue as follow-up after R41.A unblocks

## What changed

### `server/lib/shared-infra/api-gateway.ts`

- **Removed** explicit `functionName` on the PythonFunction. CDK auto-generated name (`shared-infra-stack-ApiGatewayAuthorizerFunction287-uwe63J51voUg`) stays → no Lambda replacement → no ARN change → no cross-stack collision.
- **Substitution map:** `{{authorizer_function}}` now substitutes to `\${stageVariables.authorizerFn}` (was the explicit `'tenant-api-authorizer-prod'` literal). region/account stay literal at synth (env-bound, unchanged from PR #170 hotfix).
- **Stage.Variables grows** from 2 keys to 3: adds `authorizerFn: authorizerFunction.functionName`. CFN resolves this token at deploy time to the existing Lambda's function name.

### `server/lib/shared-infra/api-gateway.spec.ts`

- Strict cardinality assertion: Stage.Variables has exactly 3 keys
- authorizerUri regex matches `function:\${stageVariables.authorizerFn}/invocations` (stage var, not literal)
- Anti-regression: still asserts region/accountId NOT in Stage.Variables (they must be literal in the spec)

### `CLAUDE.md`

NEW rule under § House rules: **Cross-stack export change pre-flight.** Documents the audit procedure (`aws cloudformation list-imports --export-name <X>`) + lists known importers from current audit + 3 resolution patterns (don't-trigger-change / SSM-decouple / coordinated-multi-stack deploy). body:
## Summary

Adds production-grade observability to the notification system — turning the async dispatch pipeline from a black box into an instrumented, traceable, and monitorable service.

### What was added

- **JSON structured logging** with `logstash-logback-encoder` — profile-aware (text console for dev, JSON file with rotation for prod)
- **Correlation ID tracing** via `CorrelationIdFilter` (first in the filter chain) — propagates across `@Async` boundaries through a `TaskDecorator` on the executor
- **Micrometer metrics** — 3 counters (`notification.dispatched`, `notification.retry.total`), 1 timer (`notification.dispatch.duration`), 3 thread pool gauges — all exposed via `/actuator/metrics` (authenticated)
- **Custom health indicators** — `DispatchHealthIndicator` (thread pool saturation), `ExternalApiHealthIndicator` (photo API ping), built-in `DataSourceHealthIndicator` — all under `/actuator/health` (public)
- **Graceful shutdown** configured (30s timeout)

### Architecture decisions

See `docs/05-technical-decisions.md` section 9 for the full reasoning, including:
- Why Micrometer over OpenTelemetry
- Why `TaskDecorator` over manual MDC copy
- Why metrics live in the listener, not the dispatcher
- Why `/health` is public but `/metrics` requires auth
- Filter chain ordering rationale

### Test plan

- **216 tests passing** (0 failures, 0 skipped) — 56 new tests
- Unit: `CorrelationIdFilterTest` (8), `DispatchHealthIndicatorTest` (8), `ExternalApiHealthIndicatorTest` (5), `AsyncConfigTest` (9), `NotificationDispatchListenerTest` (+8)
- Integration: `CorrelationIdIntegrationTest` (3 — end-to-end MDC through async dispatch), `HealthIntegrationTest` (14), `HealthEndpointIntegrationTest` (2)

| `README.md` | New Observability section, test count 160→216, removed from Areas to Improve |

| `src/main/java/.../config/health/ExternalApiHealthIndicator.java` | **New** — API reachability ping |

author: don-petry
body:
## Summary

The `compliance-retrigger.sh` script silently swallowed `gh api` failures, masking the daily retrigger as successful while no issues were actually re-triggered.

## Root cause

```bash
issues=$(gh api ... --jq '.items[]' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
```

When `gh api` returned HTTP error (e.g., search rate-limit, missing scope, transient 5xx):
- The error JSON went to **stdout** (not stderr).
- `2>/dev/null` only discarded stderr.
- `|| echo ""` didn't fire because stdout was non-empty.
- The while loop iterated once with the error JSON as the iteration value.
- `jq -r '.number'` etc. extracted `"null"` for every field.
- Log line: `[info] Skipping null#null (null) — created null, not yet stale`
- Summary: `0 retriggered, 1 skipped` — script marked successful.

This is why the org accumulated ~40 stale compliance issues over 3 days despite the daily workflow running and 'succeeding' each time.

## Fix

- Capture raw response separately from jq extraction.
- Check gh api exit code; abort with a clear error and dump the response if non-zero.
- Additionally detect error-shape JSON (\`{ "message": ..., no "items" }\`) with exit 0 - defensive.
- Log total_count so operators can see how many matches the search returned.
- Use \`jq -c\` to ensure one-line-per-object.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge.
- [ ] Trigger workflow manually with \`gh workflow run compliance-retrigger.yml --repo petry-projects/.github\`.
- [ ] Confirm log shows \`search/issues returned N matching issues\` and re-trigger lines.
- [ ] If the CI run reveals the underlying API failure cause, follow up.

body:
## Problema

PR #61 introdujo `.github/workflows/ci.yml` con dos bugs descubiertos al mergear a main:

### Bug 1
```yaml
if: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_STAGING_URL != '' }}  # job-level
```
GitHub Actions no permite `secrets.*` en `if` job-level. Rompía parsing → todos los runs fallaban en 0s.

### Bug 2
`next lint` arrancaba interactivo porque no existía `.eslintrc.json` → exit 1.

## Fix
- **Workflow YAML**: `smoke-supabase` ahora corre siempre, con un primer step que check el secret y outputs `configured=true|false`. Steps subsecuentes gatean por ese output.
- **ESLint**: `.eslintrc.json` con preset `next/core-web-vitals` + plugin `@typescript-eslint` declarado + rules relajadas pragmáticas.

- PR #68 validó 0 errors, ~18 warnings de lint

author: meganeuridae
body:
Extracts the **backend foundation** from [@nickmahdavi's PR #64](https://github.com/anima-research/animachat/pull/64) — cursor-based pagination, server-side branch activation, enriched bookmarks — and lands it independently of the (still-evolving) frontend virtual-scrolling UI in #64.

## Why split it this way

PR #64 has been open since Feb 2026 with the author's own to-do list flagging known broken state ("Tree view is broken", "Scroller height is broken", "Fix potential race conditions", "Hunt down persistence bugs"). Four months of main-flux on top of that. The full PR isn't merge-ready as-is.

But the **API design is sound**, and the foundation pieces are independently useful:
- Any future client (current frontend, the eventual virtual-scroll UI, a third-party API user) can start using the cursor-paginated `/messages` endpoint immediately
- Server-side branch activation (`/activate-branch`) removes a layer of frontend complexity for any client, not just virtualized ones
- Enriched bookmarks unblock sidebar/jump-list rendering scenarios that don't want to load the full message tree

Splitting lets us **ship the foundation now** and address the harder UI work (broken tree view, scroller height, race conditions) in a follow-up that lands on top of a known-good API.

## What this PR includes

**`shared/types.ts`:** `EnrichedBookmarkSchema` + `EnrichedBookmark` type — bookmark with denormalized `preview`, `participantName`, `model`, `role`.

**`backend/src/database/index.ts`** (+401 lines, end of class):
- `activateBranch(messageId, branchId, conversationId, ownerUserId, isDetached)` — flip the active branch server-side; returns `Map<messageId, branchId>` of pairs that changed (parent-cascade aware).
- `switchBranchesBatch(allMessages, switches)` (private helper) — applies a batch of branch switches in a single pass.
- `getConversationMessageBranchPage(conversationId, ownerUserId, limit, cursor?, direction='older', requestingUserId?)` — cursor-based pagination.
- `getVisibleMessagePath(conversationId, ownerUserId, requestingUserId?)` — returns the currently-visible message path through active branches.
- `computeVisiblePath(allMessages)` (private helper) — tree → visible path.
- `getConversationBookmarksEnriched(conversationId, userId)` — bookmarks with denormalized rendering fields.

**`backend/src/routes/conversations.ts`:**
- `GET /:id/messages` now accepts `?cursor=`, `?direction=`, `?limit=`. Unset = backward-compatible \"return all\" (limit defaults to Infinity). Invalid `limit` rejected with 400.
- `POST /:id/activate-branch` — new endpoint.

**`backend/src/routes/bookmarks.ts`:**
- `GET /conversation/:conversationId` upgraded to return enriched shape (superset of prior `Bookmark[]`; older clients still parse correctly).
- `GET /conversation/:conversationId/active-path` — new endpoint, filters bookmarks to those anchored on the currently-visible branch path.

## What this PR deliberately excludes from #64

- **`shared/types.ts` deletions.** PR #64 removed `personaContext`, `pseudoPrefillMode`, `pseudoPrefillFilename`, and `pseudo-prefill` from `ConversationModeEnum`. Those fields are now load-bearing in main — `personaContext` alone has 10+ active call sites in `handler.ts`. Bringing those deletions would be a feature regression of the persona system.
- **`package.json` re-introducing root-level runtime deps** (`compression`, `multer`, `@types/*`, `vue-virtual-scroller`). Would regress P4-6 and wipe the root `engines` block that PR #110 made the per-workspace versions match.
- **All frontend changes** (ConversationView.vue, store/index.ts, virtual scrolling implementation). The author's to-do list flags multiple broken-state items; landing those needs a substantive rebase + reimplementation pass on top of this foundation.

## One implementation detail worth noting

`tryLoadAndVerifyMessage` (a private helper PR #64 depended on) **already exists in current main** with an identical implementation — someone (probably Antra) added it independently since Feb. author: matchmoments-admin
body:
Closes #353.

## Summary

- Pinned DNS resolution between SSRF check + connect via a custom undici `Agent({ connect: { lookup } })`. Hook validates the resolved IP against private/loopback/metadata ranges; undici then dials the same IP we validated — no TOCTOU window.
- New generic primitive `ssrfSafeDispatcher` is reusable by future outbound fetchers (Phase A Visual Match #376, Phase B candidate verification #383, Phase C fingerprint #384).
- Defends against two attack classes the existing `isPrivateURL` guard cannot: (a) hostname A-records to private IP without rebinding; (b) rebinding TOCTOU mid-fetch.

## Why now

Tagged P3 hygiene because the blast radius is currently low (response body size-capped at 512 KB and never reflected to the user — `verifyShopAbnDeep` only regex-scans it for an ABN). But **Phase A clone-detection per #376 issues up to 5,000 outbound fetches/day against attacker-controlled candidate domains** — exactly the surface area where SSRF-via-rebinding hurts. This must land before #376 starts.

## Changes

- **`packages/scam-engine/src/ssrf-dispatcher.ts`** (new) — exports `ssrfSafeDispatcher` (singleton), `isPrivateIP(addr)`, `buildSsrfLookup(dnsLookup?)`. Covers IPv4 + IPv6 private/loopback/metadata ranges including AWS / GCP metadata (169.254/16), CGNAT (100.64/10), RFC1918, benchmarking (198.18/15), and IPv6 loopback / link-local / unique-local.
- **`packages/scam-engine/src/fetch-shop-page.ts`** — passes `dispatcher: ssrfSafeDispatcher` on every fetch. Cast with inline comment (the option is undici-specific, not in lib.dom's `RequestInit`).
- **`packages/scam-engine/src/__tests__/ssrf-dispatcher.test.ts`** (new) — 33 tests covering IPv4/IPv6 ranges + edge boundaries (172.15/172.32 around RFC1918 class B; 100.63/100.128 around CGNAT; 198.17/198.20 around benchmarking) + lookup-callback rejection invariants.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @askarthur/scam-engine test` — 329 passed, 5 skipped (rpcs.smoke.test skips when integration env absent — unchanged behaviour)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @askarthur/scam-engine typecheck` — clean
- [x] New file: 33 tests for `isPrivateIP` + `buildSsrfLookup` covering IPv4/IPv6 private ranges + edge boundaries + DNS error propagation
- [x] Existing `fetch-shop-page.test.ts`: 13 tests still passing — dispatcher is opaque to stubbed global `fetch`
- [ ] Manual smoke after merge: confirm a known-public shop (e.g. `https://example.com/`) still fetches successfully in a deep check
- [ ] Vercel preview: green

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `safebrowsing.isPrivateURL` and `ssrf-guard.assertSafeURL` have **duplicate** private-IP-range logic. Not fixing here per CLAUDE.md anti-scope-creep guidance — track separately as hygiene.
- Future outbound HTTP fetchers (Visual Match in #376, candidate verification in #383, fingerprint in #384) should adopt `ssrfSafeDispatcher` rather than re-implementing the lookup hook.

author: william-long-ii
body:
## Summary

Hotfix for the PWA white-screen on packaged builds. `dist/pwa/**/*` added to `asarUnpack` in `electron-builder.yml`.

**Closes:** [BDHLNDR-69](https://gobodhi.atlassian.net/browse/BDHLNDR-69)

## Root cause (from BDHLNDR-69)

\`express.static\` streams via \`fs.createReadStream\`, which doesn't work reliably on asar paths. In the packaged \`3.4.0-beta.0\` build, \`/m/assets/*\` requests fall through to the SPA fallback, which returns:
- **500** when \`sendFile\` errors propagate via \`next(err)\` → default error handler
- **404 with \`application/json\` MIME** when \`fs.existsSync\` returns false on asar (the fallback's own JSON error)

Browser refuses to apply CSS with \`application/json\` MIME → white screen.

Console from the affected build:

\`\`\`
index-BqDTC0ps.js:1  Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 500 (Internal Server Error)
m/:1 Refused to apply style from 'http://192.168.1.78:8443/m/assets/index-CC3_BKul.css' because its MIME type ('application/json') is not a supported stylesheet MIME type, and strict MIME checking is enabled.
\`\`\`

## Fix

\`\`\`yaml
asarUnpack:
  - dist/mcp-server/**/*
  - dist/hooks/**/*
  - dist/main/vector-search/**/*
  - dist/pwa/**/*   # NEW
\`\`\`

Same treatment as the existing entries — each one is content that needs filesystem-level access from packaged mode (stream / spawn / require / serve).

## Test plan

- [x] No code changes — only \`electron-builder.yml\`
- [ ] After merge: cut \`3.4.0-beta.1\` on development, install, hit \`/m/\` from a phone — see the PWA shell, not a white screen
- [ ] Manual: verify \`/m/assets/index-*.js\` returns 200 with \`application/javascript\` MIME and \`/m/assets/index-*.css\` returns 200 with \`text/css\`

## Severity

**High** — blocks the entire mobile companion PWA on the just-cut \`3.4.0-beta.0\` beta. Trivial fix; next beta cut picks it up automatically.

author: harol-reina
body:
## Why

First post-merge run of the freshly-shipped `visibility-monitor.yml` and `digest-reconciliation.yml` from PR #5 both FAILED with `cosign verify FAILED for ghcr.io/verbara/platform/{api,realtime,renderer,mail}:v2.4.2 (unsigned or wrong key)` — but locally with maintainer's `cosign v3.0.6` the same verify passes.

**Root cause**: cosign version drift. CI runs v2.5.2, local runs v3.0.6. Cosign v3.x refactored the detached-signature distribution layout — signatures produced by v3.x are unreadable by v2.5.2. The 4 v2.4.2 images are correctly signed; they just can't be read by the CI runner's old cosign.

The prior comment claiming "cosign-installer@v3 fails on cosign v3.x" was inaccurate — `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3` has supported v3.x since installer release v3.5+.

## Changes

1. **All 3 workflows**: `cosign-release: 'v2.5.2'` → `'v3.0.6'` (matches maintainer-local). Comments rewritten with the actual rationale (cross-context alignment).
2. **Both monitor workflows**: drop `--label "security,priority/high"` from `gh issue create` — those labels don't exist on the repo and cause a secondary failure that masks the real one in the GH Actions UI.

The `cosign sign --tlog-upload=false` and `cosign verify --insecure-ignore-tlog` flag syntax is unchanged in v3.x (verified via `--help`); release.yml signing command needs no changes.

- [ ] Post-merge: visibility-monitor manual dispatch → all 6 steps green (including the 4 v2.4.2 cosign verifies and the cosign.pub URL match)

The deprecated cleanup is tracked in Fase 3.4 of the v2.4.3 release plan.

author: riddim-developer-bot[bot]
body:
## Why

Extends the SwiftLint ruleset with architectural and safety rules that are especially valuable for LLM-generated code — the more constraints we give the model, the less it reaches for lazy shortcuts.

## What changed

Seven rules added to `opt_in_rules` in `.swiftlint.yml`:

**Architectural (high value):**
- `swiftui_state_private` — `@State` must be private; leaking view state breaks encapsulation
- `implicitly_unwrapped_optional` — `var x: T!` is an init-order hack; use proper DI or `lazy var`
- `private_over_fileprivate` — `fileprivate` leaks to the whole file; `private` is tighter
- `superfluous_disable_command` — catches stale `swiftlint:disable` comments after violations are fixed

**Design smell detection:**
- `discouraged_optional_boolean` — `Bool?` is a tristate smell; use an explicit enum
- `unowned_variable_capture` — `[unowned self]` crashes on dealloc; `[weak self]` is always safer
- `no_magic_numbers` — inline numeric literals should be named constants (1712 existing warnings; forward constraint for new code)

## Trade-offs not taken

- `no_magic_numbers` has 1712 existing violations — all in SwiftUI layout code. These are warnings (non-blocking) tracked as forward constraints; a future design constants layer will drive them to zero.
- `explicit_acl` considered but too noisy to retrofit on a small single-team codebase.

## Test plan

CI SwiftLint job passes (warnings are non-blocking per the config; only violations above `error` thresholds would fail).

author: pamplemousse-glitch
body:
## Summary

- **Full PFC taxonomy**: Expanded `PFC_MAP` from 11 patterns to cover all official Plaid PFC codes. Previously ~90% of detailed category codes mapped to `null` and were stored silently in the DB.
- **Fixed broken patterns**: `UTILITIES_*` and `MORTGAGE_*` prefixes don't exist in Plaid's taxonomy — real codes are `RENT_AND_UTILITIES_*` and `LOAN_PAYMENTS_MORTGAGE_PAYMENT`. Fixed.
- **Fixed RENT_AND_UTILITIES split**: Everything under `RENT_AND_UTILITIES_*` was incorrectly mapped to `'rent'` via the old `[/^RENT_/, 'rent']` catch-all (including gas/electric, internet, water). Now `RENT_AND_UTILITIES_RENT` → `'rent'` and all others → `'utilities'`.
- **Legacy category fallback**: Added `mapLegacyCategory()` using Plaid's `transaction.category: string[]` field. Fires when `personal_finance_category` is `null` (regional banks, credit unions). Covers paycheck (`["Income","Payroll"]`), groceries, restaurants, travel, medical, loan payments, and more.
- **`bill_paid_on_time` rule rewrite**: Was matching hardcoded strings like `'electric company'` — never fired in production. Now matches PFC-mapped categories: `utilities`, `loan_payment`, `rent`, `insurance`, `mortgage`. Will fire for `CONSOLIDATED EDISON`, `AT&T*BILL`, credit card payments, etc.

## What fires now that didn't before

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gas/electric bill via ACH | `null` → no rule | `utilities` → `bill_paid_on_time` |
| Credit card payment | `null` → no rule | `loan_payment` → `bill_paid_on_time` |
| Rent payment | `'rent'` → no rule | `'rent'` → `bill_paid_on_time` |
| Netflix / streaming | `null` → no rule | `entertainment` → (future rule) |
| Doctor visit | `null` → no rule | `medical` → (future rule) |
| Paycheck at regional bank | `null` → no `paycheck_received` | `'paycheck'` via legacy fallback |

## Test plan

- [ ] 189 Vitest tests pass locally ✓
- [ ] `bill_paid_on_time` now has 5 tests (was 2) covering utilities, loan_payment, rent, non-bill categories, and credit tx guard
- [ ] CI green

## Why
[/opportunites](https://news.edlight.org/opportunites) was showing only ~5 cards. Diagnosis: the 50-point score + 0.50 audience-fit bars (both tuned for scholarship copy) rejected almost every wider-taxonomy item (hackathon, leadership_program, accelerator, mentorship, …) and global opportunities open to Haitians that don't name-drop Haiti (Erasmus, Schwarzman, MIT Solve, …).

## Changes
**Web** — [apps/web/src/app/opportunites/page.tsx](apps/web/src/app/opportunites/page.tsx)

  - +0.15  lifecycle === 'deadline_soon'
  - −0.30  lifecycle === 'expired'

**Worker** — on-demand seeder

author: eumemic
body:
## Summary
- Replace the single fabricated `"No result was received for this tool call."` with two branched messages keyed on the existing `tool_execute_start` span: `"may have completed; verify before retrying"` when the span exists, `"did not run; you may retry"` when it doesn't.
- This stops the harness from *lying* about non-idempotent tool outcomes (bash mutations, http_request POST, connector send), which under the project's "model retries on error" philosophy was double-firing those operations on the model's retry.

- Producer side: move `bound_log = log.bind(...)` below the span append so the load-bearing "first action in this lifecycle" comment is literally true; comment now explicitly covers the `CancelledError`-during-await race.

author: roryford
body:
Closes #1447

## Root cause

`SessionManagerViewModel.configure(bootstrap:)` calls `configure(persistence:autoLoad:true,...)`, which schedules `Task { [weak self] in await self?.loadSessions() }` as a fire-and-forget background task and returns immediately. Three independent DX agents hit the same symptom: `sessionVM.sessions` was still empty after `configure` returned, because the initial SwiftData fetch hadn't run yet. They were forced to add polling loops to recover — a clear signal the API was misleading.

## Fix

Added a new `async` method `configureAndLoad(bootstrap:)` on `SessionManagerViewModel` that configures with `autoLoad: false` and then explicitly `await`s `loadSessions()` before returning. Callers that need `sessions` populated synchronously (scene restore, launch-time session selection) use this new method. Callers that rely on `SessionListView`'s `.task {}` modifier can continue using the synchronous `configure(bootstrap:)` overload.

The synchronous `configure(bootstrap:)` doc comment now prominently warns about the fire-and-forget behaviour and points to the new method.

## Tests added (`RuntimeConfigurationTests`)

- `test_configureAndLoad_sessionsPopulatedBeforeReturn` — pre-populates two sessions, calls `configureAndLoad`, asserts `sessions.count == 2` immediately with no polling (regression for #1447)
- `test_configure_autoLoadEventuallyPopulateSessions` — documents and locks the synchronous overload's fire-and-forget contract: `sessions` is empty immediately, populated after `autoLoadTask` drains

author: teknium1
body:
## Summary

`terminal(background=true)` without `notify_on_complete=true` or `watch_patterns` runs the process SILENTLY — the agent has no way to learn it finished short of calling `process(action='poll')` explicitly. The tool result now includes a `hint` field on that exact code path so the agent sees the footgun on the same turn it triggers it, and self-corrects without needing the user to surface anything.

## Why

May 23, 2026 (PR #31231 cycle): I launched a CI-watch poller with `background=true` only. The poller ran fine, exited green 6 minutes later, I never noticed. Teknium had to surface 'we are green CI, you can merge.' Skill docs and memory both said *what* to do (poll in background) but not *how* to receive the result — the `notify_on_complete=true` flag exists and works, but is easy to forget when `background=true` alone seems sufficient.

Teknium's pushback was: 'no one but us has access to the skill — we should find a way to make background=true + notify_on_complete=true a more obvious pathway in the tool definition or something.' This PR is that.

## Changes

### Runtime nudge — `tools/terminal_tool.py`

When `background=true` is set without either `notify_on_complete=true` or `watch_patterns`, the tool result now includes:

```json
{
  "output": "Background process started",
  "session_id": "...",
  "pid": ...,
  "hint": "background=true without notify_on_complete=true means this process runs SILENTLY — you will not be told when it exits. If this is a bounded task (test suite, build, CI poller, deploy, anything with a defined end), you almost certainly wanted notify_on_complete=true so the system pings you on exit. Re-launch with notify_on_complete=true, or call process(action='poll') / process(action='wait') yourself to learn the outcome. Only ignore this hint for genuine long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers, daemons)."
}
```

Cost for legitimate server cases (where silence is correct): one ignored read, ~50 tokens. Cost for forgot-notify cases: prevented blindness. False positives << false negatives.

### Schema/description rewrite — same file

`TERMINAL_TOOL_DESCRIPTION` (top-level) and the `background` parameter description now lead with **'Almost always pair with notify_on_complete=true'** instead of presenting it as one of two equally-likely patterns. The two legitimate non-notify shapes (long-lived servers; watch_patterns for mid-process signals) are still documented, but framed as the minority case.

### Tests — `tests/tools/test_notify_on_complete.py`

Four new tests covering all four shapes:

| Shape | Hint? |
|---|---|
| `background=true` alone | yes |
| `background=true, notify_on_complete=true` | no |
| `background=true, watch_patterns=[...]` | no |
| `background=false` (foreground) | no |

Hint content is asserted on substance — must name `notify_on_complete` (so the agent knows what to fix) and must explain the failure mode (`silent` / `no way to learn`), not just suggest a flag.

## Validation

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_notify_on_complete.py` | 21/21 | 25/25 (+4 new) |
| `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool_pty_fallback.py` | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `tests/tools/test_watch_patterns.py` | 29/29 | 29/29 |
| `tests/gateway/test_background_process_notifications.py` | 31/31 | 31/31 |
| `tests/gateway/test_internal_event_bypass_pairing.py` | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| `tests/tools/test_process_registry.py` | 64/64 | 64/64 |

160/160 across all related test files. E2E confirmed: the hint shows up exactly as designed for bg-only, and is absent for bg+notify, bg+watch, and foreground.

## Not in scope

- `code_execution_tool` already blocks `background` in its sandbox (no fix needed).
- `delegate_tool` already references the correct `background=True, notify_on_complete=True` pairing in its doc string (no fix needed).
- Cron jobs / process(action='wait') already produce notifications inherently — no nudge needed there.


## Infographic

![terminal-bg-silent-hint](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0a9b7270/ly3zQFw7n7oX4IdMwiHlD_K7tIkAsu.png)

# PR Summary — Issue #2753 ## Summary `generation_complete` training events emitted `averageFitness: NaN` on the default code path (`verbose: false`), because `makeElitists()` only computed the population mean when `verbose === true`. Downstream consumers (loggers, charts, TSV exports) could not distinguish "average not computed" from a genuine numerical failure, and `.toFixed()` / JSON serialisation surfaced `NaN` to operators. This applies **Option 1** from the issue: the population average is now always computed for `generation_complete`. The `verbose` flag continues to control only the per-creature training log emitted by `logVerbose()`, not whether the aggregate is available to telemetry — matching how `bestFitness` is always populated. Changes: - `src/architecture/ElitismUtils.ts`: extracted a `computeAverageScore()` helper that sums `creature.score` over the population. `makeElitists()` now always calls it to populate `averageScore`; `verbose` only gates `logVerbose()`. - `src/config/TrainingEvent.ts`: clarified the `averageFitness` doc comment — it is always a finite number, independent of `verbose`. Closes #2753. ## Evidence Backend/CLI change — no web interface to screenshot. Verified via unit tests (see Test Plan). The `./quality.sh` gate passed cleanly: `6865 passed | 0 failed`. ### Data flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Pop[Population] --> CAS[computeAverageScore
always runs] CAS --> R[ElitistsResults.averageScore

per-creature log] R --> EV[generation_complete

author: balaji-embedcentrum
body:
## Why

Sessions used to be listed from `/api/sessions`, which the hermes-adapter agent serves out of its per-user SQLite. Whenever the fleet wipes / rebuilds a container (which happens regularly), that DB goes with it — the sidebar empties, and the user loses every conversation they had on record. The container can also lag or be unreachable, which would render the sidebar empty even when there's nothing actually wrong with the data.

Moving the **session index** to the browser keeps the user's view of \"my conversations\" stable across agent restarts. Messages themselves still live in the agent and are fetched on demand via `/api/history` — only the index moves.

## What

- `src/screens/chat-v2/runtime/local-sessions.ts` — small versioned localStorage store. `LocalSession[]` with `key`, `label`, `lastSnippet`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Cross-tab updates via the `storage` event. Exports `list / get / upsert / delete / subscribe / snippetFromText`. Safe in SSR (no-op when `window` is missing).
- `src/screens/chat-v2/components/sessions-sidebar.tsx` — drops the TanStack Query fetch from `/api/sessions`. Uses `useSyncExternalStore` to subscribe to the local store. Adds a per-row delete (×) on hover that also drops any cached history for that session. \"New chat\" now mints a fresh sessionKey so each one is a distinct row instead of overwriting `new`. Footer reads \"Stored locally in this browser.\" so the model is visible to the user.
- `src/screens/chat-v2/chat-screen-v2.tsx` — `useEffect` on `messages` upserts the current session. Label is derived from the first user message (snippet, 60 chars). `lastSnippet` is the most recent text part regardless of role.
- Also cleans up the pre-existing `handlePaste` lint warning in the same file (`ClipboardEvent.clipboardData` is non-nullable in React's types).

## Trade-offs

- Sessions are now per-browser / per-device, not synced. If the user clears site data the sidebar empties. That's an acceptable cost given how often the agent container empties it currently anyway.
- The agent's `/api/sessions` is left in place for now (other surfaces still use it). Cleanup can come later once chat-v2 fully owns this UX.

## Test plan

- [ ] Send a message in a fresh chat → row appears in the sidebar with label = first user message, latest snippet underneath
- [ ] Refresh the page → sidebar still shows it
- [ ] Restart / rebuild the agent container → sidebar still shows it
- [ ] Click \"+ New chat\" → distinct new row created with a fresh `s_*` key
- [ ] Hover a row → × button appears; click → row vanishes, history cache for it cleared
- [ ] Open chat in two tabs → upserts in one tab show up in the other within a tick
- [ ] Delete the currently-open session → bounces to a freshly-minted chat

author: copilot
body:
Agents consuming `rsm_search_symbols` and `rsm_build_context_pack` via MCP could silently lose full repo-relative paths or hallucinate symbols because key fields were buried in nested structures. This adds explicit top-level fields that agents can read directly without digging into nested payloads.

## `rsm_search_symbols` — per-result additions

```json
{
  "entity_id": "...",
  "kind": "function",
  "name": "build_context_pack",
  "path": "src/repo_semantic_memory/context/pack_builder.py",
  "start_line": 136,
  "end_line": 397,
  "score": 43.339296,
  "source_range": { ... },
  "ranking_reasons": [ ... ]
}
```

- `path`, `start_line`, `end_line` — top-level aliases of `source_range.*`; `path == source_range.path` is a test invariant
- `score` — numeric BM25 score extracted directly (was only in `ranking_reasons` as a string like `"score=43.339296"`)

## `rsm_build_context_pack` — response-level additions

- `selected_files` — sorted unique repo-relative paths; derived from `suggested_files_to_inspect` when non-empty, else from selected entity source ranges
- `selected_entities` — top-level alias of `payload.selected_entities`
- `selected_relations` — top-level alias of `payload.selected_relations`

## Both tools

- `agent_instructions` — short stable tuple added to both response shapes:
  ```json
  [
    "Use only paths listed in this response.",
    "Do not infer missing paths, symbols, or class names.",
    "Verify edits against cited source ranges."
  ]
  ```

## Compatibility

All pre-existing fields (`matches`, `results`, `citations`, `budget`, `uncertainties`, `payload`, `rendered`, `selected_entity_ids`, `selected_relation_keys`, `suggested_files_to_inspect`) are preserved unchanged. No ranking or retrieval behavior was modified.

## Docs

`docs/usage/mcp.md` gains a "Reading MCP tool output safely" section listing the preferred agent-facing fields and a prompt example.

author: rrhester
body:
## Operator caught this

> "It thinks I only need 1 driver? The logic it should use for estimated driver shortage is = 1 Driver can fill 4 shifts a week. So if I am 8 shifts short then I need 2 drivers."

## The bug

Formula `ceil(unstaffed / curMax)` was always right. The bug was **which `unstaffed` count** we fed it:

- **Engine.uncovered** (was used) — shifts the engine literally couldn't fill. Under-counts because the engine treats onboarding-driver assignments as "filled" (locked).
- **Strip-unstaffed** (now used) — `needed - filled` from the KPI strip. Matches the operator's mental model: strip shows 14 unstaffed → 14/4 → ceil → **4 more drivers needed.**

## What changed

`stripUnstaffed` (from `_rrLiveSchedCoverage`) is now the primary source, with `baseUncov` as fallback if the strip stash isn't available. Two message states (was three):

- `stripUnstaffed === 0` → "Fully staffed"
- `stripUnstaffed > 0` → "~K more drivers needed" where K = `ceil(stripUnstaffed / curMax)`

Removed the "pending driver activation" message from #1665 — the operator's mental model treats those shifts as gaps too.

Subtitle also rephrased to "N shifts on the board are unstaffed" so it matches the strip's "N/M shifts staffed" language.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Operator's example (strip 71%, 35/49): drill-down says "~4 more drivers needed" (was "~1")
- [ ] Strip 100% staffed: drill-down says "Fully staffed"
- [ ] Strip 80% (39/49 staffed → 10 unstaffed): drill-down says "~3 more drivers needed" at maxDays=4

author: sunhaoxiangwang
body:
## Summary

Implements the Stage 11d.0-approved triple-key allowlist schema. **The allowlist remains empty** — both `MAINNET_APPROVED_PROOF_SYSTEM_ENTRIES` and the legacy `MAINNET_APPROVED_PROOF_SYSTEMS` ship as `&[]`. No proof system is mainnet-eligible after this PR.

## Schema additions (`crates/omni-zkml/src/proof.rs`)

- **`AllowlistEntry`** struct with seven fields: `proof_system`, `backend_id`, `circuit_id_hex`, `model_hash`, `model_format`, `verification_key_hash_hex`, `chain_team_review_ref`. Derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq`. Allowlist-side uses unambiguous `verification_key_hash_hex` (the value IS a hash); existing artifact-side `ProofMetadata::verification_key_hex` schema is preserved unchanged.
- **`MAINNET_APPROVED_PROOF_SYSTEM_ENTRIES: &[AllowlistEntry] = &[]`** (structured triple-key allowlist; empty by design).
- **`MAINNET_APPROVED_PROOF_SYSTEMS: &[ProofSystem] = &[]`** (legacy back-compat alias, also empty).
- **`MAINNET_VK_HASH_DOMAIN_SEPARATOR = b"OMNINODE-VK:v1:"`** + **`mainnet_vk_hash(canonical_vk_bytes) -> [u8; 32]`** helper computing `BLAKE3(domain_separator || canonical_vk_bytes)`. No new dep — `blake3` already a workspace dep used by `omni-zkml`.
- Layer 6 of `check_mainnet_eligible` rewired to consult the structured triple-key match (proof_system + circuit_id_hex + model_hash) with the legacy list as OR-bridge. Bounded references still refused by layer 3 before layer 6.

## 12 new tests

- Empty-list invariants (×2)
- `stage11b_halo2_reference_never_in_allowlist`
- `bounded_reference_refused_before_allowlist_lookup`
- `testnet_or_dev_only_refused_before_allowlist_lookup`
- `wrong_circuit_id_hex_rejects_even_with_correct_proof_system`
- `wrong_model_hash_rejects_even_with_correct_proof_system_and_circuit_id`
- `matching_structured_entry_would_pass_layer_6_for_synthetic_production_metadata` (uses `#[cfg(test)]` helper `check_mainnet_eligible_with`)
- `legacy_alias_match_also_passes_layer_6`
- `every_allowlist_entry_has_required_metadata` (forward-looking guard rejecting Mock / bounded-reference / Gguf / Other(_) / malformed-hex / empty-string entries)
- `vk_hash_helper_uses_documented_domain_separator`
- `vk_hash_helper_is_byte_stable` (validates `BLAKE3(domain_separator || input)` bit-for-bit)

## Doc tightenings (chain-team review feedback)

- **`docs/mainnet-eligibility-criteria.md`**: VK name clarification (§1.5), defense-in-depth note (§1.6), NEW §1.7 VK hash scheme, NEW §1.8 deterministic byte-stability mandate, NEW §3.1 framework-bindings location, §6 explicit `Gguf` / `Other(_)` / bounded-reference invalidity.
- **`docs/stage11d-review-packet.md`**: new packet-metadata fields (`verification_key_hash_hex`, `review_board_roster_ref`, `benchmark_record_ref`), NEW §3.4 byte-stability checklist, NEW §3.5 benchmark record requirements (exact command, build profile = release, run count ≥ 100, CPU/RAM/OS, rust toolchain, p50/p95/max, p95 ≤ 1000 ms threshold), §6 failure-mode table extended to cover all six `MainnetRefusalReason` layers, §8.1 framework-bindings sub-table, §11 review-board roster sign-off row.
- **`docs/stage11d-mainnet-eligibility-FAQ.md`**: NEW Q12 (VK hash scheme), Q13 (bounded references never allowlisted), Q14 (non-deterministic provers not eligible), Q15 (allowlist `verification_key_hash_hex` vs artifact `verification_key_hex`).
- **`docs/operator-runbook.md`**: `ProofSystemNotMainnetApproved` row updated; mainnet-eligibility line extended through Stage 11d.1.
- **`README.md`**: Stage 11d.1 row bumped to Complete.

## Test plan

body:
## What

Field / FieldSet を `@layer components` クラス API に移行する #154 sweep-7。
**本 PR の merge で全 18 lv1 コンポの class API が出揃い、v0.9.0 の
「消費者 Tailwind 不要化」が達成される** — `#154` および `#58` Phase 2 を
同時にクローズする。

主な diff:

- **Field**: `.st-field` + 6 sub-element + 4 derived flex modifier。
  root に `[data-error]` 属性を新規 emit (FieldSet → Field collapse 経路
  の external observability hook)。
- **FieldSet**: `.st-fieldset` (`<fieldset>` reset chrome) + 4 sub-element。
  `direction` / `wrap` は `__children` 側 2 modifier。header 余白は
  `:has(> .st-fieldset__legend)` / `:has(> .st-fieldset__description)`
  で CSS 側に閉じる。
- **完了処理**:
  - `src/docs/CSSApi.stories.tsx` の Tailwind utility 依存を完全排除
    (page-local `<style>` + `.cssapi-doc__*` prefix で chrome 吸収)。
    Field / FieldSet 章を追加。
  - README の Tailwind 必須記述を削除し v0.9.0 完了体に。
  - AGENTS.md に「消費者は Tailwind 不要」のコールアウトを追加。

## Why

- #154 (CSS class API 整備、v0.9.0) の最後の lv1 sweep。Field / FieldSet
  が片付けば 18/18 完了で、`<button class="st-btn st-btn--primary">` 等が
  Tailwind なしで動く DS の主張が **全コンポに行き渡る**。
- `[data-error]` を Field root に出すことで、FieldSet → Field の collapse
  経路が JS 経路 (React context) からも CSS 経路 (属性 selector) からも
  observability 持つ。vanilla HTML 消費者が外部スタイルをフックする余地
  ができる (root の視覚は今回当てない — Field 自身の error は引き続き
  内部 form input 側で表現する設計を維持)。

  整理 — api-stability の v1.0 凍結対象を肥大化させない配慮。
- AGENTS.md のコールアウト追加は、AI コーディング支援が「Schatten 内部 =
  Tailwind なので consumer 側にも Tailwind が必要」と誤誘導するのを防ぐ
  ため。

## Summary

Keeps the xtask history zombie reaper's 2s SIGTERM grace in normal builds, but shortens that grace to 25ms under `cfg(test)`. This removes an artificial two-second idle from the stale-PID cleanup proof.

## Problem

`xtask history tests slowest --latest-per-test --limit 30 --json` showed `xtask::history::db::test_history_db_open_kills_overage_background_job_rows` at 2.014902738s. Exact rerun job 256 measured 2.012555812s. The test exercises the live zombie-reaper branch, so it was paying the production SIGTERM grace period just to prove the DB state transition.

## Solution

Introduce `ZOMBIE_REAPER_SIGTERM_GRACE` with:

- 2s for non-test builds.
- 25ms for test builds.

The test still spawns a live `sleep` process, runs open-time cleanup, and asserts the invocation/background-job rows become cancelled/killed with exit code 124.

author: agt
body:
Before patching a pod's tolerations, the controller now checks genuine
free capacity:

  free[lane] = lane_capacity[lane] - running_units[lane] - admitted_but_not_running_units[lane]

A new _admitted_resources dict tracks pods that have been patched but
have not yet transitioned to Running. Pods that don't fit are re-submitted
to the scheduler queue and left in _pending for the next cycle, rather
than being silently admitted into a full lane.

Also fixes a pre-existing dead-code bug in _running_pod_from_pod where
_resource_units (which returns float) was incorrectly unpacked as a tuple.

author: akarlin3
body:
## Summary

The architectural inflection from pure-client to client+server. Adds a FastAPI + PostgreSQL + S3-compatible backend (`api/`) that persists **patches** (full encoded URL state), **captures** (loop-pedal audio), and **recordings** (schema + endpoints only; export is v1.0), under **anonymous-first** identity. The existing client keeps working fully with the backend offline.

- **Anon identity** — `x-anon-id` header is authoritative; missing → server mints one (echoed via header + soft-recovery cookie). `localStorage['am_anon_id']` on the client.
- **Patches CRUD + short links** — every patch gets a `short_slug` reachable at `/p/<slug>`; `GET /patches/:idOrSlug` resolves either; `state` immutable, PATCH edits metadata only; default `unlisted`; real deletion.
- **Captures** — multipart WAV upload → server transcode to Opus (ffmpeg) → object storage; `GET` 302s to a presigned URL; server-side **ref-counting** + scheduled **orphan sweep**. Save defaults to params-only; "include captures" is opt-in.
- **Single source of truth** — the URL schema lives once (TypeScript). `npm run gen:schema` compiles it to `schema/manifest.v4.json`, which the server validates against **strictly** (reject, not clamp). CI fails on drift.
- **Rate limits + quotas** from day one (typed `409`/`413`/`429`); Alembic migrations; `docker compose` local dev (Postgres + MinIO + API + web); structured logs; Sentry stub.
- **Client** — typed API client, Save dialog + My Patches drawer beside Copy Link, `/p/<slug>` route that re-hydrates loop slots (incl. frozen + grain params) from captures.

### Decisions (from `docs/v0.7-PLAN.md`, all overridable)
- **Monorepo-lite**: `api/` + `schema/` added; web stays at repo root (no `apps/*` churn).
- **Object storage = Cloudflare R2** (S3 API, zero egress) over a Railway volume.
- **Web stays on Firebase**, only the API runs on Railway.
- **Audio**: client uploads WAV, server transcodes to Opus (Safari MediaRecorder gaps; capture is a buffer, not a stream).
- The audio engine code is unchanged — additive only: `LoopSlot.loadBuffer`, `Orchestrator.decodeAudio`/`loadLoopBuffer`, and a recognized runtime-only `cap` loop flag.

## Verification done locally
- Backend: **43 pytest** pass (SQLite fast path); pyright clean.
- Client: **193 vitest** pass; `tsc` typecheck, eslint, prettier all clean; `vite build` OK.
- Schema manifest regenerates with no drift.
- Migration applies against a real Postgres in CI (`migrations` job); could not run Postgres/Docker locally (no daemon), so that path is exercised in CI only.

## Smoke matrix (manual — needs a browser + running backend, not exercised in this env)
- [ ] Save patch (params only) → reload via `/p/<slug>` → state matches
- [ ] Save patch with one frozen capture → reload → buffer hydrates, freeze applies
- [ ] Backend offline → app still works, Save shows a toast; inline `#s=` link still loads
- [ ] Hit quota → graceful `409` toast
- [ ] Hit rate limit → graceful `429` toast

## Notes / deferred
- Deploy is config + docs only (no Railway/R2 credentials in this environment): `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.github/workflows/api.yml`, `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- Per plan: real auth + claim-by-email → post-v1.0, public gallery → v0.8, recording export pipeline + embed → v1.0, soft-delete → never.

See `docs/v0.7-PLAN.md` for full rationale, `docs/API.md` for the endpoint reference.

## Summary

- **Extended quality gate (Step 1.5):** typecheck → lint → build run in sequence; each gate is independently blocking; new `references/quality-gates.md` documents every command, fallback, and failure path.
- **CI checks wait loop (Step 5.5):** `gh pr checks --watch` with a 10-min timeout before any merge; configurable skip with `⚠️` audit trail; new `references/ci-checks.md` covers the full decision table.
- **Network retry logic (Steps 3 & 4):** exponential back-off (5 s → 15 s → 30 s) for `git push` and `gh pr create`; transient failures retry, hard rejections stop immediately.
- **Branch protection check (Step 4.5):** reads required reviews + required checks from GitHub API; blocks merge attempt if protection rules would prevent it.
- **Rollback map (new `references/rollback.md`):** per-stage recovery procedures (quality-gate failure → post-commit → post-push → post-PR → post-merge → post-worktree-delete).
- **Adaptive merge strategy (Step 6A):** detects repo settings via API and selects squash → merge-commit → rebase in priority order; no longer hardcodes `--squash`.
- **Push notification on completion (Step 9):** calls `PushNotification` harness tool so background-agent runs surface to the user even when terminal is not visible.
- **Draft PR option (Step 4):** counts files vs `main`; offers draft mode when > 20 files changed.
- **Conflict escalation after 3 attempts:** `git merge --abort` + `--force-with-lease` push + PR converted to draft + recovery checklist output; documented in `references/conflict-resolution.md § Escalation After 3 Failed Attempts`.
- **Output format updated:** new `🔄 Rollback` emoji; Steps 4.5 and 5.5 rows added to both happy-path template and variant rows; complete example updated.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1544. Addresses the root cause of #1542 in the build pipeline itself rather than relying solely on the counter-offset defense.

- Store the compiled (pre-resolve) client JS content in the build cache via a new `compiledClientJs` field on `CacheEntry`
- In the combine step (step 6), prefer the cached compiled content over reading from disk
- This prevents stale `__bf_inline_N` IIFEs from a prior build's `resolveRelativeImports` pass from leaking into the combined file

## Root cause (deeper)

On incremental/watch builds:
1. Step 4 skips cached components — the `.client.js` on disk is the **final** output from the previous build (post-resolveRelativeImports, with `__bf_inline_N` IIFEs)
2. Step 6 (combine) reads this stale file and inlines it into a freshly-recompiled parent
3. Step 6b (resolveRelativeImports) creates **new** `__bf_inline_N` that collide with the stale ones

#1544 added a counter-offset defense so new IDs skip past existing ones. This PR eliminates the problem at the source: the combine step now uses the original compiled content (before resolution), so there are no stale identifiers to collide with.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `build-cache.ts` | Add `compiledClientJs?: string` to `CacheEntry` |
| `build.ts` | Add `compiledClientJs` to `CompileEntryOutcome` and cache entry creation |
| `build.ts` | Build `compiledClientJsByKey` lookup; prefer it over disk reads in step 6 |

body:
### 🛡️ Sentinel: Secure Upload Handling

#### 🚨 Severity: MEDIUM

#### 💡 Vulnerability:
1. **Lack of File Size Validation:** The `upload_document` endpoint did not check the size of incoming files before processing, which could allow an attacker to exhaust server resources (DoS).
2. **Information Leakage:** API error responses and database error records contained raw exception strings, which could expose internal file paths or system internals to users.

#### 🎯 Impact:
*   **DoS:** A malicious user could crash the service or fill up storage by uploading extremely large files.
*   **Info Leak:** Attackers could gain knowledge of the server's file structure or software stack through detailed error messages.

#### 🔧 Fix:
*   Added an immediate check for `file.size` against `settings.max_upload_size_bytes` in the `upload_document` endpoint.
*   Wrapped file saving and processing in `try-except` blocks that log detailed errors to the server console while returning/storing generic "Failed to save/process" messages.
*   Updated `FileTooLargeError` to use `status.HTTP_413_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE`.

#### ✅ Verification:
*   Created `backend/tests/test_security_upload.py` with tests for:
    *   `test_upload_file_too_large`: Verifies that files exceeding the limit return HTTP 413.
    *   `test_upload_file_error_sanitization`: Verifies that internal path details are stripped from error responses.
*   Ran the full backend test suite (53 tests passed).

## Purpose
Resolves https://github.com/wso2/product-is/issues/27771

Introduce In-Flow Extension as a new action type that enables invoking external services during authentication flow execution. Sensitive flow context data is JWE-encrypted before being sent to the external endpoint.

## Goals
- Add `IN_FLOW_EXTENSION` action type under the `EXTENSION` category
- Support JWE encryption/decryption of flow context data (user claims, credentials, properties, inputs) using tenant-specific keys
- Introduce `AccessConfig` to control what context data is exposed to and modifiable by the external service, with per-path encryption
- Validate context paths using hierarchical prefix matching to prevent overlapping configurations
- Enforce action name uniqueness per action type
- Address review comments: refactor module structure, add `ActionValidator` interface, introduce `InFlowExtensionPathUtil`, add `InFlowUser` and `InFlowExtensionFlow` models

## Approach
- `InFlowExtensionAction` extends `Action` with an `AccessConfig` (expose/modify context paths with encryption flags) and an `Encryption` configuration (certificate for JWE)
- The request builder filters the flow execution context based on the expose configuration and JWE-encrypts values for paths marked as encrypted
- The response processor validates and applies REPLACE operations from the external service response, decrypting values for modify paths marked as encrypted
- Hierarchical prefix matching (via `InFlowExtensionPathUtil`) ensures context path configurations don't conflict and supports bidirectional parent-child matching
- Action name uniqueness is enforced case-insensitively within each action type at create and update time
- `ActionValidator` interface introduced to decouple validation logic from the service implementation
