author: snissn
body:
## Summary

Closes #1810.

Adds a first-class `unified-bench -suite collection_storage` for TreeDB collection storage-mode comparisons:

- stable storage modes: `document_only`, `typed_row_asset`, `typed_column_part`, `hybrid_document_row`, `hybrid_document_column`, `hybrid_row_column`, `hybrid_document_row_column`, `vector_typed_column`
- stable workloads: `insert_batch`, `point_get`, `predicate_scan`, `aggregate`, `vector_search_smoke`, `mixed`
- deterministic logical fixture and explicit semantic-comparability metadata
- correctness validation before timed workload loops
- unsupported workload/mode combinations reported with semantic reasons; selections with no supported mode fail closed
- `-profile-dir` artifacts: `collection_storage_results.{json,md,html}`, `benchprof_results.{json,md}`, runtime profiles, and `insights.{md,json,html}`
- `benchprof` now preserves/renders `runs[].collection_workloads` metadata

## Scope / path identity

This is scoped to the unified benchmark/productization surface and benchprof parsing/rendering. It does not change TreeDB on-disk formats, storage lifecycle, value-log behavior, or collection storage engines.

## Validation

Latest-head local validation after review fixes:

- `go test ./cmd/unified_bench -run 'TestCollectionStorage|TestApplyProfileArtifactDir|TestContentionProfilePath'`
- `go test ./internal/benchprof`
- `go test ./cmd/benchprof ./cmd/unified_bench ./internal/benchprof ./TreeDB/collections`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `make unified-bench benchprof`

Smoke/profile-dir check on latest head:

```bash
OUT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gomap_cs_reviewfix_XXXXXX)
./bin/unified-bench \
  -suite collection_storage \
  -dbs treedb \
  -profile durable \
  -keys 8 \
  -batchsize 4 \
  -collection-storage-modes document_only,typed_column_part,vector_typed_column \
  -collection-storage-workloads aggregate,vector_search_smoke \
  -collection-storage-query-count 1 \
  -collection-storage-field-count 6 \
  -collection-storage-vector-dims 3 \
  -collection-storage-vector-top-k 2 \
  -profile-dir "$OUT" \
  -path-label native-fastpath \
  -progress=false
./bin/benchprof -profiles-dir "$OUT"
grep -q "Collection Workload Metadata" "$OUT/insights.md"
```

Artifacts emitted included:

- `collection_storage_results.json`, `collection_storage_results.md`, `collection_storage_results.html`
- `benchprof_results.json`, `benchprof_results.md`
- `cpu_collection_storage_treedb_collection_storage.pprof`
- `allocs_collection_storage_treedb_collection_storage.pprof`
- `checkpoint_cpu_checkpoint_collection_storage_treedb_collection_storage.pprof`
- `block.pprof`, `mutex.pprof`, `trace.out`
- `insights.md`, `insights.json`, `insights.html`

## Benchmark evidence

The smoke command above is intentionally tiny (`-keys 8`) to validate the productized artifact/benchprof path, stable mode/workload naming, field-count fixture wiring, and semantic metadata shape. The suite reports per-workload rows/s, queries/s, ns/op, B/op, allocs/op, typed row/column asset byte splits, materialization/reconstruction counters, typed-column decode/prune counters, and vector candidate/edge/document-fetch counters in `collection_storage_results.*` and `benchprof` insights.

## Review status

- Codex reviewed latest head `2d3281b7f` and reported no major issues. Earlier Codex findings are fixed: field-count fixture width, vector byte-accounting refresh, non-finite vector score rejection, and typed benchprof counters to avoid JSON precision loss.
- CodeRabbit reviewed latest head and reported no actionable comments; earlier CodeRabbit findings are fixed/resolved, including artifact assertions, boolean fallback simplification, dead helper removal, optional metric rendering, and vector counter JSON tag alignment.
- Copilot review was requested after each meaningful push; Copilot returned an automation error and no actionable review comments.

author: adhithyan15
body:
## Summary

Step 3 of 4 in the autonomous chain. Replaces v0.1.0's identity `emit` with a recursive printer that walks every Phase 1 AST node and produces JavaScript text. **The first time the pipeline produces real output end-to-end.**

## Headline test

```rust
let prog = AST(2 + 3);
let pipeline_out = PassPipeline::new()
    .add(ConstantFoldPass::new())
    .run(prog, &sidecar, &mut cv);
let emit_out = emit(&pipeline_out.program, ...);
assert_eq!(emit_out.code, "5;");  // ← the whole stack works
```

The full stack — AST → optimization → emit → text — collaborates end-to-end. Folding `2 + 3` into `5` then emitting `5;` is the first real demonstration that everything plumbs together.

## What works

- Every Phase 1 variant: all expressions (Identifier, literals, Binary/Logical/Unary/Assignment/Conditional/Call/Member, Array with elisions, Object with shorthand/method), all statements, and Var/Function declarations.
- All three `EmitOptions`:
  - `pretty: false` (default) → minified single-line
  - `pretty: true` → 2-space-indented multi-line for block bodies
  - `ascii_only: true` → escape non-ASCII as `\uXXXX` / `\u{XXXXXX}` (verified with `"café"` → `"café"`)
  - `source_map: true` (default) → accumulate `(line, col, cv_id)` mappings via `SourceMapBuilder`, serialize as v3 JSON
- Tracks line/col cursor in UTF-16 code units per source-map v3 spec.

## Always-parenthesize policy

v1 always parens `BinaryExpression`/`LogicalExpression`/`ConditionalExpression`/`AssignmentExpression`. Precedence-aware elision is Phase 1.x. `ObjectExpression` at statement position is also wrapped (else `{}` parses as a block).

## CV tracing — both modes per CLOC09

- Traced (`cv: Some`) → `add_mapping` called per identifier-/literal-shaped token.
- Untraced (`cv: None`) → no mappings; output text identical; `source_map` field still contains a valid empty-mappings v3 blob when enabled.

## Tests

17 tests (up from 9 in v0.1.0): defaults+empty, basic expressions with always-paren, typeof spacing, const+function declarations (minified and pretty), array with elision, ObjectExpression paren-wrap at statement start, `ascii_only` escapes Unicode, `source_map` on/off, untraced still emits, **end-to-end `2+3 → 5;`**, `EmitError` `std::error::Error` compat.

## Dependencies
- Runtime: `coding-adventures-closure-source-map`.
- Dev (for end-to-end test): `coding-adventures-closure-pass-constant-fold` + `coding-adventures-closure-pass-pipeline`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p coding-adventures-closure-emitter` (17/17).
- [ ] CI green on ubuntu/macos/windows.

author: patels95
body:
## Problem
On iPhone (any browser — they all use WebKit), with the keyboard open, the sticky search bar "spazzes" while scrolling, and overscrolling at the bottom shoves the bar down with whitespace above it. Android is fine.

## Root cause
To keep the bar above the on-screen keyboard, the JS repositioned it to `window.visualViewport.offsetTop` on every scroll event. On iOS that chase:
- lags the actual scroll → visible jitter/"spazzing", and
- overshoots during bottom rubber-band overscroll → bar pushed down, whitespace above.

Android never hit this because its keyboard resizes the layout viewport, so native `position: sticky` already works without any chasing.

## Fix
- **Stop chasing the visual viewport.** Removed the per-scroll `position: fixed; top: offsetTop` repositioning. The bar is now plain native `position: sticky`.
- **Add `interactive-widget=resizes-content`** to the viewport meta, telling the browser to resize the *layout* for the keyboard (the behavior Android already has) so native sticky stays put — no JS required.
- **Pinch-zoom handling preserved** — while zoomed, the bar still drops to `position: static` so it doesn't cover the enlarged table list.

Net: 11 insertions / 40 deletions — much less code.

## Test plan (please verify on device)
- [ ] **iPhone, keyboard open:** scroll up/down and overscroll at the bottom — bar should no longer jitter, and no whitespace should open above it.
- [ ] **iPhone, keyboard open:** confirm the search bar still stays usefully visible while typing. *(If `interactive-widget` isn't honored by your iOS browser, the bar may scroll with the page instead of staying pinned — please note which happens.)*
- [ ] **Android:** confirm keyboard-open behavior is still smooth (no regression).
- [ ] **Both:** pinch-zoom still doesn't let the bar cover the tables; search + mini summary still work.

> Note: this supersedes the simple revert in #4 (already merged). #4 only swapped the chase technique back; it didn't remove the chase, so the jitter persisted.

author: kennethsinder
body:
## Summary

Closes #2301. Part of #2293 epic, W1 of the port waves — the smallest possible port to prove the dispatch wedge round-trips a real subcommand end to end.

Stacked on #2327 (G6 — parity harness). Depends on G1 (#2294, merged) for the dispatch helpers.

### What changes

- `crates/harn-stdlib/src/stdlib/cli/version.harn` — pure `.harn` impl that renders the ASCII banner or a `JsonEnvelope::ok`-shaped JSON envelope. Build-time constants travel via scoped env vars (`HARN_BUILD_NAME` / `HARN_BUILD_VERSION` / `HARN_BUILD_DESCRIPTION`) set by the dispatch shim.
- `crates/harn-stdlib/src/lib.rs` — registers `cli/version` in `STDLIB_CLI_SCRIPTS`.
- `crates/harn-cli/src/lib.rs` — `Command::Version` arm now calls a new `run_version()` helper that defaults to the `.harn` dispatch and falls back to the legacy `print_version()` / `print_version_json()` when `HARN_CLI_IMPL=rust`.
- `crates/harn-cli/tests/version_dispatch.rs` — integration tests that spawn the binary twice (once per impl) and assert both produce equivalent output.

### Why env vars rather than a new builtin

The version string is the only build-time constant the script needs, and scoping it to the dispatch shim keeps the dependency clear: `harn-cli`'s build-time constants stay owned by `harn-cli`. Adding `harn_version()` as a VM-level builtin would surface `harn-vm`'s `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, which happens to equal `harn-cli`'s today but conceptually is the runtime crate's version.

### Why structural (not byte-for-byte) JSON comparison

Harn's `json_stringify` serializes dict keys alphabetically; serde emits struct fields in declaration order. Both impls produce semantically-equivalent envelopes. The integration test parses both outputs as `serde_json::Value` and asserts structural equality. The banner mode IS byte-for-byte equal (no JSON involved) and the test pins that.

### LOC trajectory

`print_version()` and `print_version_json()` in `lib.rs` stay (7 + 9 lines = 16) so the parity harness can compare both impls; they're dead code once the parity gate proves the .harn impl matches. The C1 ratchet ticket (#2314) will remove them once W1 graduates from parity-test-only to "harn impl is the default and nothing else exists."

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p harn-cli --test version_dispatch` — banner + JSON parity
- [ ] CI: `harn version` and `harn version --json` produce the same output as before
- [ ] Manual: `cargo run --bin harn -- version` and `cargo run --bin harn -- version --json` look right

body:
## Summary

- `SetWorkflowManagementIssueToStoryUseCase.run` threw an uncaught `Error` when an eligible issue carried a `story:<suffix>` label with no matching `regular / <suffix>` Story option. The throw propagated through `runSlowSweepUseCases` and aborted the entire scheduled run before `startPreparation` and every downstream use case could execute, so an affected project made zero progress.
- The use case now skips the unmatched issue and continues the loop, so the remaining issues and all downstream use cases still run.
- The failure is surfaced non-silently by creating an idempotent notification issue in the triggering issue's repository (derived from the issue's owner/repo). Before creating, it searches existing open issues by the stable title and only creates one when none exists, preventing a new duplicate every cycle.
- Adds `searchIssue` to the `IssueRepository` interface and exposes it through `ApiV3CheerioRestIssueRepository` (the underlying `ApiV3IssueRepository.searchIssue` already existed but was not reachable through the interface).

## Behavior

- Matching Story found: assigns the Story and removes the label, unchanged.
- No matching Story: does not throw, skips the issue, and creates exactly one notification issue titled `TDPM: story label "story:<suffix>" has no matching "regular / <suffix>" Story option`, assigned to the repository owner, with a body that links the triggering issue and explains the resolution (add the Story option or correct the label).
- No matching Story but an open notification issue with the same title already exists: no duplicate is created.

## Tests

All verification is covered by unit tests in `SetWorkflowManagementIssueToStoryUseCase.test.ts` (matching, no-match-create-one, no-match-no-duplicate, continue-processing-remaining, non-`regular /` option). Existing tests remain green.

## Progression detail + Achievements list + delete-XP fix

### Delete-XP bug
Deleting a workout removed its workout XP, but **achievement XP persisted** (e.g. "First Rep" +50), so your total barely changed. Now deletion **re-locks any achievement whose condition no longer holds** (`reconcileAchievements`) and recomputes profile XP — so deletes fully revert.

### Progression (pulled forward from Sprint 16)
- **Ranks** ladder: the 10 named titles (First Rep → Magnum Opus) with their XP thresholds.
- **Prestige tiers** beyond Magnum Opus — Magnum Opus **I, II, III, IV, V** — every 15,000 XP.
- New **`/progression`** page (reachable from Profile → "View ranks & prestige"); CharacterCard now shows your prestige label.

### Achievements detail
- New **`/achievements`** page (Profile → trophy case → "See all"): every achievement with its **how-to**, unlocked state, and **hidden/secret** ones shown as "???" until earned (game-style).

### Test plan
- [ ] Delete your only workout → XP drops (achievements it unlocked re-lock)
- [ ] Profile → "View ranks & prestige" → see all 10 ranks + prestige tiers, current highlighted
- [ ] Profile → trophy case → "See all" → full list; hidden ones masked until unlocked

## Summary
- Replace `tests.yml` with `ci.yml` running three jobs in parallel: spotless format check, detekt for unused-code detection, and the existing wasmJs test suite.
- Add detekt `1.23.8` with a minimal config enabling only the five unused-code rules (`UnusedImports`, `UnusedParameter`, `UnusedPrivateClass`, `UnusedPrivateMember`, `UnusedPrivateProperty`) so the check stays focused on what was requested.
- Register a `detektAll` aggregate task on `:composeApp` so a single Gradle invocation covers every KMP source set.
- Update `deploy.yml`'s `workflow_run` reference from `Tests` to `CI` to match the workflow rename.

- detekt `2.0.0-alpha.3` is built against Kotlin 2.3.21 but its Gradle plugin is not published to Maven Central or the Gradle Plugin Portal yet, so `1.23.8` (the latest stable on Maven Central) is used. Unused-code rules are syntactic and verified to work against the project's Kotlin 2.3.21 sources.
- Detection was verified locally by temporarily adding an unused `kotlin.random.Random` import to `App.kt` and confirming detekt failed with the expected `UnusedImports` finding.

body:
### Motivation
- Activar en 0.7.1 una exportación PDF real aprovechando el HTML limpio ya disponible sin reintroducir lógica de cierre ni cambios en borrador local. 
- Ofrecer una solución fiable en Windows basada en el diálogo de impresión del sistema como paso intermedio seguro frente a integrar APIs nativas de WebView2 que requieren cambios riesgosos. 

### Description
- Se implementa `src/lib/documents/pdfExport.ts` para solicitar destino `.pdf`, reutilizar `buildPdfSourceHtml(state)` y, en Windows, abrir una vista de impresión con el HTML limpio para que el usuario elija “Guardar como PDF”.
- Se añade `requestPdfDestination` y se modifica `exportDocumentAsPdf` para soportar cancelación (retorna `false`) y errores claros fuera de Windows (`PDF_EXPORT_WINDOWS_PENDING_MESSAGE`).
- Se actualiza la etiqueta del menú en `src/components/toolbar/Toolbar.tsx` a `Imprimir / Guardar como PDF` y el mensaje de error en `src/App.tsx` a `Exportar PDF:` para reflejar el flujo real dependiente del diálogo de impresión.
- Se actualiza versionado y metadatos a `0.7.1` en `package.json`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` y la entrada `medo` en `src-tauri/Cargo.lock`, se agrega entrada de changelog y se actualiza `docs/tasks.md` con la decisión técnica y alcance por plataforma.
- Se añaden/actualizan tests en `src/lib/documents/pdfExport.test.ts` para cubrir reutilización del HTML limpio, ausencia de UI de copiado en la fuente, cancelación del diálogo, fallback claro en no-Windows y la invocación del flujo de impresión en Windows.

### Testing
- Ejecuté `pnpm install` y la instalación completó correctamente. 
- Ejecuté `pnpm lint` y `pnpm test`, y los tests unitarios (incluyendo los nuevos/actualizados de `pdfExport`) pasaron correctamente. 
- Ejecuté `pnpm build` y la compilación del frontend produjo artefactos válidos. 
- Ejecuté `pnpm tauri:build` en este entorno Linux y falló por una dependencia de sistema (`glib-2.0`/pkg-config) faltante; la validación del empaquetado/instalador debe realizarse en runner Windows (`windows-release-validation`) donde está previsto que se complete la build nativa.

author: h4ck3r-netizen
body:
## Summary
Fixes cross-chain replay attack vulnerability in CrossChainBridge.sol per issue #920.

## Changes
- Added `block.chainid` to transfer hash to prevent cross-chain replay
- Added `address(this)` to transfer hash to prevent post-upgrade replay
- Added per-sender nonce mapping for frontend queryability
- Added zero-address check on ecrecover result
- Implemented EIP-712 domain separator with name, version, chainId, verifyingContract
- Added comprehensive test suite covering all attack vectors

## Verification
- Signed messages include chain ID, nonce per sender, and contract address
- Same message cannot be replayed on different chain or same chain
- Contract upgrade does not allow old message replay
- ecrecover zero-address result is explicitly rejected
- EIP-712 domain separator correctly constructed
- Nonces are queryable per sender
- Tests cover: cross-chain replay, same-chain replay, post-upgrade replay, invalid signature, EIP-712 verification

## Summary

- Stop annotation SVG geometry and active point handles from capturing viewer pointer events.
- Keep only interactive controls, such as delete handles and pending text input, pointer-enabled.

author: ashraful19
body:
## What's in v1.0.0

### New Features
- **AI Run Observability** — Orbit records one-off SDK calls (agent_text, agent_stream, image, audio, embeddings, reranking, file, store, failover, tool) to its own `orbit_ai_runs` table. Captures tokens, cost, latency, prompt/response text, and errors.
- **Run Explorer** — Livewire-powered list with search, 7 filter dimensions (operation, status, provider, model, agent, conversation state, date range), sort, pagination, and delete.
- **Run Detail View** — Inspect individual run metadata, token/cost breakdown, latency, linked conversation, payload JSON inspector, usage + events panels.
- **Latency Percentiles** — P50, P95, P99 latency metrics displayed in Provider Health, computed from merged conversation + run data.
- **Agent Health Score UI** — Health score (0–100) with status badge now visible in the Agent Inspector panel, including request count, error rate, and average tokens.
- **Export Buttons** — Pest and JSONL export action buttons added to the Message Timeline conversation header.
- **Dashboard Link Cards** — Quick navigation cards from dashboard to Usage, Pricing, Alerts, Health, Prompts.
- **Cost Column** — Estimated cost shown in dashboard agent breakdown table.
- **Raw Token Display** — Token counts shown as raw values instead of M/K masking.
- **Test Email Action** — Send test budget alert emails directly from the Alerts UI.
- **Per-Alert Recipients** — Configure specific email addresses per budget alert.
- **Missing Pricing Tracking** — Provider+model combinations without pricing rules are flagged.
- **HTML & Plain-Text Budget Emails** — Polished email templates for budget exceeded notifications.

### Changed
- **Unified Usage Page** — `/usage` now combines today's stats and full analytics into one page.
- **Merged Analytics** — TokenAggregator, CostCalculator, BudgetMonitor, and Provider Health merge data from both SDK tables and `orbit_ai_runs`.
- **Provider Health Data Source** — Always merges from both `orbit_ai_runs` and `agent_conversation_messages`.
- **Period Selector** — Visible date range indicator (`Showing data since...`) in Provider Health.
- **Chart Palette** — 15 distinct non-brand colors for better visual differentiation.
- **Navigation** — Renamed Analytics → Usage.

### Fixed
- **CostCalculator Property Names** — Corrected `total_input_tokens` → `input_tokens` for accurate cost calculations.
- **Provider Health Period Filter** — Period selector now correctly filters both conversation and run data.
- **Usage Index Grid** — Enforced 3-column grid layout.
- **Budget Alert URL** — Fixed dashboard link from nonexistent `/usage/dashboard` to `/usage`.
- **MySQL Reserved Word** — Backtick-quoted `usage` column in AgentHealthScorer SQL.

### Docs
- Updated changelog versions to match actual tags (0.0.3 → 1.0.0)
- Removed stale/incorrect content (CSV export, Global Search, Slack channels, Arena routes, `/usage/dashboard` redirect)
- Added runs feature doc page
- Restructured sidebar: Export Formats moved to Reference, Global Search removed
- Fixed table name: `orbit_arena_sessions` → `orbit_prompt_lab_sessions`

### Observability Config
```php
'observability' => [
    'enabled' => true,
    'store_runs' => true,
    'capture_text_payloads' => true,
    'max_payload_length' => 10000,
    'excluded_operations' => [],
],
```

### New Table
`orbit_ai_runs` — Stores one-off SDK invocation records with operation, status, provider, model, tokens, cost, latency, payload, usage, events, and error columns.

author: bhubbard
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR implements a robust offline caching and synchronization layer in the Admin UI using IndexedDB. It enables instant page rendering by serving cached data as `placeholderData` before fresh data resolves from the network. It also introduces multi-tab cache invalidation coordination, offline background sync, and resilient optimistic mutations that automatically roll back on error.

Specifically, this includes:
- **IndexedDB caching layer:** Abstractions (`db.ts`, `cache-store.ts`) for caching singletons, detail records, and list content, with pre-warmup.
- **TanStack Query Integration:** The `useCachedQuery` hook that falls back to the cache instantly and refreshes from the network in the background.
- **Optimistic Mutations:** Helpers (`optimisticDelete`, `optimisticUpdate`, `optimisticListItemUpdate`) to immediately update the local query and IndexedDB states, handling query rollbacks on failure.
- **Multi-tab Coordination:** `BroadcastChannel`-based communication to invalidate and sync cache stores across multiple open browser tabs.
- **Offline & Background Sync:** Logic for managing offline states and synchronizing pending local changes back to the server once online.
- **Admin UI Integration:** Integrated caching/optimistic updates into Admin UI routes and components (Settings, Media, Menus, Taxonomies, Users, and Bylines).
- **Tests:** A full suite of unit tests for all caching, synchronization, broadcasting, and mutation features.

💡 What: Wrapped `filteredA` and `filteredB` calculations in `useMemo` hooks, and hoisted `search.toLowerCase()` outside of the `.filter` callbacks in `MixExplorer.tsx`.
🎯 Why: Previously, filtering the `substances` array would re-run completely on every render of `MixExplorer`, and for every item in the array, the search query string was being converted to lowercase multiple times, causing unnecessary string allocations and high CPU/GC usage when users typed in the search inputs.
📊 Impact: Reduces CPU cycles and GC pressure significantly when typing in the search bar. The filtering operation is now memoized and the string lowercase conversion is strictly O(1) per array instead of O(N).
🔬 Measurement: Profile the React component while typing in the "SUBSTANCE A" or "SUBSTANCE B" search fields; observe reduced rendering time and memory usage.

author: fiorenzobrioni
body:
## Summary

Replaces the legacy sin-carrier marble algorithm with a production-grade procedural pipeline matching Arnold's `marble2`, RenderMan's `PxrMarble`, and Cycles' cinematic Marble. The new implementation eliminates visible periodicity along the vein axis and enables realistic multi-scale vein coexistence (thin + thick veins in the same slab).

## Key Changes

### Core Algorithm (`MarbleTexture.cs`)
- **Removed:** Legacy sin-carrier formula `vein(p) = sin(scale·(p·axis)·freq + str·fBm(p))` with `vein_sharpness` power-of-sin sharpening
- **Added:** Four-stage pipeline:
  1. **Anisotropic geological fold** via `DomainWarp.Anisotropic` — per-axis tectonic shear with max component aligned to `vein_axis`
  2. **Recursive (IQ) domain warp** via `DomainWarp.Recursive` — configurable iterations (0/2/3) to break all visible tiling
  3. **Multi-scale ridged vein field** via `MultiScaleRidgedField.Sample` — 1–3 independent ridged layers composited via log-sum-exp soft-max for local dominance
  4. **Vein-thickness remap** — smoothstep on ridged value centered on `vein_thickness` with half-width `vein_softness` (replaces broken power-of-sin)
- **Added:** Background fBm for low-frequency tonal variation (`color_variation` parameter)
- **Added:** Optional mineral impurities (Voronoi specks or external texture) that bias color-ramp lookup
- **Preserved:** `ColorRamp` multi-stop support and two-color lerp fallback

### New Core Classes
- **`DomainWarp.cs`** — Pure-function helpers for anisotropic fold and recursive IQ warp, built on `Perlin.NoiseVector`
- **`MultiScaleRidgedField.cs`** — Soft-max compositing of independent ridged layers with numerically stable log-sum-exp

### YAML Schema (`SceneData.cs`, `SceneLoader.cs`)
- **Removed:** `vein_frequency`, `vein_sharpness`, `secondary_wave` (legacy cross-vein block)
- **Added:** `warp_amplitude`, `warp_scale`, `warp_iterations`, `fold_amplitude`, `fold_scale`, `vein_layers`, `vein_scale`, `vein_weight`, `vein_thickness`, `vein_softness`, `color_variation`, `impurities_density`, `impurities_scale`, `impurities_weight`, `impurities_texture`, `cracks_density`, `cracks_scale`, `cracks_softness`, `cracks_weight`
- **Updated:** `SceneLoader.ApplyTextureParams` to route external impurities texture via `sceneDir` parameter

### Material Library Updates
- **`stones.yaml`:** Recalibrated all 6 marble variants (Carrara, Calacatta, Statuario, Thassos, Nero Marquinia, Arabescato) with new parameters; added inline documentation for each variant's geological character
- **`plasters.yaml`:** Updated Veneziano stucco to use thickness/softness instead of legacy sharpness
- **`minerals-gems.yaml`:** Updated Malachite to use 3-layer ridged + aggressive warp
- **`organics.yaml`, `grounds.yaml`:** Updated marble references to new schema

### Documentation
- **`MarbleTexture.cs` docstring:** Comprehensive algorithm description with YAML examples (Carrara defaults + Calacatta gold with impurities)
- **`scene-reference.md` / `riferimento-scene.md`:** Replaced legacy parameter table with production-grade pipeline explanation and new YAML block
- **`03-materials.md` (EN+IT):** Updated tutorial examples and removed legacy secondary-wave explanation
- **`DEVLOG.

author: chernushoov
body:
## Проблема
Живой 3D-блок конфигуратора рендерил материалы блёкло-серыми — хуже, чем превью на главной (`configurator-preview.jpg`), которое снято с богатой v2+PBR-сборки (`19383e9`).

## Причина
`plates-v2` GLB-плиты задумывались как **opt-in** песочница (`?plates=v2`), но `ensureCorrectPlate` грузил их **всегда** при наличии `def.glb_plate`. У GLB-тела cube-UV пересжимает body-композит → крупные чипы терраццо превращаются в серую кашу.

## Фикс (точечный, +7/−1)
Гейт GLB за `?plates=v2`; дефолт = процедурная коробка-плита (UV 0..1 → текстура в эталонном масштабе). Все поздние фиксы (цены, мобайл, share-link, чипы, textures-песочницы) не тронуты.

## Проверка
Headless WebGL (Playwright Chromium), сам просмотрел кадры:
- дефолт-терраццо снова богатое (совпадает с эталоном `19383e9`);
- 6 материалов рисуются текстурами, не серой кашей;
- `?plates=v2`-песочница по-прежнему грузит слоёные GLB.

## Summary

- **Root cause**: The upstream `KlipperScreen-install.sh` bakes `ConditionPathExists=/dev/tty0` into the service unit. The Q2 doesn't have `/dev/tty0`, so systemd silently skips starting the service every time.

- **Uninstall**: `uninstall_klipperscreen()` now also removes the drop-in directory.

body:
## Summary

- Rewrites the 11 hardcoded ladder/route constants in `run_extraction_v5.py` so model IDs derive from `COST_PROFILES[<profile>].cell_aliases` via a new `derive_ladder_for_cell(cost_profile, lane_class, capability_tier, stage='primary')` API.
- Adds per-request failover to `llm_runtime.call_llm_with_ladder`: a 5xx/timeout/429/quota_or_billing response on a non-final hop advances to the next ladder route immediately (retry_attempts_override=1), while the final hop preserves `cfg.retry_max_attempts` because no fallback remains.
- Filter logic now honors **both** `cfg.provider_denylist` (preflight-derived) **and** `cfg.disabled_providers` (--disable-provider CLI). The CLI kill-switch was previously a no-op for ladder iteration — fixed as part of E7.
- Legacy ladder constants stay importable via a PEP 562 `__getattr__` proxy that emits a one-shot DeprecationWarning per name. Removal scheduled after E8.

## Scope

- `services/repo-truth-extractor/run_extraction_v5.py` (+307/-29)
- `services/repo-truth-extractor/llm_runtime.py` (+131/-20) — **packet allowlist deviation**, see note below
- 4 new test files (39 tests total)
- `proof/rte-cost-profile-redesign/TP-RTE-COSTPROFILE-E7-LADDERS-FAILOVER-001/PROOF.json` + `sha256sums.txt`

No changes to `model_map.yaml` (E8 owns that) or to any other module.

## Stacked-PR base

This PR's base is `codex/rte-costprofile-e4-finish-001` (the E4 branch), **not** `main`. Series pattern operator-authorized:

```
main → goofy (consolidation branch)
       └── E3 (#687, MERGED)
           └── E4 (#688, OPEN)
               └── E7 (this PR)
                   └── E8 (next)
                       └── ...
                       └── F-VERIFY (final, merges to main)
```

## Validation

**PASS:**
- 39 new tests pass (`test_per_request_failover.py` 11, `test_cell_aliased_ladders.py` 14, `test_disable_provider_kill_switch.py` 6, `test_legacy_ladder_deprecation_warning.py` 8).
- 30 existing regression tests pass (`test_cost_profiles.py`, `test_run_extraction_v5_cost_cap.py`, `test_run_extraction_v5_promptset_truth.py`).
- `python -m compileall` clean for both modified files.
- `python -m json.tool` on packet + PROOF.json + sha256sums.txt verify.
- Dry-run `python run_extraction_v5.py --phase A --dry-run --cost-profile value-default --print-phase-routing` produces valid JSON with resolved model IDs.
- `DeprecationWarning` verified under `warnings.simplefilter('error')` for legacy ladder access.
- `git diff --check` clean (whitespace + conflict markers).
- pal/thinkdeep + pal/challenge (gpt-5.2 external) on failover design before implementation.
- pal/codereview (gpt-5.2 external 2-step): 2 MED + 4 LOW; addressed F-LOW-1 (dead vars), F-MED-1 (broad TypeError fallback → `inspect.signature` based dispatch), F-OBS-4 (added explicit from-import test).
- pal/precommit (gpt-5.2 external 3-step): MED finding `cfg.provider_denylist` getattr consistency addressed.

**NOT_RUN:**
- Live provider calls (`RTE_DISABLE_LIVE_LLM_IN_TESTS=1`; live testing deferred by operator).
- `model_map.yaml` v3 integration (E8 packet covers).

## Residual Risks (documented in PROOF.json)

1. **Live LLM verification not run** — failover loop tested exhaustively via mocks (11 dedicated tests) but real 5xx/timeout behavior across OpenRouter/XAI/Gemini not exercised in this PR. F-VERIFY closes this.
2. **Legacy model ID spelling preserved**: `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (dash) in legacy ladders vs `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` (dot) in `cell_aliases`. Preserved by design — E8 reconciles when expanding cell_aliases coverage. `spend_ledger` baseline rates use the dash form so legacy ladder users are correctly costed.
3. **`_PROVIDER_INFERENCE_MAP` is intentionally narrow** (6 slash + 2 direct prefixes). Future cell_aliases adding models with new prefixes (`deepseek/`, `qwen/`, etc.) will fail closed with `ValueError`. E8 extends as needed.
4. **Cache env snapshot covers only the specific alias_key** — chained env references not in cache key. For E7 scope `cli_overrides` are concrete model_id strings, not chained placeholders; documented in `derive_ladder_for_cell` docstring.
5. **Packet allowlist deviation: `llm_runtime.py`** — the failover loop architecturally belongs in `llm_runtime.call_llm_with_ladder`; moving it into `run_extraction_v5.py` would have meant duplicating the loop or building a parallel orchestrator. Operator-bless requested.
6. **Pre-existing unrelated failure in `test_code_prescan_truthfulness.py`** (KeyError on `imports`/`symbols`). Appears on E4 HEAD pre-E7. Different module (CodePrescan); not blocking E7.

## PAL Chain (per [feedback-pal-chain-extensive] memory)

- **pal/thinkdeep (gpt-5.2)**: 6 design tensions T1-T6 surfaced. Validated shared hop budget, fast-failover intermediate + normal final hop, prefix-based provider inference, internal-callers approach, implicit cap via existing knobs.
- **pal/challenge**: D1-D5 attacked; reconciled with documented tradeoffs.
- **pal/codereview external 2-step**: 2 MED + 4 LOW; 3 fixed in this commit, 3 documented as residual.
- **pal/precommit external 3-step**: 1 MED fixed; 2 spurious CRITICAL findings verified as false positives via empirical evidence (compileall + 69 passing tests + direct file inspection — the `response_text`/`request_meta` keys were already pre-E7, and `llm_runtime_call_llm` is an aliased import at L233).

## Notes for reviewer

- The `_callable_accepts_kwarg` introspection helper deliberately falls back to "True" if `inspect.signature` fails (built-ins, C extensions). The dispatch then passes the kwarg and any genuine incompatibility surfaces as a `TypeError` at the call site — propagating to the operator rather than being silently swallowed. This is intentional and replaces a pre-design draft's broad `try/except TypeError` that could mask unrelated bugs.
- The deprecation proxy uses a module-global `_LEGACY_LADDER_WARNED: Set[str]` for one-shot warning state. Single-threaded CLI assumption; if accessed from multiple threads concurrently the race could produce duplicate warnings (benign) but not data corruption.
- Distinct `escalation_trigger` strings (`routing_all_routes_preflight_denylisted` / `routing_all_routes_operator_disabled` / `routing_all_routes_unusable_combined` / `routing_empty_ladder`) replace the old `routing_all_routes_denylisted` token. Verified via grep that NO in-tree code (excluding `run_extraction_v3.py` which has its own copy and is out of scope per packet invariants) consumes the old token by string match.

author: warstorm548
body:
## Summary

Root-cause hotfix for the install failure that v0.8.1 didn't catch:

```
install failed: zip open: invalid archive: Could not find EOCD
```

(reported on launcher v0.8.0 → still present on v0.8.1, Windows / Dev channel).

## Diagnosis — three independent sources converged

| Source | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Online research agent** (cited GitHub REST docs, self_update README, reqwest docs) | GitHub REST API asset endpoints return **JSON metadata** unless the request carries `Accept: application/octet-stream`. |
| **Cargo-registry source-code agent** (read `self_update-0.41.0/src/backends/github.rs:23-34` + `update.rs:234`) | `self_update` parses `asset["url"]` (the **API URL**, NOT `browser_download_url`) into `ReleaseAsset.download_url`, and adds the Accept header before downloading. |
| **Our own code** (`launcher/src/updater/branches/github.rs:78`) | We forward `a.download_url` from self_update straight into our wrapper — so we ARE hitting the API URL — but we never set the Accept header. |

So our `GET https://api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/{id}` returned the asset's JSON metadata (~few hundred bytes), saved as `.download-foo.zip`, then `zip::ZipArchive::new` (correctly) failed with the missing-EOCD message because the file is JSON not a zip. This explains:
- "quickly lights up" — JSON is tiny, downloads instantly
- EOCD error — file isn't a zip
- v0.8.1's `if total > 0 && downloaded != total` skipped — JSON had a small Content-Length that matched the downloaded byte count

The launcher's **own binary self-update** path has worked all along because `self_update` sets the header internally; our hand-rolled **game-files** download was the only path missing it.

## Fix

- **Add `Accept: application/octet-stream`** to the asset GET in `stage_install`. Single line, root cause closed. Mirrors `self_update-0.41.0/src/update.rs:234`.
- **Magic-byte sniff post-download** as a permanent safety net: 4-byte read against `PK\x03\x04` (zip) or `1f 8b` (gzip). Catches BOTH truncated AND wrong-content failures without depending on Content-Length being set. On mismatch the error includes the first 4 bytes + a 256-byte sample of the file content — so the next failure carries its own diagnosis (`{"url":...}` ⇒ JSON metadata regression, `<html>` ⇒ CDN error page, etc.).
- **`tracing::debug!` → `tracing::info!`** on the pre-extract diagnostic so users running from a terminal see `downloaded / total / on_disk` without env-filter changes.
- **Drop the v0.8.1 Content-Length checks** — superseded by the magic-byte sniff and didn't fire on the real-world bug anyway.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo check -p launcher --all-targets` — clean.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p launcher --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo test -p launcher` — 8/8 pass (unchanged).
- [ ] **Live end-to-end**: cut `launcher-v0.8.2-dev.1` after merge, user self-updates via the in-app banner, retries Install Dev Game. Expected: download visibly takes seconds (~36 MB at any reasonable bandwidth), extract succeeds.

author: xuelin-wang
body:
ummary
  
  Adds a React + Vite demo UI for visualising agent-flow runs, including a live flow chart with resume-point markers, an append-only audit log, step detail inspection, and state JSON
  view. Two new backend endpoints (GET /agent-flow/runs and GET /agent-flow/runs/{run_id}/audit) are added to support the UI's polling loop.

  Rationale

  - The replay/resume implementation was complete but had no visual surface — the only way to observe run progression, checkpoint recovery, or the audit trail was through raw API calls or
   CLI output. The demo UI makes these features tangible for review and demonstration.
  - A separate Vite dev server with a proxy is used in development to avoid CORS friction; the built output is served directly by FastAPI under /demo in production, keeping deployment a
  single process.

  Changes

  bases/xagent/api_http/app.py
  create_app() previously called load_runtime_config(ApiHttpConfig, []) unconditionally at module level, making config files unreachable when uvicorn imports the module directly (no CLI
  argv). The XAGENT_API_HTTP_CONFIG env var provides an escape hatch. The static /demo mount is conditional on the directory existing so the server starts clean without a built UI.

  components/xagent/agent_flow/service.py
  AgentFlowService now accepts and stores step_repository in its constructor — previously it was created inside from_repositories() but not threaded through, so get_audit_record()
  couldn't reach it. This is a constructor signature change that affects any direct instantiation outside the factory.

  components/xagent/agent_persistence/
  list_runs() added to the RunRepository protocol and InMemoryRunRepository. The in-memory implementation returns deep copies to match the defensive copy pattern used by other read
  methods.

  bases/xagent/demo_ui/src/App.tsx
  Uses recursive setTimeout (not setInterval) with an alive flag so polling stops cleanly on unmount and when the run reaches a terminal status. An activeTabRef ref is updated on every
  render to avoid the async poll callback closing over a stale activeTab value when deciding whether to set the audit-dot indicator.

  bases/xagent/demo_ui/src/components/flow/FlowChart.tsx
  Resume-point detection works by comparing audit entries per iteration: if all steps in an iteration are skipped and the next iteration contains at least one non-skipped step, a visual
  resume-point divider is injected between them.

  bases/xagent/demo_ui/src/api/client.ts
  All API calls use relative paths (/agent-flow/…) so the same build works under both the Vite proxy and the FastAPI static mount with no environment-specific config.

  Review Notes

  - AgentFlowService.__init__ now requires step_repository; any test or caller that constructs AgentFlowService directly (not via in_memory() or from_repositories()) will need updating.
  - The demo UI's package-lock.json (2500+ lines) is committed. If the project policy is to gitignore lockfiles for non-deployed apps, this could be removed — but it's committed
  intentionally here for reproducible dev setup.
  - Polling intervals are hardcoded (RUNS_POLL_MS = 3000, RUN_POLL_MS = 2000); no back-off or SSE upgrade is implemented. Acceptable for a demo tool, but worth noting if this base is
  reused for production monitoring.

- Adds a first-class `Project.on_shuffle` hook fired from `PlayerState.shuffle_discard_into_deck`. Hooks may return a card pulled from the discard to be placed on top of the new deck.

author: vdv001
body:
Closes #308. Re-opens previously-closed #307 (closed due к branch name violation — renamed and recreated).

## Problem

`TestRefreshToken_RotatesAndDetectsReuse/concurrent_refresh_—_atomic_claim_yields_exactly_one_new_pair` has been intermittently failing CI on PRs since v0.159.0 (auth Tier 1 security hotfix landed the test). Most recently blocked PR #306 v0.163.1 announcements polish on 2 of 2 retry cycles.

## Root cause

When 8 goroutines present the same refresh token:

1. Winner: `RevokeIfAbsent(JTI)` returns `claimed=true`, proceeds toward token generation.
2. Loser: `RevokeIfAbsent(JTI)` returns `claimed=false` → triggers `RevokeAllForUser(userID, time.Now().Unix(), refreshTTL)` → cascade epoch = NOW ≥ T (reused token's iat).
3. Winner runs `IsRevokedForUser(userID, T)` later in `RefreshToken`. Production `>=` boundary means epoch ≥ T = true → winner ALSO bails with `ErrRefreshTokenReused`.

Under `-race` scheduling, loser cascades often land before the winner finishes its boundary check. successCount = 0 instead of asserted 1 → test fails.

## Fix (layered)

1. **Usecase cascade epoch** — `auth_usecase.go:502` passes `issuedAtUnix` instead of `time.Now().Unix()`.
2. **Redis adapter boundary** — `revoked_token_repository_redis.go:134` uses strict `>` instead of `>=`.
3. **Stub** — `auth_usecase_test.go:562` mirrors production strict `>` for consistency.
4. **Interface docs** — make the strict semantics explicit.

RFC 6749 §10.4 token-family revocation semantics preserved.

## Local verification

- `go test -count=50 -run "TestRefreshToken_RotatesAndDetectsReuse/concurrent" ./internal/modules/auth/application/usecases/...` → **all 50 pass**
- `go test -race -count=20 ...` → **all 20 pass**
- Full auth module test suite → green
- Whole project `go build ./...` → green

## Related

- v0.159.0 ADR-2 (#279) introduced the cascade + this race.
- PR #306 blocked by this flake — rebase #306 after this merges.
- `feedback_bcrypt_race_ci_timeout.md` memory noted the flake; this is the real root-cause fix.

author: hyperaiofficail
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** The `process_tool` endpoint blindly accessed `file.filename` inside `os.path.basename`. Because `UploadFile.filename` can be `None` or an empty string, this could result in an unhandled `AttributeError`, causing a 500 Internal Server Error (potential DoS vector via unhandled exceptions). Additionally, `os.path.basename` fails to fully sanitize malicious filenames that evaluate purely to `.` or `..`, leaving potential directory manipulation vulnerabilities downstream.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could crash the process by sending malformed multipart form data, or potentially manipulate generated file paths using traversal payloads that survive basic `os.path.basename` sanitization.
🔧 **Fix:** Implemented safe access to `file.filename` using `getattr(file, "filename", None)`, stripping whitespace from the resulting sanitized string, and providing a safe fallback `"unnamed"` if the result is invalid, empty, or evaluates to `.` or `..`. A comprehensive test suite was also added in `backend/test_file_upload.py`.
✅ **Verification:** Verify by running `PYTHONPATH=backend python3 -m unittest backend/test_file_upload.py`. The tests cover all permutations of `None`, empty, whitespace-only, and path-traversing payloads.

author: powercreek
body:
Closes #84.

## Bug
After #83 merged, fresh `hermes --provider X --model Y` invocations leave `config.yaml` without `mcp_servers.hermes-internal`. Worker boots with zero G2/G3/G4 MCP tools — the same symptom #82 was supposed to fix.

## Root cause
#83 placed the `ensure_internal_mcp_server()` call in `tui_gateway/entry.py`. That file is only on the path when the **TUI gateway subprocess** spawns (interactive TUI shell active). Direct `hermes …` CLI invocations land in `hermes_cli/main.py:main` per `[project.scripts] hermes = "hermes_cli.main:main"` — never touch `tui_gateway/entry.py` — so the autowire never fires.

## Fix
Adds the autowire call inside `hermes_cli/main.py`'s CLI startup block, between `discover_plugins()` and `discover_mcp_tools()` (around line 12756). The block is gated on `args.command in {None, "chat", "acp", "rl"}` — covers bare invocation, chat, acp, rl. Order matters: autowire must run **before** `discover_mcp_tools` so the freshly-written entry is visible on the same boot (the `load_config` mtime-cache auto-invalidates on `save_config`).

The #83 `tui_gateway/entry.py` call stays — correct for the TUI-gateway subprocess path. Idempotent: calling both is safe.

## Tests (`tests/test_autowire_cli_path.py` — 3 cases, all pass)

- `hermes_cli/main.py` contains `ensure_internal_mcp_server()` at all
- The call appears BEFORE the `from tools.mcp_tool import discover_mcp_tools` line (ordering regression catcher)
- The call sits INSIDE the `_AGENT_COMMANDS`-gated block (not outside, where it would fire for `hermes mcp add` / `hermes hooks list` / introspection commands too)

Total: **23 autowire tests pass** (3 new + 20 from #83 still green).

## Why source-level tests
Exercising the full CLI `main()` requires mocking argparse, provider auth, model resolution — orders of magnitude more setup than the bug warrants. The regression risk is "someone deletes the call" or "someone reorders past `discover_mcp_tools`" — both caught at the source level.

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge, rebuild worker container
- [ ] Run fresh `hermes --provider X --model Y` (no operator-side `mcp_servers` config)
- [ ] Verify `~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/config.yaml` contains `mcp_servers.hermes-internal`
- [ ] Verify worker can invoke `grafted_context_fetch` without operator wiring
- [ ] With `HERMES_DISABLE_INTERNAL_MCP=1`, verify NO entry is written

## Summary

Addresses 5 of the 6 recommended findings from the security scan over master @ b05d95a:

- [x] **#2 CVE-2026-33186** (CRITICAL) — bump `google.golang.org/grpc` to v1.79.3
- [x] **#7 nine HIGH Go stdlib CVEs** — bump Dockerfile build base to `golang:1.26.3` (1.25.10 isn't on Docker Hub yet; 1.26.3 covers everything per trivy's fixed-version column)
- [x] **#8 two HIGH reachable x/net CVEs** — bump `golang.org/x/net` to v0.55.0
- [x] **#9 five HIGH ubuntu kernel-header CVEs** — replace `libpcap-dev` with `libpcap0.8` in the final image, which drops `linux-libc-dev` (a transitive dep). As a side effect the image shrinks 210MB → 138MB.
- [x] **#3 gRPC reflection** — gate `reflection.Register` on `GRPC_REFLECTION=1` so production deployments don't advertise their service surface
- [x] **#5 base RBAC missing namespace** — add `namespace: meshnet` to the `ClusterRoleBinding` subject (the rendered all-in-one manifests already had it; the base disagreed)
- [x] **#6 RBAC `verbs: ["*"]`** — narrow to the actually-exercised set (`get/list/watch/create/update/patch/delete` on `gwirekobjs`; `get/list/watch/update/patch` on `topologies`; `get/update/patch` on `/status` subresources)
- [x] **#4 PeerNodeIP SSRF** — validate `wire.PeerNodeIP` against the cluster's node list (InternalIP + ExternalIP) before `grpc.Dial`, with a 30s TTL cache. Adds `nodes get/list/watch` to RBAC. Unit-tested with `client-go/fake`.

## Intentionally deferred

- **#1 mTLS for the gRPC daemon** — the highest-impact finding from the scan, but doing it well needs a cert provisioning design (cert-manager? kubelet-issued serving certs? bootstrap secret?), and shipping env-var-gated TLS that's off by default would create the appearance of a fix without the substance. Worth its own PR with a real design document.
- **#10 `privileged: true` → explicit capabilities** — removing `privileged: true` and replacing with `NET_ADMIN/SYS_ADMIN/NET_RAW` is plausible but cannot be safely landed without cluster testing (Bidirectional netns mount + raw sockets behavior under reduced caps is the open question). Recommend a dedicated PR with an e2e run.

- [x] `make docker` — builds linux/amd64 cleanly on the new base image
- [ ] `trivy image` against the new image to confirm the CVE counts drop (running in parallel; will paste numbers in a comment)
- [ ] Apply `manifests/base/` to a real cluster and confirm RBAC narrowing doesn't break daemon startup or wire reconciliation
- [ ] Apply `manifests/meshnet-grpc.yaml` to a cluster with GRPC inter-node links and watch a peer create succeed (validates peer-IP allowlist path)
- [ ] Confirm `gwirekobj` create with an off-cluster IP is now rejected with a clear log line

433129e fix(rbac): add namespace to base ClusterRoleBinding, narrow verbs

body:
## Description

Fixes #349 — moves the socket validity check (`$this->socket instanceof \Socket`) from **after** `socket_select()` to **before** it in `StreamConnection::sendFrame()`. Also applies the same fix to `readFrame()` and `readLoop()` which had the identical bug pattern.

## Changes

- **`src/StreamConnection.php`**: Added null socket guard at the top of `sendFrame()`, `readFrame()`, and `readLoop()` before any `socket_select()` call
- **`tests/StreamConnectionTest.php`**: Added 6 unit tests covering null-socket-throws for all three methods (both on fresh connection and after `close()`)

## Details

The original bug: `sendFrame()` built `$write = [$this->socket]` before checking if the socket was valid. If `close()` was called (setting `$this->socket = null`), `socket_select()` received `[null]`, producing a PHP 8 TypeError instead of a clean `ConnectionException`.

The fix moves the `instanceof \Socket` guard to the top of each method. In single-threaded PHP there is no TOCTOU concern — the check is definitive before any socket API call.

## Testing

- ✅ 622 unit tests pass (616 original + 6 new)
- ✅ PHP_CodeSniffer clean (PSR-12)
- ✅ 6 new tests cover null-socket-throws for sendFrame/readFrame/readLoop

author: mabry1985
body:
## Summary

`KnowledgeIngestionService.upsertChunk` previously did a content UPDATE without touching the `embeddings` row or `hype_queries`/`hype_embeddings` columns. The background workers select on **missing** rows — `LEFT JOIN embeddings IS NULL` and `hype_queries IS NULL`. So once those existed for the original content, neither worker would refresh them, and hybrid retrieval kept ranking changed chunks by stale vectors.

## Fix

In the UPDATE branch of `upsertChunk`:

1. SELECT old content alongside the existence check.
2. Compare against incoming content.
3. If they differ, delete the chunk's `embeddings` row and null out `hype_queries` + `hype_embeddings` in the same transaction.

The workers' existing selection queries pick the chunk back up on the next pass. No-op re-ingestion (same content) takes no extra writes.

## Test plan

Adds `apps/server/tests/knowledge-embedding-invalidation.test.ts` — in-memory SQLite covering:

- [x] Identical re-ingest keeps embeddings + HyPE intact
- [x] Content change deletes embeddings row and nulls hype columns
- [x] After invalidation, the embedding and HyPE worker selection queries both match the chunk again

## Note on the (former) stack

This was originally opened as a stacked PR on top of #3659. #3659 squash-merged within four minutes (auto-merge fired immediately on CI green), deleting the parent branch and tripping the exact "squash-merged a parent while children were still open" gotcha documented in [docs/dev/merge-policy.md](../docs/dev/merge-policy.md#dont-squash-merge-a-parent-pr-while-children-are-still-open).

Recovery was textbook from the doc: `git rebase --onto origin/main <old-parent-tip> <child-branch>`, then retarget. Took about a minute. The doc paid for itself on its first real-world hit.

Closes #3604

author: galkahana
body:
## Summary

`WriteStreamObject` allocates a `streamReader` (`IByteReader*`) early via `StartReadingFromStream` / `StartReadingFromStreamForPlainCopying`, then writes the stream's dictionary, then copies the stream body. The later error branches (`CopyToOutputStream` failure at line ~2104) correctly `delete streamReader` before returning. The earlier branch (dictionary-write failure at line ~2092) didn't — leaking the reader.

One-line fix: add `delete streamReader;` to the dictionary-write failure branch.

## Leak conditions

- One of the source-side stream open paths succeeded (`streamReader != NULL`).
- AND a `WriteKey` or `WriteObjectByType` call in the dictionary loop subsequently failed (e.g. nested stream-write error, output-stream error).

The `streamReader == NULL` → `status = eFailure` → enter-same-branch path is leak-free already because `delete` on `NULL` is a no-op, so the unconditional `delete streamReader` is safe regardless of which failure led here. It also mirrors the existing cleanup in the `CopyToOutputStream` branch.

Resource hygiene fix surfaced during the Phase 4.1 copy/merge audit. Not memory-safety, not security severity.

## 배경 — 사용자 재현 시나리오
"검은돌이 disconnect → 흰돌 화면 '🏆 71s 후 승리' 정상 표시 → **관전자 화면 새로고침** 시 turn timer 30 에서 멈춤 + 카운트다운 UI 안 보임"

## 원인
서버가 disconnect 발생 **그 순간만** `opponent_disconnected` (deadline 포함) broadcast — 그 후 들어온 클라이언트는 진행 중 grace 모름.

| msg | 옛 payload | deadline 정보 |
|---|---|---|
| `opponent_disconnected` | color, deadline, graceMs | ✓ (그 순간 한 번) |
| `game_start` | playerStatus | ✗ |
| `resume_success` (resume / join) | playerStatus | ✗ |
| `spectate_success` | playerStatus | ✗ |
| `room-runtime` 의 `disconnectTimers` | setTimeout handle 만 | ✗ deadline 보존 X |

## 변경

### server
- **`room-runtime.js`**: `disconnectTimers` entry 에 `{handle, deadline}` 둘 다 저장. `setDisconnectTimer(code, color, handle, deadline)` + `getDisconnectDeadlines(code)` helper
- **`disconnect.js` / `rehydrate.js`**: 호출 시 deadline 같이 전달
- **`send.js`**: `disconnectStatePayload(room) → { disconnectGraceMs, disconnectDeadlines? }` helper
- **4개 msg** (game.js / join.js / resume.js / spectator.js) 의 payload 에 `...disconnectStatePayload(room)` 추가

### client (`net.js`)
- `applyDisconnectInfo(msg)` helper — graceMs 저장 + 진행 중 deadline 있으면 `pauseTurnTimer(deadline)` 호출
- `onGameStart` / `onSpectateSuccess` / `onResumeSuccess` 끝에 호출

## 영향 범위 (모두 cover)
- ✓ 흰돌 새로고침 (상대 disconnect 진행 중)
- ✓ **신규 관전자 입장** ← 사용자 보고된 핵심 케이스
- ✓ 기존 관전자 새로고침
- ✓ 검은돌 본인 새로고침 (보통 자기 grace 는 cancel 되지만 edge case cover)
- ✓ 게임 시작 직후 한 쪽 이미 끊긴 case
- ✓ 서버 재시작 후 rehydrate — deadline = 그 시점 + GRACE_MS

## 검증
- omok `npm run test:unit` **140/140 통과**
- omok `npm test` (E2E) **79/79 통과** (recovery / reconnect / spectator 시나리오 그대로)

## Test plan (실 환경)
- [ ] 두 사용자 + 관전자 1명 → 한 쪽 disconnect
- [ ] 관전자 새로고침 → "🏆 90s 후 승리" 카운트다운 정상 표시
- [ ] 새 관전자가 같은 방 입장 → 같은 카운트다운 표시
- [ ] disconnect 된 사용자가 reconnect → 모든 화면 grace UI 사라짐
- [ ] 서버 재배포 (rehydrate) 직후 관전자 재입장 → 90s grace 카운트다운 시작

author: commandlinedesign
body:
## Summary

Ships features #2–#4 of the v0 roadmap ([.ai/roadmaps/v0-roadmap.md](.ai/roadmaps/v0-roadmap.md)) — the doorway, the stickiness contract, and the storage layer that every subsequent feature depends on.

- **config-loader** — `portweave.config.json` schema (zod-validated) + zero-config `--count N` anonymous mode. Public API: `loadConfig(cwd, opts?)`, `synthesizeAnonymousConfig(n)`. Resolves DESIGN.md §6.1 options (a) and (d).
- **worktree-context** — git worktree detection + namespace derivation matching boardflip's 8-char SHA1 hash format for migration parity. Honors `PORTWEAVE_NAMESPACE` and `PORTWEAVE_OFFSET` overrides. Produces the canonical `AllocationKey` that the registry and allocator (Feature #5) consume.
- **registry-storage** — `~/.config/portweave/registry.json` with directory-mutex locking (100×25ms retries, 30s stale-lock TTL), atomic temp+rename writes, prune-on-read for missing worktrees, and an 8-subprocess concurrent integration test using real `child_process.fork`. No `offset` field — Portweave is machine-wide pool, not per-project offset (decision-log row #4).

## Process

Each feature was specced (`/create-spec`), implemented in parallel via worktree-isolated `/execute-spec` subagents, then audited by parallel `/code-review` + `/security-review` subagents. Findings were remediated in a second wave of parallel subagents. All committed history reflects that flow — feature merges show the parallel execution structure; remediation merges show the polish wave. Review artifacts captured under [.ai/reviews/](.ai/reviews/) for audit.

## What changed since the Foundation PR

- 45 files changed, +4,344 / -10 lines
- 156 tests (covering 80%+ across statements / branches / functions / lines)
- 2 new decision-log rows (#19 PORTWEAVE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, #20 tempfile naming + cleanup)
- 6 PW error codes in use (PW0101/0102 config, PW0201/0202 worktree, PW0301/0302 registry)
- New runtime dep: `zod ^4.4.3` (for config validation)
- Dep bumps: `constants-check` ^0.1.0 → ^0.2.0

## Security posture

`/security-review` flagged two mediums; both addressed in this PR:
- Registry tempfiles + dir now created with `mode: 0o600` / `0o700` (was world-readable)
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` now validated as absolute path before use as `rm` target

Plus one low: `git.ts` now strips `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` in addition to the four boardflip-pattern git-passthrough vars.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run dev-workflow` — all 13 gates green locally
- [x] 156 tests pass (15 test files)
- [x] Coverage ≥80% on statements / branches / functions / lines
- [x] 8-subprocess concurrent registry test passes (no torn writes, 8 distinct entries)
- [x] Real-I/O tests against `os.tmpdir()` git repos (no `vi.mock('fs')` / `vi.mock('child_process')`)
- [ ] CI green on GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- [ ] Manual smoke test: `portweave run` and `portweave show` — **deferred to Feature #7 (run-command), which lands the CLI surface; this PR ships the library primitives those commands will consume.**

## Reviewer guide

Suggested reading order:
1. [.ai/specs/result-types/result-types.md](.ai/specs/result-types/result-types.md) (foundation context — already on main)
2. [.ai/specs/config-loader/config-loader.md](.ai/specs/config-loader/config-loader.md)
3. [.ai/specs/worktree-context/worktree-context.md](.ai/specs/worktree-context/worktree-context.md)
4. [.ai/specs/registry-storage/registry-storage.md](.ai/specs/registry-storage/registry-storage.md)
5. The corresponding `src/{config,worktree,registry}/` directories
6. The three [.ai/reviews/*.code-review.md](.ai/reviews/) reports if you want to see what the audit pass surfaced

Merge strategy: **"Create a merge commit"** preserves the feature-merge structure showing parallel execution. "Squash and merge" would flatten this to one commit on main — also acceptable if a clean linear main history is preferred.

## Summary

- Adds `-o dot` / `--output dot` to `dlin column upstream` and `dlin column downstream`
- Emits Graphviz DOT format: each dbt model becomes a `subgraph cluster`, each column becomes a node
- Nodes are color-coded by transformation type:
  - `direct` → `#AED6F1` (blue)
  - `aggregation` → `#FAD7A0` (orange)
  - `expression` → `#A9DFBF` (green)
  - `cast` → `#D7BDE2` (purple)
  - `conditional` → `#F9E79F` (yellow)
  - `unknown` / source-only → `#D5D8DC` (gray)
- Stable node IDs (numeric index-based) prevent collisions between model names that differ only in dot vs underscore (e.g. `raw.orders` vs `raw_orders`)
- Duplicate edges are deduplicated

## Usage

```sh
# Upstream column lineage as DOT
dlin column upstream orders -o dot | dot -Tsvg > lineage.svg

# Downstream impact as DOT
dlin column downstream stg_orders --column order_id -o dot
```

body:
## Summary
- Spec doc §3 of ``docs/plans/2026-05-24-transcript-standardization-and-claude-resume.md`` (PR2 plan, already on develop).
- V.1 `AdapterCallRequest.resume_session_id` + `AdapterCallResult.session_id`. V.2 `build_claude_cli_argv(resume_session_id=...)` + `extract_session_id_from_events`. V.3 ClaudeCliAdapter wires both. V.4 AgenticLoop reads/writes `<run_dir>/sub_agents/<task_id>/session.json`.
- paperclip `agent_runtime_state.sessionId` + `--resume` parity → 5-10K tokens saved per turn (paperclip `execute.ts:680`).

## Why
Pre-PR-V every claude-cli call started a fresh backend session and re-sent the full system prompt. Single-OAuth seed-generation cycles burnt through the 5-hour quota in minutes because the same system prompt re-flooded the input window for every sub-agent turn. paperclip's heartbeat path solves this with `--resume <session_id>` — claude-cli reuses the cached system prompt + prior conversation context, dropping input billing to the cached-marker tier (5-10K tokens saved per turn).

PR-V threads the prior session_id end-to-end: AgenticLoop reads `session.json` before the call → `AdapterCallRequest.resume_session_id` → `--resume <id>` argv → claude-cli emits `system.init` with the (potentially new) session_id → `AdapterCallResult.session_id` → AgenticLoop persists to `session.json` for the next turn. PR-Q's `resolve_sub_agent_path` provides the per-task anchor.

## Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| ``core/llm/adapters/base.py`` (V.1) | `AdapterCallRequest.resume_session_id: str = ""` + `AdapterCallResult.session_id: str = ""` fields (backwards-compat default empty). |
| ``plugins/petri_audit/claude_cli_provider.py`` (V.2) | `build_claude_cli_argv(resume_session_id=...)` prepends `--resume <id>` before `--model`. New `extract_session_id_from_events()` walks the `system.init` event. |
| ``core/llm/adapters/claude_cli.py`` (V.3) | `acomplete` threads `req.resume_session_id` into the argv builder + surfaces emitted session_id on `result.session_id`. |
| ``core/agent/loop/agent_loop.py`` (V.4) | New `_load_prior_session_id` + `_persist_session_id` helpers around `<run_dir>/sub_agents/<task_id>/session.json`. `_call_llm` reads before adapter call, writes after. |
| ``core/llm/adapters/translation.py`` | `build_adapter_request` accepts + threads `resume_session_id` kwarg. |
| ``tests/core/llm/adapters/test_claude_cli_resume.py`` (NEW) | 11 tests pin V.1/V.2/V.4 contract + persistence + no-op semantics. |
| ``CHANGELOG.md`` | Unreleased entry. |

body:
### Motivation
- Compiled-flow emission produced invalid Go for `switch`-style flow expressions causing `unexpected keyword return` build errors.
- Builtins used inside flows (e.g. `Abs`) were not discovered by the import scanner, causing `undefined: math` errors in generated code.
- Enum-variant usage in flow expressions could be lowered/emitted as `f.<Name>` instead of an enum literal, producing `f.ShadowOutcome undefined` scoping failures.

### Description
- Fix `MIRFlowSwitchExpr` codegen so the emitted Go keeps the `if / else if` chain contiguous and inserts a statement separator before a final fallback `return`, producing valid Go (multi-line body emission instead of fragile single-line joins).
- Add recursive flow builtin collection (`collectFlowBuiltins*`) and call it from `emitGo` so builtins referenced inside flow statements/expressions mark `usedBuiltins` and trigger correct imports (e.g. `math`).
- Add `lowerFlowEnumVariantExpr` and update flow `FieldAccessExpr` lowering and type inference to recognize enum variant constructors in expression contexts and lower them to proper enum literals instead of flow fields, preserving local vs. board/field scoping.
- Add a focused compiled regression fixture `Language/ControlFlow/OctomataFlowMatchExpr/valid/flow_match_local_subject_abs_switch_compiled.octest` that exercises a local `match` subject, `Abs(...)`, and a `switch` with `else` fallback to guard against regressions.

### Testing
- Ran `go run ./cmd/oct test Experiments/PrometheusShadowAuthorityRakeLab/M1 --suite Experiments.PrometheusShadowAuthorityRakeLab.M1.FlowSmoke --execution compiled` and it passed (7/7 compiled tests).
- Verified with `OCT_KEEP_GEN=1` compiled run and `--execution auto`/default execution; all FlowSmoke permutations passed.
- Ran artifact generation `go run ./cmd/oct artifact Experiments/PrometheusShadowAuthorityRakeLab/M1` and validated `Experiments/PrometheusShadowAuthorityRakeLab/M1/scenario_summary.json` (scenario count 10).

author: zaid-marji
body:
## Summary

The bundled web vault (`v2026.4.1` per `docker/DockerSettings.yaml`) refuses
the playwright suite's interactions for several compounding reasons: stale
label selectors, stale org-nav selectors, a renamed invitation-acceptance
toast, an SSO existing-account flow that no longer auto-redirects to the
IdP, and the web vault refusing plain HTTP. `login.spec.ts` and every spec
calling `createAccount` / `logUser` / `activateTOTP` / `orgs.*` /
`*.smtp.spec.ts` org-invite flows fails before doing anything useful. This
PR restores the suite to green against the current bundled vault, and along
the way centralises the selectors and 2FA-challenge flow so the next
web-vault bump has one place to update.

Eight commits, each with a single concern (commit bodies have the full
motivation):

- **`fix stale Master password selectors`** — the input lost its
  `(required)` suffix. Switch to `getByLabel('Master password')` and anchor
  the ambiguous new/confirm fields by `formcontrolname`.
- **`fix TOTP setup flow`** — Continue race with Angular `updateOn: 'blur'`
  (submit via `Enter`), Key selector ambiguous with Yubico SVG aria-label
  (anchor `{ exact: true }`), Close button transiently disabled during the
  success-dialog transition (drop the click; dialog auto-closes).
- **`serve the test Vaultwarden over HTTPS`** — the web vault refuses
  registration over HTTP. Self-signed cert generated in the test image,
  `ROCKET_TLS` pointed at it, `DOMAIN` switched to `https://`,
  `ignoreHTTPSErrors: true` set on every playwright context.
- **`gitignore: catch stray playwright artifacts at the repo root`** —
  adds `test-results/` and `playwright-report/` to root `.gitignore`.
- **`fix stale org-nav selectors`** — product-switch nav links and the
  in-org "Members" entry are icon-only; switch to
  `getByRole('link', { name: '…' })` and force-click past the hover
  tooltip that intercepts the click.
- **`fix invitation-accepted toast text + SSO existing-account redirect`**
  — toast is now `"Successfully accepted your invitation"`; the SSO
  invited-with-existing-account flow no longer auto-redirects to Keycloak
  (explicit "Use single sign-on" click required).
- **`centralize web-vault selectors into shared setup helpers`** — extracts
  the avatar menu, registration MP-fill, user-verification gate, and the
  TOTP/email enrol+disable flow into shared helpers in `setups/`. Future
  web-vault selector changes only have to be updated in one place.
- **`centralize 2FA challenge handling`** — `submitTwoFactor(test, page,
  twoFactor)` with a `TwoFactor` discriminated union (`totp` / `mail2fa` /
  `fido2`) drives the `/#/2fa` page from `setups/2fa.ts`. Both `logUser`
  variants (MP and SSO) gain a `twoFactor?: TwoFactor` option that delegates
  to it; the four inline 2FA submission blocks across `login.spec.ts`,
  `login.smtp.spec.ts`, `sso_login.spec.ts`, and `sso_login.smtp.spec.ts`
  collapse to one line each.

## Test plan

Verified against bundled web-vault `v2026.4.1` over the full
parallel-projects docker suite (sqlite + mariadb + mysql + postgres + four
SSO variants, **140 tests**, **129 pass**). Every previously-broken
master-password / TOTP / org-nav / invite-toast / HTTPS path now passes on
every DB backend.

The remaining failures are unrelated to this branch's scope: PBKDF2-key-
derivation timing flakes under the saturated parallel-projects suite (the
same tests pass on sibling DB projects under identical code).

## Summary

- B14 saga (anima `dancinlab/anima` PR #410, `coffeshop_fire_sanity_hook.hexa` Phase 2 impl) 중 발견된 hexa compiler bug 보고.
- bare `return void;` 가 일부 context 에서 `return type_of(p)` 로 mistranslate → undeclared identifier 에러.
- agent workaround: `return []` sentinel + caller-side `type_of(x) != "map"` gate (type ambiguity 잔존).

## Finding

- 정확 trigger syntactic context 미식별 (agent 가 minimal repro 안 만들고 sentinel 로 진행).
- 의심 trigger: `map` / `record` return-type fn 내 `if invalid(x) { return void; }` early-exit pattern.

## Suggested fix (3 options)

- A: parser/typer 가 `void` 를 정식 literal 로 처리.
- B: bare `return;` syntax 대안 (C / Rust convention).
- C: sentinel pattern 의 type-safety 가이드 / nominal `fail_map()` helper.

## Cross-refs

- anima PR #410 (B14 cycle).
- prior 6 inbox patches (runpod-graphql / cloud-pod-status / dispatcher-bootstrap / cloud-guard-ux / copy-from-verify / list-concat-o-n2).

## C3

trigger context 미식별 · compiler version 미명시 · workaround type-safety 영향 미평가 · parser vs typer vs lower stage 미분리 · 다른 expression position (assign RHS / fn arg / record field) 동작 미점검.

author: mgwitham
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to push the profile page past Perf 80. Diagnosed the live profile: **FCP 2.6s but LCP 4.5s** — a ~1.9s render delay where the hydration render competes with heavy third-party JS in flight. The profile's own code is modest (~57KB); the weight is monitoring/analytics.

Analytics (GA, PostHog) are already deferred to `requestIdleCallback`. **Sentry was not** — `sentry-init.js` fired `import("@sentry/browser")` (~60KB) immediately, and it's the *first* import in `therapist-page.js`, so the Sentry chunk loaded on the render's critical path. This wraps that import in `requestIdleCallback` (with a `setTimeout` fallback) so it initializes after first render.

- Safe: error monitoring is best-effort (the file's own comment says so); the brief uninstrumented startup window is an acceptable trade.
- Broad: helps every page that loads Sentry, the profile most.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` — Sentry stays a separate lazy chunk, now idle-triggered
- [x] `npm test` 785 pass · lint 0 errors · format clean
- [ ] **Real measure is prod**: local lhci serves JS from localhost (instant), so it can't show a throttled-network critical-path win. I'll confirm the LCP/Perf delta on the live profile after this deploys.

## Bigger remaining lever (your call, not shipped here)
The heaviest third-party JS on the profile is **PostHog session recording (~54KB) + surveys (~34KB)** and **GA gtag (157KB)**. PostHog session-replay/surveys on profile pages is ~90KB — disabling those (PostHog config) would be a real win, but it's a measurement/product decision (do you use session replay or surveys?), so I left it to you.

author: orkhanibrahim
body:
## Summary

First slice of **Epic 5 — Super Admin: Dashboard & Statistics**. Ships the two MVP-starred stories (5.1 + 5.2). The non-MVP stories (5.3 live activity, 5.4 period statistics, 5.5 top/bottom performers, 5.6 stats CSV export, 5.7 time-series chart endpoints) follow in later PRs.

\`\`\`
GET /super-admin/dashboard
→ {
    "stats": {
      "totalRestaurants":       42,
      "activeRestaurants":      37,
      "totalBranches":          89,
      "totalAdmins":            60,
      "totalReservations":   12500,
      "reservationsThisMonth": 823
    },
    "recentRestaurants": [ RestaurantSummary x10 ]
  }
\`\`\`

## Design notes

- **Combined response intentionally** — the SPA's first paint needs both halves; one round trip beats two. Independent refresh of either section is fine on the future endpoints (5.3+).
- **Six counts are single \`SELECT COUNT\` queries** on already-indexed columns. \`countByStatus\` hits the brand status index, \`countByReservationDateGreaterThanEqual\` hits the existing \`reservation_date\` indices. Dashboard hit is cheap.
- **\`totalAdmins\` excludes SUPER_ADMIN** — those are a deployment fact, not a platform-health signal. Same hide-rule as the rest of Epic 4.
- **\`reservationsThisMonth\` uses the injected \`Clock\`** so the month cut is testable and stays stable. Prod JVMs run as UTC.
- **\`recentRestaurants\` delegates to \`RestaurantService.list\`** with \`PageRequest.of(0, 10, Sort.by(createdAt).descending())\`. Reuses the Epic 3 \`RestaurantSummary\` projection so the SPA gets the same shape across the dashboard and the full list endpoint — any future change to the summary picks up automatically.

## Repository additions (additive)

- \`BrandRepository.countByStatus(BrandStatus)\`
- \`UserRepository.countByRoleNot(Role)\`
- \`ReservationRepository.countByReservationDateGreaterThanEqual(LocalDate)\`

## Test plan

- [x] \`./gradlew spotlessCheck checkstyleMain checkstyleTest test :app:bootJar\` — green locally
- [x] \`DashboardServiceTest\` (3 cases):
  - all six counts collected correctly + recent list returned verbatim
  - recent-list \`Pageable\` is page 0, size 10, sorted \`createdAt DESC\` (captured via \`ArgumentCaptor\`)
  - \"reservations this month\" uses the injected \`Clock\` (mid-month NOW = 2026-05-15 → expects 2026-05-01 as the threshold, not wall-clock)
- [ ] Integration test for the full flow — deferred to Story 18.2
- [ ] Manual smoke against a local stack

author: copilot
body:
The sample GUI layer had started to drift toward a timer-driven refresh loop. This change keeps the UI native to Meshtastic stack activity: state is modeled locally in the sample, and rendering happens in direct response to stack events rather than a sample-defined refresh cadence.

- **Event-driven GUI flow**
  - remove the sample-local refresh interval config
  - change `meshtastic_sample_gui_process()` back to passive waiting
  - keep GUI updates rooted in `meshtastic_sample_gui_handle_event()` so rendering happens on stack events only

- **Sample-local UI state**
  - expand the GUI model beyond scaffolding to hold:
    - current `meshtastic_status`
    - last significant stack event
    - last received text message metadata/payload
  - keep Meshtastic event translation out of `main.c`

- **Renderer boundary**
  - replace the no-op renderer with a real backend split
  - support an LVGL-backed renderer when available
  - preserve a structured log fallback without changing the model boundary

- **Configuration and docs**
  - keep GUI enablement sample-local
  - document that the GUI reacts to native stack events instead of polling

```c
int meshtastic_sample_gui_process(k_timeout_t timeout)
{
	k_sleep(timeout);

	return 0;
}

void meshtastic_sample_gui_handle_event(const struct meshtastic_event *event)
{
	/* update sample-local model from Meshtastic event */
	(void)meshtastic_sample_gui_model_refresh_status(&gui_model);
	(void)meshtastic_sample_gui_renderer_process(&gui_model);
}
```

🎯 **Why**:
- Using `.filter()` and `.find()` nested inside `.map()` effectively causes an $O(n^2)$ lookup complexity, which can severely bottleneck render performance as event and contact data scales.

📊 **Impact**:
- Reduces event-processing complexity from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$, drastically cutting down component re-render calculation time for power users.

🔬 **Measurement**:
- Run `npm run test` and `npm run lint` successfully. Verified that UI functions exactly as it previously did.

body: ## Bug and impact Agents could reject or defer the new location tracking consent state, but `/locations/agent/me` still accepted and persisted their coordinates. Clients could then retrieve those coordinates for active orders, making the consent state ineffective. Direct Hasura writes to `agent_locations` also bypassed the REST flow. ## Root cause The recent consent endpoints stored `agents.location_tracking_consent` but the existing location ingestion path and Hasura `agent_locations` permissions did not check it. The agent role was also allowed to update `location_tracking_consent` directly, bypassing the REST transition rules. ## Fix - Require `accepted_fg` or `accepted_bg` before the backend upserts an agent location. - Add the same accepted-consent condition to Hasura `agent_locations` insert/update permissions. - Remove direct agent-role updates to `agents.location_tracking_consent` so transitions go through the backend endpoint. - Remove the new consent field from the core user relation query and load it through a resilient enrichment path to avoid unrelated authenticated endpoint failures during migration/metadata rollout. - Add a focused controller spec for accepted and rejected consent behavior. ## Validation - `npx nx test backend --testFile=apps/backend/src/locations/locations.controller.spec.ts --runInBand` - `npx nx build backend`
