body:
## Summary
EHG_Engineer side of **ADR-STAGE0-INTAKE-001** (Stage 0 Opportunity-Intake Canonicalization). Paired with ehg PR rickfelix/ehg#639 (F1/F2/F3 UI). No runtime cross-dependency; merge order is irrelevant.

### F4 — Stage 0 request status desync (RCA-driven)
**Root cause** (`sub_agent_execution_results` `2e7c5c9d`): a stale-claim re-execution re-ran a request whose venture was already created. `persistVentureBrief` re-inserted the same active venture name → tripped the partial unique index `idx_ventures_unique_active_name` (SQLSTATE `23505`) → threw → the request was recorded `failed` **despite genuinely succeeding** (Canvas AI; brief + venture both exist).

**Fix** (`lib/eva/stage-zero/chairman-review.js`, +22 LOC): on a `23505` duplicate-active-name collision, look up and **return the existing active venture** instead of throwing — the re-run completes idempotently and the processor records `completed`. A genuine synthesis failure throws *upstream* (before the insert), so it's still recorded `failed` with **no orphan** venture/brief. The lookup-by-name is correct here because the collision means a same-named active venture exists at that moment.

### FR-005 — cross-repo contract (gap G5)
`docs/architecture/stage-zero-requests-contract.md` documents the `stage_zero_requests` producer (`ehg` `useRequestStageZero`) → consumer (this repo's `stage-zero-queue-processor.js`) contract: columns, status lifecycle, the four `metadata.path` values. Referenced from the now-committed `ADR-STAGE0-INTAKE-001`.

## Tests
- `chairman-review.test.js`: **10/10 green**. +3 guard tests (23505→returns existing; 23505+no-existing→throws; non-23505→throws without lookup) and fixed a pre-existing stale mock (`.limit`/`.maybeSingle`) that had 2 reds on `main`.

## Scope notes
- Production code delta is **+22 LOC**; remainder is docs (ADR 183 + contract 77) and tests (104).
- **Deferred (systemic follow-on SD):** durable `venture_briefs.stage_zero_request_id` FK + request-id idempotency in `checkForDuplicate` + a `releaseStaleClaims` reconcile step. #1 alone (this PR) already resolves the desync; the FK is needed to do the reconcile *robustly* (names can change post-creation).
- The single known bad row (`eb698149`) was reconciled to `completed` via a verify-first one-off.

## Related Links

- specs/WPT tests:

## [Required] Overview

WPT test fixture files (URL and URLPattern test data) were previously committed directly to the repository as static copies. This made it hard to track which version of wpt the fixtures came from, and required a manual copy step whenever upstream test data changed.

This PR replaces the committed copies with a sparse-checkout git submodule pointing to the canonical [web-platform-tests/wpt](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) repository. Only the two subdirectories used for test data are materialized — the rest of the wpt tree (which is several gigabytes) is never downloaded.

The CI test job is updated to initialize the submodule using a partial-clone strategy (`--filter=blob:none --no-checkout`) followed by sparse-checkout configuration, so only the required blobs are fetched on each CI run.

A `justfile` with a `setup` recipe is added so contributors have a single command to run after cloning. `CONTRIBUTING.md` is updated accordingly.

## Scope of Change

- [x] Tooling / CI
- [x] Documentation

## Breaking Changes

- [x] No breaking changes

No public API surface changes. `.mbti` files are unaffected.

Contributors will need [just](https://just.systems/) installed and should run `just setup` instead of `moon update` after cloning — this is documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Deferred Items and TODOs

- **`gen-*` justfile recipes** — `just gen-idna` and `just gen-combining-mark` recipes for regenerating IDNA/combining-mark tables from Unicode data are deferred to a follow-up PR to keep this change focused on the submodule migration.

## 概要

`install.sh` の `--force` オプションが consumer 固有の `CLAUDE.md` を汎用 template で
silent 上書きしてしまう問題を修正した。

consumer repo は自プロジェクト向けにカスタマイズした `CLAUDE.md` を持つことが前提であり、

コードパスで上書きされていた。

本 PR では `--force` の CLAUDE.md 挙動を「live 据え置き + 差分時 `.org` 並置（= フラグ無しと同一）」
に固定し、template 上書きを望む場合にのみ使う専用フラグ `--force-claude-md` を導入した。

## 対応 Issue

Closes #208

## 関連 PR

- 設計 PR: なし（中〜小規模 Issue のため Architect フェーズなし）

## 変更内容

- **`--force` 単体での CLAUDE.md 上書きを廃止**
  - `copy_claude_md_with_org` の OVERWRITE 分岐条件を `FORCE` → `FORCE_CLAUDE_MD` 駆動に変更
  - `backup_claude_md_once` の発火条件も `FORCE` → `FORCE_CLAUDE_MD` に変更
  - `--force` 単体では `.bak` 退避せず、CLAUDE.md は据え置き + 差分時 `.org` 並置（フラグ無しと同一挙動）
- **新フラグ `--force-claude-md` を導入**
  - 指定時のみ CLAUDE.md を `.bak` once-only 退避 + template 上書き（旧 `--force` の CLAUDE.md 挙動を移設）
  - `--force --force-claude-md` 併用で「agents/rules も CLAUDE.md も上書き」が成立
- **`--force` の agents/rules 挙動を完全維持**
  - `copy_with_hybrid_overwrite` は `FORCE` 参照のまま変更なし → consumer の stale 同期手段として機能
- **ドキュメント / help 整備**
  - `install.sh` ヘッダコメント: `--force` の CLAUDE.md 記述を「agents/rules のみ」に修正、`--force-claude-md` 説明を追加
  - `--help` の出力範囲を拡張し `--force-claude-md` を含める（`sed -n '3,28p'`）
  - merge ガイド（`CLAUDE_MD_ORG_HINT`）: 上書き手段の案内を `--force-claude-md` に変更、`--force` 単体は agents/rules のみという注記を追記
  - `README.md`: migration note 付きで `--force` / `--force-claude-md` の違いを説明する blockquote 追加、フラグ表・使いどころ節を更新

## Breaking Change / Migration note

> **`--force` 単体では CLAUDE.md が更新されなくなりました（#208）**
>
> 旧動作: `./install.sh --repo <path> --force` → CLAUDE.md を `.bak` 退避 + template 上書き
>
> 新動作: `./install.sh --repo <path> --force` → CLAUDE.md は据え置き（フラグ無しと同一）、agents/rules のみ上書き
>
> **CLAUDE.md を template で上書きしたい場合は `--force-claude-md` を使ってください:**
> ```
> ./install.sh --repo <path> --force-claude-md          # CLAUDE.md のみ上書き
> ./install.sh --repo <path> --force --force-claude-md  # agents/rules + CLAUDE.md を両方上書き
> ```

## Test plan

Reviewer 独立スモークテスト（Test A〜M）および Developer スモークテスト（S1〜S6）で検証済み。
以下は主要シナリオのサマリ:

- **`--force` で CLAUDE.md 据え置き + `.org` 並置**: SKIP ログ確認、`CLAUDE.md.bak` 不作成を確認（Req 1.1/1.2/1.5）
- **`--force` で agents/rules 上書き**: `developer.md` が BACKUP + OVERWRITE、CLAUDE.md は引き続き据え置き（Req 3.1/3.2）
- **`--force-claude-md` で CLAUDE.md 上書き**: `.bak` = consumer 内容、本体 = template 一致（Req 2.1）
- **`--force --force-claude-md` 併用**: CLAUDE.md も agents/rules も OVERWRITE（Req 2.5）
- **dry-run 整合**: `--dry-run --force` は CLAUDE.md SKIP + `.org` NEW 分類、FS 変更ゼロ（Req 5.1/5.4）
- **dry-run `--force-claude-md`**: CLAUDE.md BACKUP + OVERWRITE 分類、FS 変更ゼロ（Req 5.3/5.4）
- **冪等性**: 再実行で `.bak` once-only 温存、CLAUDE.md SKIP（Req 4.1/4.2）
- **通常経路同一**: フラグ無しで CLAUDE.md 据え置き + `.org` 並置（NFR 1.4）
- **`shellcheck install.sh` 警告ゼロ**（Reviewer 独立検証済み）

1. **env var override（`FORCE_CLAUDE_MD=true`）は未提供**: requirements.md Open Question 2 で
   Architect 判断事項とされていたが、既存 `--force` も env override を持たない慣習に揃えてフラグのみで提供した。
   env override が必要な場合は別 Issue での対応を想定。
2. **`--force-claude-md` フラグ名の確定**: requirements.md で候補として挙がったフラグ名を採用したが、

author: sentinel-web
body:
Closes #228.

## Finding

The audit (finding #6) said the ORBAT chart had "no scroll container." On inspection it **already wraps the tree in an overflow container**, and verification at mobile widths showed **no clipping and no page-level horizontal scrollbar** (`docHorizOverflow: 0`). `react-organizational-chart` shrink-to-fits, so with realistic data the tree fits the viewport; a larger hierarchy would overflow into — and scroll within — that container.

Per discussion on the issue, scope here is the **minimal polish**, not a node min-width rework.

## Change

- **`Orbat.tsx`** — wrapper `overflow: auto` → `overflowX: 'auto'`: makes the intent explicit (a wide tree pans horizontally within the card) and guards against a nested vertical scrollbar if the wrapper's height is ever constrained. Vertical growth flows into the page's content scroll.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors
- `npm test` (mocha) — 364 passing
- `npm run e2e` — 106 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed
- Manual: ORBAT at 360/375px renders fully, no clipping, no page-level horizontal scrollbar.

## Note

The deeper "large org squishes nodes instead of scrolling at a readable size" concern (shrink-to-fit has no min node width) is left as-is by design — flagged for a potential future follow-up if needed.

body:
## Resumen del cambio

Corrige 5 bugs del dashboard frontend del panel de tesis. Todos los issues fueron verificados con TypeScript (tsc exit 0) y validación manual de flujos.

### Bugs corregidos

1. **`irrigation-chart-y-scale`** — La vista "sumatoria" y "apilado" mostraba valores de humedad en 0 con saltos extraños. El eje Y estaba en escala 0–4 en vez de 0–100%. Corregido forzando `suggestedMax: 100` en la configuración de Chart.js para todos los modos de visualización.

2. **`irrigation-chart-sensor-gaps`** — Los gráficos multi-sensor no manejaban correctamente los períodos sin lectura, generando líneas que unían puntos no contiguos. Corregido introduciendo manejo de gaps explícitos con `spanGaps: false` y puntos `null` en el dataset.

3. **`notifications-display-and-read`** — Las notificaciones almacenadas en Supabase no se mostraban en la UI. Faltaba integración completa del componente de notificaciones con el hook de datos. Corregido conectando el panel de notificaciones al hook `useNotifications` y el botón "marcar como leído" al endpoint RPC correspondiente.

4. **`realtime-connection-state`** — El indicador de conexión realtime aparecía siempre como "desconectado". El estado se calculaba incorrectamente: no se consideraba el canal de Supabase Realtime como fuente de verdad. Corregido usando el estado del canal (`SUBSCRIBED` → conectado) para derivar el badge de conexión.

5. **`system-health-overall`** — El estado de "salud general" del sistema mostraba "parcial" incluso con todos los sensores OK. La lógica derivaba el estado desde campos opcionales ausentes. Corregido ajustando la función de cálculo para manejar correctamente los campos `null`/`undefined` y retornar `healthy` cuando corresponde.

author: kauanpassos
body:
## 📋 Descrição

Este PR implementa e consolida o fluxo completo de autenticação da aplicação mobile.

A autenticação foi estruturada para ocorrer diretamente no Firebase Auth pelo cliente MAUI, enquanto a API ASP.NET Core permanece responsável pela autorização dos endpoints protegidos via Bearer Token.

Além do login, o fluxo também contempla persistência segura da sessão, restauração automática após reinicialização do aplicativo e envio automático do token JWT nas requisições protegidas da API.

---

## 🛠️ O que foi feito?

* **Login via Firebase Auth:** integração do `FirebaseAuthClient` no MAUI para autenticação utilizando e-mail e senha diretamente no Firebase.
* **Persistência segura da sessão:** armazenamento do `idToken` do Firebase utilizando `SecureStorage`.
* **Restauração de sessão:** implementação do `VerificarSessaoAtivaAsync()` com leitura e parsing local do JWT salvo no dispositivo, mantendo a sessão ativa após fechar e abrir o app novamente.
* **Mapeamento de roles:** leitura da claim `"role"` do payload do JWT e conversão para o enum `TipoUsuario`.
* **Navegação baseada em perfil:** ajuste na `LoginViewModel` para redirecionamento automático conforme o tipo do usuário autenticado:

  * `Almoxarife` → `GestaoFilaPage`
  * `Colaborador` → `HomeColaboradorPage`
  * demais cenários → `EstoquePage`
* **Interceptor HTTP autenticado:** implementação do `AuthenticatedHttpHandler` para incluir automaticamente o cabeçalho:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

em todas as chamadas protegidas.

* **Configuração do HttpClient no MAUI:** encadeamento do `DelegatingHandler` com bypass de certificado SSL local em ambiente de desenvolvimento.
* **Logout:** limpeza do token salvo localmente e encerramento da sessão do Firebase.

---

## 🧪 Como testar?

1. Iniciar a API ASP.NET Core localmente.
2. Executar o app MAUI (Windows ou Emulador Android).
3. Realizar login com um usuário já existente no Firebase.
4. Validar se o app redireciona corretamente conforme a role do usuário.
5. Fechar completamente o aplicativo.
6. Abrir novamente e validar se a sessão permanece ativa sem exigir novo login.
7. Executar qualquer ação que consuma endpoint protegido e validar se o token Bearer está sendo enviado automaticamente.
8. Executar logout e validar se:

   * token foi removido do `SecureStorage`
   * sessão do Firebase foi encerrada
   * usuário volta para tela de login

---

## 🏁 Checklist de homologação

* [x] Login realizado diretamente via Firebase Auth
* [x] Token persistido com `SecureStorage`
* [x] Sessão restaurada após reinicialização do app
* [x] Claim `role` extraída do JWT
* [x] Conversão da role para `TipoUsuario`
* [x] Navegação baseada no perfil do usuário
* [x] Bearer Token enviado automaticamente em chamadas protegidas
* [x] Logout removendo token local e encerrando sessão do Firebase

---

author: sirily
body:
## Goal

Fix production Cashier PWA sync for real Beancount ledgers that use Python plugins, without changing the PWA code or the existing API response shape.

Production PWA currently calls the existing read-only endpoint:

```text
GET /infrastructure?file_path=main.bean
```

and then recursively downloads includes/globs. That works for plain ledgers, but production `main.bean` contains Python `plugin` directives. The browser/WASM offline parser cannot execute those plugins and reports errors such as:

```text
Python plugin "..." requires python-plugin-wasm feature
```

The correct fix is not to strip/ignore plugin directives in the PWA. The server already runs in the Python Beancount environment and can load the ledger with plugins applied.

## Proposed behavior

Keep the existing endpoint and JSON shape:

```json
{ "content": "..." }
```

Change only the content returned when the requested infrastructure file is the configured root book (`BEANCOUNT_FILE`, e.g. `/workspace/main.bean` requested as `main.bean`):

1. Load `BEANCOUNT_FILE` with Beancount on the server so Python plugins run normally.
2. Materialize the resulting entries into Beancount text.
3. Return that materialized single-file ledger as `{ "content": "..." }`.
4. Do not include raw `plugin` or `include` directives in that root response.
5. Preserve existing raw behavior for all non-root paths and glob requests.

This keeps Stage 1 read-only and avoids PWA changes:

```text
PWA -> /api/infrastructure?file_path=main.bean -> materialized content
PWA saves main.bean to OPFS
PWA offline parser parses a plugin-free, include-free snapshot
```

## Non-goals

- No `POST /xact`.
- No write-back to the Beancount workspace.
- No client-side commenting/removal of `plugin` directives.
- No new API route unless implementation proves the old endpoint cannot safely preserve compatibility.

## Validation plan

- Add server tests proving root `main.bean` returns a materialized snapshot through the existing `/infrastructure` shape.
- Add tests proving non-root infrastructure files and glob responses keep the old raw behavior.
- Run `uv run pytest`.
- After merge/deploy, validate through the production PWA UI sync flow.

author: dukewood
body:
## Summary

The published v1.0 catalogue advertised **36 skills / 9 personas**. The actual count on `main` is **37 skills / 10 personas**. This PR closes the off-by-one drift with 11 single-character edits across 5 files.

## Why this drifted

The PRD `docs/23` §4 used "36-skill catalogue" as planning vocabulary — it numbered slots 1-38 with placeholders for skills that might merge during build (e.g. `/cost-estimate-detailed` "may merge with #15"). At ship time, all planned skills built independently *and* a 10th persona (Meta Utility — `/learn`, `/audit-log`, `/vstack-upgrade`) was added in v1.0 for toolkit ergonomics. The published READMEs + CHANGELOG headline lines kept the original "36 / 9" framing.

## Actual counts (verified on main)

- **37 EN `SKILL.md` files** in `skills/` (`git ls-tree -r main | grep -E "^skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$" | wc -l` = 37)
- **37 zh-CN parallel files** in `skills/i18n/zh-CN/`
- **10 personas**: Trip Planner (5) + Document Engineer (7) + Accountant (4) + Minor Specialist (5) + Sponsor Specialist (1) + Forms Specialist (3) + Appointment Coordinator (4) + Application Auditor (2) + Recovery Advisor (3) + Meta Utility (3) = 37

## Edits (11 total, 5 files)

| File | Edits | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 1 | Status block: "the full 36-skill catalogue" → "37-skill" |
| `README.zh-CN.md` | 1 | Status block: 完整的 36 → 完整的 37 |
| `skills/README.md` | 3 | Headline count, H2 heading, v1.x roadmap intro |
| `skills/README.zh-CN.md` | 3 | Mirrors EN |
| `skills/CHANGELOG.md` | 3 | v1.0.0 entry headline (36→37 + "9 personas"→"10 personas"); persona summary table footer total (36→37) |

## What was deliberately NOT changed

- **`skills/CHANGELOG.md:181`** — "16 more skills filling the 36-skill catalog" lives inside the v0.3.0 release entry as a forward-looking statement *at that time*. Rewriting historical CHANGELOG entries falsifies the per-release record. The "36" was the planning target at v0.3.0; the reality at v1.0.0 turned out to be 37, and the v1.0.0 entry now reflects that.
- **`skills/README.md:7` ("team of nine specialists") + `:9` (descriptive paragraph) + `skills/README.zh-CN.md:9` (九位虚拟专家)** — these intentionally describe only the **9 visa-domain personas**. Meta Utility is "toolkit ergonomics" and is introduced separately in its own dedicated section with a different framing ("these aren't visa-domain content — they manage your experience with the toolkit itself"). The "nine specialists" cold-open is a deliberate framing choice, not a count error.

## No regressions

- **No anchor links broken.** Grep confirmed no TOC entries or cross-references point to `#36-skills` / `#36-个技能` anchors. Renaming the H2 headings is safe.
- **No code or skill content changed.** Only `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `skills/README.md`, `skills/README.zh-CN.md`, `skills/CHANGELOG.md` touched.
- **No install / upgrade flow affected.** The install one-liner (`curl … install.sh | sh`) is unchanged.

## Diff scope

**5 files changed · +10 lines · -10 lines** (the 11th edit changes both "36" and "9 personas" in the same line, hence 10+/-10 not 11+/-11).

## Test plan

- [x] Skill count audit: `git ls-tree -r main | grep -E "^skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$" | wc -l` = 37
- [x] zh-CN parallel count: same = 37
- [x] Persona table in `skills/CHANGELOG.md` v1.0.0 entry sums to 37 (matches the file count)
- [x] No remaining "36 skills" / "36-skill" / "36 个技能" / "9 personas" references in current-state docs (grep clean except the deliberately-preserved historical line at `skills/CHANGELOG.md:181`)
- [x] Heading anchors not referenced from TOCs or cross-refs

## Summary

PR #35 (fix #14) で進行中の無惨死を null マスクしたが、null だと「未死亡 / マスク / バグ」の区別が API consumer から付きにくい。neighborhood project の [firewolf の DeadView](https://github.com/h-orito/firewolf/blob/main/backend/src/main/kotlin/com/ort/firewolf/api/view/dead/DeadView.kt) / [VillageParticipantView](https://github.com/h-orito/firewolf/blob/main/backend/src/main/kotlin/com/ort/firewolf/api/view/village/VillageParticipantView.kt) に揃えて以下に変更:

### Backend

- **新規 \`api/response/village/dead/DeadView.kt\`**:
  - フィールド: \`code: String\`, \`name: String\`, \`day: Int\`
  - \`constructor(dead, shouldMaskMiserable)\` でマスク判定し、無惨死 (襲撃 / 呪殺 / 罠死 / 爆死 / 雑魚) は code=**\"MISERABLE\"**, name=**\"無惨\"** に統一 (CDef にない API 専用合成コード)
  - 突然 / 処刑 / 後追 は CDef コード透過
- **\`VillageParticipantView\` から \`isDead\` / \`deadReasonCode\` / \`deadReasonName\` / \`deadDay\` の 4 フィールドを除去**し、\`dead: DeadView?\` (生存中は null) に統合
  - ドメインモデル \`VillageParticipant.dead: Dead\` と対称になる

### Frontend

- \`pnpm gen:api\` で OpenAPI 型再生成 (構造変更を含むため必須)
- **RoomGridPanel**: \`participant.isDead/deadReasonCode/deadDay\` → \`participant.dead?\` 経由に。\`deadMarkOf\` に \`case \"MISERABLE\" → \"▲\"\` を明示追加
- **villages.\$id.tsx (ParticipantsPanel)**: \`p.isDead/deadReasonName/deadDay\` → \`p.dead?\` に。\`?? \"無惨死\"\` フォールバックは不要 (backend が必ず返す)
- **CreatorPanel / AdminPanel**: \`!p.isDead\` → \`!p.dead\`

## Test plan

- [x] \`cd backend && ./gradlew test\` passing
- [x] \`cd frontend && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build\` passing
- [ ] ローカル backend + frontend で進行中の村を開き、DevTools で API response の \`dead.code === \"MISERABLE\"\` / \`dead.name === \"無惨\"\` を確認
- [ ] pr-reviewer サブエージェントで review → 反映

author: abhimehro
body:
💡 **What:** 
The optimization batches candidate appends per-directory and hoists the `extend` and `append` method lookups to avoid redundant method call resolution inside the hot inner loop of `os.walk`. It creates a temporary `dir_candidates` list for each directory, populates it using the hoisted `append` method, and then `extend`s the main `candidates` list.

🎯 **Why:** 
The innermost block processes many files across the repository. Previously, it appended each candidate directly to the main list with `candidates.append(...)`. Method attribute lookups (like `.append` on a list object) inside a tight loop introduce minor but accumulating CPython overhead. Further, appending individually scales linearly with the number of files. While seemingly small, batching results and hoisting the C-backed method references provides the fastest execution path without altering the block's semantics or wrapping the inner logic in a generator/helper function (which incurs its own function call overhead).

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
A focused benchmark mimicking the target file traversal across the current workspace running 200 iterations measured:
- **Baseline:** ~66.3 seconds
- **Optimized (Batched + Hoisted extend/append):** ~64.9 seconds
- **Improvement:** ~1.4 seconds (~2.1% speedup over baseline).

*Note: Attempts using generator expressions and list comprehensions coupled with helper functions were slightly slower than the baseline (typically ~68s) due to the python function call overhead generated for each file.*

author: rafe-walker
body:
## Summary

Two follow-on deliverables from the #207 CC#2 hand-off — both small, parallel, ship without waiting on other lanes.

**Deliverable A — \"All tenants\" aggregate cost panel.** When the operator picks the aggregate pseudo-option in the tenant picker, `/cost-state` now renders side-by-side per-tenant cost cards (one card per tenant) sourced from the snapshot v6 `cost_ladder_by_tenant` block. Aggregate footer surfaces total spent + combined credit pool. DashboardPage's small Cost card shows a compact one-line aggregate summary in the same mode, linking through to `/cost-state` for the breakdown.

**Deliverable B — Deep-link URLs + active-tenant header badge.** `?tenant=marvin` (and `?tenant=all` for aggregate) deep-links work on every tenant-scoped page. Every audit + cost + promotion page header gets an `<ActiveTenantBadge>` that surfaces the current tenant + opens the sidebar picker on click + copies a share-URL via the Clipboard API (with `prompt()` fallback for blocked contexts). Hidden on single-tenant deployments.

## What changed

### `web/src/hooks/useActiveTenant.ts`
- `ALL_TENANTS_URL_ALIAS = \"all\"` — operator-readable URL form for the aggregate sentinel. Internal sentinel stays `\"__all__\"` so it can't collide with a real tenant_id named \"all\". `useResolvedTenant` translates the alias on read.
- `tenantToUrlValue()` helper round-trips sentinel → alias for share-URL construction.
- `OPEN_TENANT_PICKER_EVENT` custom-event name + `requestOpenTenantPicker()` helper — page-header badges dispatch this to ask the sidebar picker to open. Decouples badge (per-page) from picker (sidebar) without prop-drilling.

### `web/src/components/TenantPicker.tsx`
- Listens for `OPEN_TENANT_PICKER_EVENT` and sets `open=true` when fired.

### `web/src/components/ActiveTenantBadge.tsx` (new)
- Compact `Viewing: <tenant>` chip + Copy-share-URL button.
- Hidden when `loadingTenants || !isMultiTenant` (B.2 single-tenant degradation).
- Share-URL uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText` in secure contexts; falls back to `window.prompt()` for blocked clipboard / non-HTTPS.
- Re-exports `ACTIVE_TENANT_BADGE_USES_SENTINEL = ALL_TENANTS_SENTINEL` so the drift-guard test pins the badge ↔ hook constant tie.

### `web/src/components/AggregateCostCards.tsx` (new)
- Fetches `/api/snapshot` once (re-fetches on parent-supplied `reloadKey` bump).
- Renders one `<TenantCostCard>` per tenant from `availableTenants` (default-first, then alphabetical). Empty-state card for tenants listed but absent from `cost_ladder_by_tenant`.
- Per-card: tenant name + canonical-tenant chip for `default` + tier badge + spent / pool + pct-used progress bar with tone tracking the rung.
- Aggregate footer (when ≥2 summable tenants): total spent across all tenants + combined credit pool + skipped-count for tenants with no numeric data yet.
- Italic foot-note explaining what's *not* in the aggregate view (per-tenant deferred tickets / reconciliation history / rate-limit pulse live on the single-tenant view — picker swap to a specific tenant for those).

### `web/src/pages/CostStatePage.tsx`
- Renders `<ActiveTenantBadge>` in the page header.
- `loadState` early-exits when `isAllTenants` (no misleading default-tenant payload pinned to page state); Reload button bumps `aggregateReloadKey` instead.
- Renders `<AggregateCostCards>` when `isAllTenants`; otherwise the existing single-tenant burn / deferred / reconciliation sections.
- Drops the #207 \"falling back to default\" explainer (aggregate is real now).

### `web/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx`
- Captures `snap.cost_ladder_by_tenant` into local state during `loadInitial`.
- Cost DashboardCard title becomes `\"Cost (all tenants)\"` in aggregate mode; body switches to `<AggregateCostCardBody>` showing `\"$N / $M, K tenants · click for breakdown\"`. Falls back to the single-tenant body when the snapshot's by-tenant block isn't populated (single-tenant deployments).

### Audit + promotion page headers
ProbeInvestigations, AlertInvestigations, EmailIntentLog, OutboundEmailLog, Autofix, KoraActions, PromotionReview — each H2 now sits inside a `<div className=\"flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap\">` alongside `<ActiveTenantBadge />`. URL `?tenant=` deep-link already works (the #207 hook resolves URL → localStorage → default); the badge surfaces which tenant is active in the page chrome.

### `tests/test_tenants_endpoint.py`
- New `test_fe_aggregate_and_deeplink_pins` pinning:
  - `ALL_TENANTS_URL_ALIAS = \"all\"` (URL form)
  - `ALL_TENANTS_SENTINEL = \"__all__\"` (internal form)
  - `OPEN_TENANT_PICKER_EVENT = \"kora:open-tenant-picker\"` name
  - `ACTIVE_TENANT_BADGE_USES_SENTINEL = ALL_TENANTS_SENTINEL` re-export in badge
  - `cost_ladder_by_tenant` literal grep in AggregateCostCards (asserts canonical data-source choice)

## Deep-link examples

- `/probe-investigations?tenant=marvin` — investigations scoped to marvin (badge: Viewing marvin)
- `/cost-state?tenant=all` — aggregate cost cards (badge: Viewing All tenants)
- `/kora-actions?tenant=default` — explicit default view (badge: Viewing default, only if multi-tenant)

URL precedence (from #207): URL `?tenant=` → localStorage → \"default\". Picker selections write localStorage but do NOT mutate the URL — a shared deep-link continues to anchor the page even after the operator clicks a different tenant.

## Build
- `tsc -b && vite build` ✓ clean (one pre-existing chunk-size warning; not introduced by this bucket).
- `python3 -m py_compile tests/test_tenants_endpoint.py` ✓.
- Pytest runtime not available in CC#2 worktree (no `.venv`); CI runs it on PR.

## Test plan
- [ ] `?tenant=marvin` direct link → useActiveTenant returns `\"marvin\"`; picker shows marvin selected; audit endpoints get `?tenant_id=marvin`
- [ ] `?tenant=all` direct link → `isAllTenants=true`; badge shows \"All tenants\"; cost-state renders aggregate cards
- [ ] Direct link without `?tenant=` → falls back to localStorage → \"default\"
- [ ] Single-tenant deployment: badge hidden everywhere (mirrors picker auto-hide)
- [ ] 2+ tenant deployment + All tenants pick:
  - CostStatePage shows N cards, default-first
  - aggregate footer surfaces `$X across N tenants this period · $Y combined credit pool`
  - DashboardPage Cost card shows compact `$X / $Y, N tenants · click for breakdown`
- [ ] Mobile viewport (< md breakpoint) → aggregate cards stack 1-up
- [ ] Copy-share-URL: badge button copies `<current URL>?tenant=<active>` to clipboard; non-secure context falls back to prompt()
- [ ] Click badge → sidebar picker opens
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_tenants_endpoint.py` — 6 tests pass (3 endpoint + 3 drift-guard, +1 new aggregate/deeplink pin)

## Recommendation for next CC#2 dispatch
**Per-tenant audit BE filter verification (depends on CC#1 #447 landing).** Once CC#1's per-tenant audit JSONL paths + `?tenant_id=` BE filter ship, add a small verification bucket: spin up two tenants, fire seam events for each, assert each FE audit page (with the existing `?tenant_id=` forwarding from #207) renders only the matching subset. ~½ day. Tightens the contract that's currently \"BE may ignore the param\" into \"BE filters correctly.\"

**Lighter follow-on if #447 hasn't landed yet:** TenantPicker keyboard nav + URL-write toggle. Currently the picker is mouse-only and selections never mutate the URL. Add (a) ↑/↓/Enter/Esc keyboard nav and (b) an opt-in \"also update URL\" toggle in the picker so deep-link-anchored pages can decouple if the operator wants. ~3 hours.

author: ibondarenko1
body:
## What

Adding a new hunting query: **Raw IP Address Used as URL Domain** under `Hunting Queries/Microsoft 365 Defender/Email and Collaboration Queries/Phish/`.

## Why this is novel for this list

I checked existing queries in both the `Phish` and `URL` subfolders. The URL folder covers click metrics (Top Users, SafeLinks, blocked clicks, by-workload, etc.) and the Phish folder covers Detection Technology reporting + appspot/punycode/device-code patterns. **No existing query specifically detects URLs where the domain is a raw IPv4 address.**

This pattern is a strong indicator of:
- Commodity phishing avoiding DNS-takedown
- Generic spam campaigns rotating raw IPs
- Compromised hosts used as throwaway payload servers

The query is straightforward (regex match on `UrlDomain` plus inner join to `EmailEvents` for enrichment) and complements existing detection technology coverage by surfacing infrastructure that may not yet be classified by reputation systems.

## What it detects

```kql
EmailUrlInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where UrlDomain matches regex @"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$"
| join kind=inner (EmailEvents ...) on NetworkMessageId
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
```

MITRE: T1566 Phishing, T1566.002 Spearphishing Link.

## Source

This query is contributed from [m365-security-operations](https://github.com/ibondarenko1/m365-security-operations), an open-source M365 + Cloudflare audit-and-remediate toolkit. It is drill 06 (`01-sentinel-detection-engineering/kql/06-ip-as-url-detection.kql`) in the toolkit's published KQL hunting drill set, hand-authored for small-org Microsoft 365 tenants and published under MIT.

## Tuning notes (also in `description-detailed`)

- Filter on `EmailDirection == "Inbound"` to exclude outbound security correspondence that may legitimately reference raw IPs (vulnerability disclosures, security workflow).
- Maintain an allowlist of trusted security workflow mailboxes if outbound security correspondence is a common false-positive source.

## License

The query content follows the existing Azure-Sentinel community contribution model; happy to adjust attribution or remove any portion of the description that would be better placed elsewhere.

author: mattsears18
body:
Closes #296

## Summary

GitHub returns two different login shapes for the same GH App account depending on which API the caller hits:

- **REST** (e.g. `/repos/.../issues/N/events`) → `sentry[bot]`
- **GraphQL Bot/App actor objects** (what `gh issue list --json author` returns) → `app/sentry`

Pre-#296 `setup.md` step 1.7 did a literal lowercased-substring match between the GraphQL `author.login` and the entries in `.shipyard/trusted-authors.txt`, so a maintainer who followed the file's documented convention and put `sentry[bot]` in the allowlist saw every Sentry-bot-filed issue silently bucketed as untrusted by step 2's bucket 0.5 and dropped by step 4's client-side filter. The setup-time `[trusted-authors] loaded 2 author(s)` advisory was misleading — the bot was "in the file" but not effectively trusted.

The fix adds a shared shell helper (`plugins/shipyard/scripts/trusted-authors-normalize.sh`) that reads the allowlist and, for every `<name>[bot]` or `app/<name>` entry, **cross-adds the other shape** to the set. So a file with `sentry[bot]` produces `{sentry[bot], app/sentry}` and either form matches at comparison time. Human logins (no `[bot]` suffix, no `app/` prefix) pass through unchanged. A `--report-aliases` mode emits the per-alias log line the acceptance criterion requested.

The two GitHub Actions workflows (`intake-refinement-gate.yml`, `label-event-audit.yml`) that resolve the same allowlist inline equivalent `awk` logic — workflows live in consumer repos and can't reach into the shipyard plugin's `scripts/` dir, so the helper script is for the orchestrator-side and the `awk` is for the workflow-side. Test suites guard both implementations.

Verified the failure mode end-to-end on `mattsears18/lightwork` before writing the fix: `gh issue view 1041 --repo mattsears18/lightwork --json author --jq '.author.login'` returns `app/sentry`, confirming the GraphQL shape mismatches the documented `sentry[bot]` file convention.

Implements **option 2** from the issue body (the cheapest, least disruptive). Both shapes "just work" after this lands.

## Test plan

- [x] New test suite `trusted-authors-normalize.test.sh` (38 assertions) covers alias expansion, input cleaning, `--report-aliases` mode, file-argument mode, and sort+dedupe.
- [x] Updated `refine-issues.test.sh` and `label-event-audit.test.sh` assert that both workflows define an `expand_aliases` helper and handle both shapes.
- [x] All 21 existing test suites in `plugins/shipyard/scripts/tests/` still pass.
- [x] `shellcheck` is clean across all 37 plugin shell scripts (the project's `severity=style` gate).
- [x] Manually verified the `awk` logic in the workflows matches the bash helper's output for the canonical input cases (`sentry[bot]`, `app/sentry`, mixed humans+bots+apps, pre-paired both-shapes input).

## Acceptance criteria from #296

- [x] An issue authored by a GH App actor (e.g., Sentry's `app/sentry`) is recognized as trusted when the allowlist file lists either `app/sentry` OR `sentry[bot]`.
- [x] Setup-time advisory log emits an `[trusted-authors] alias: sentry[bot] -> app/sentry` line per alias applied (via `--report-aliases`).
- [x] Documented the dual login shapes in `setup.md` §1.7's new "GH App alias normalization" sub-section (the `.shipyard/trusted-authors.txt` template header lives in consumer repos, not this one — `setup.md` is now the canonical reference and the helper's own header comment carries the rationale for any direct readers).

body:
## Summary

Establishes the token architecture for multi-city visual identity.
This is **scaffolding** — no visible change for Rome, and Barcelona /
Athens get their own accent hue on every existing CTA / active state /
link surface automatically via the existing \`var(--accent)\` cascade.

## Architecture

Two layers of tokens:

| Token | Status | Drives |
|---|---|---|
| \`--accent\`, \`--accent-deep\` | **City-overridable** | CTAs, active states, ghost-button text, links, timeline markers, map markers |
| \`--brand-accent\`, \`--brand-accent-deep\` | **Brand-locked** | Parranda logo gradient (\`.brand-mark\`) |
| \`--terracotta\` | **Brand-locked** | Live Pulse dot |
| \`--gold\` | **Brand-locked** | Logo gold partner, score pills |

City overrides live in \`body[data-city-key="..."]\` blocks at the top
of \`styles.css\`. The body element already carries \`data-city-key\`
(set server-side in \`server/app.js:669\`), so no wiring change is
needed.

## City values

| City | --accent | --accent-deep | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rome (default) | \`#af4d24\` | \`#7f2d1a\` | Existing terracotta |
| Barcelona | \`#2c5282\` | \`#1e3a5f\` | Mediterranean cobalt |
| Athens | \`#1a5276\` | \`#0e3a52\` | Aegean indigo |

All four override values pass WCAG AAA contrast for white text on
button backgrounds (>7:1).

## What changes visibly

- **Rome**: nothing (default \`--accent\` is unchanged terracotta).
- **Barcelona**: every CTA, active tab/chip, link color, and active
  filter pill becomes Mediterranean cobalt. Pulse dot stays brand
  terracotta. Parranda logo stays brand terracotta+gold.
- **Athens**: same, with Aegean indigo.

## What does NOT change

- No component restructure
- No new components
- No Planner/Blitz/Pulse logic changes
- No copy changes
- No new icons
- No new font work
- Pulse cross-city visual rule (\`pulse-cross-city-css.test.js\`)
  still holds — only accent hue swaps, surface structure stays
  shared.

## Contract test

New \`tests/cross-city-accent-tokens.test.js\` pins the rule:

- City blocks may override \`--accent\` / \`--accent-deep\` only
- Promoting any brand-locked token (\`--brand-accent\`, \`--terracotta\`,
  \`--gold\`, structural surface tokens) to overridable is a regression
- \`.brand-mark\` must reference \`--brand-accent\`, not \`--accent\`,
  so the Parranda logo never shifts color per city

## Files changed (2)

1. \`styles.css\` — :root tokens + Barcelona/Athens city blocks +
   .brand-mark migration to \`--brand-accent\`
2. \`tests/cross-city-accent-tokens.test.js\` (new) — 5-test contract

## Tests

- \`node --test tests/cross-city-accent-tokens.test.js\` — 5/5 pass
- \`node --test tests/pulse-cross-city-css.test.js\` — 4/4 pass
  (existing cross-city consistency rule still holds)
- \`npm test\` — **534/534 pass** (+5 new contract tests, +1 existing)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Manual visual QA: load \`/barcelona\` and \`/athens\` and confirm
  CTA/link colors flip as expected
- Possible future: city-specific \`--brand-accent\` if a city is ever
  promoted to standalone product
- Possible future: dark-mode token layer (uses same architecture)

author: jagmarques
body:
## Bug

PyPI rejected the asqav 0.4.6 publish with:

```
400 Invalid distribution file. ZIP archive not accepted:
Duplicate filename in local headers
```

for `asqav/templates/shadow-ai/README.md` and `asqav/templates/shadow-ai/docker-compose.yml`.

The 0.4.6 release only landed after a one-time manual `zip -d` on the wheel to delete the duplicate entries before `twine upload`. That was a hack and should not be required again.

## Root cause

`python/pyproject.toml` had:

```
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/asqav"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"src/asqav/templates" = "asqav/templates"
```

`packages = ["src/asqav"]` already pulls every file under `src/asqav/` (including `templates/`) into the wheel under `asqav/`. The `force-include` block then mapped the SAME source path to the SAME destination path, so hatch wrote each template file twice into the zip - one local header per write.

`twine`/PyPI treat duplicate local headers as malformed.

## Fix

Drop the `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]` and `[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.force-include]` blocks entirely. The package config already covers them.

Bumped 0.4.6 -> 0.4.7. Python-only; TypeScript version untouched.

## Verification

```
cd python && rm -rf dist/ && uv build
unzip -l dist/asqav-0.4.7-py3-none-any.whl | grep templates
```

Output:

```
1608  ... asqav/templates/shadow-ai/README.md
1065  ... asqav/templates/shadow-ai/docker-compose.yml
```

Each template path appears exactly once. No duplicate filenames anywhere in the wheel.

```
cd python && uv run --no-sync pytest tests/ -q
```

`805 passed in 12.96s` - matches the 0.4.6 baseline.

comment hygiene clean

author: hughhan1
body:
## Summary

`Cache` is now the fakeable SDK contract, and `gestalt.Cache()` returns `cache.Cache` directly instead of a client-shaped wrapper.

## Interfaces

```go
func Cache(name ...string) (cache.Cache, error)

type Cache interface {
  Get(context.Context, string) ([]byte, bool, error)
  GetMany(context.Context, []string) (map[string][]byte, error)
  Set(context.Context, string, []byte, cache.SetOptions) error
  SetMany(context.Context, []cache.Entry, cache.SetOptions) error
  Delete(context.Context, string) (bool, error)
  DeleteMany(context.Context, []string) (int64, error)
  Touch(context.Context, string, time.Duration) (bool, error)
}
```

## Usage

```go
cache, err := gestalt.Cache("sessions")
if err != nil { return err }
err = cache.Set(ctx, "session:1", []byte("ready"), gestalt.CacheSetOptions{})
```

## Call Path

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Go --> RPC["rpc/cache"]
  Py --> Proto
  TS --> Proto
  Rust --> Proto
  RPC --> G["gestaltd"]
  Proto --> G
  G --> RPC2["rpc/cache"]
  RPC2 --> P["provider"]
```

Go uses `gestaltd/rpc/cache`; Python, TypeScript, and Rust use the shared generated proto service exposed by gestaltd.

body:
`/game` and `/playbot` were using static `<title>` values, which made tabs/history non-descriptive. This change moves title generation server-side so game pages render participant-aware titles while preserving safe fallbacks.

- **Routing + rendering path**
  - Added `GamePageRenderer` and routed `/game` + `/playbot` through it.
  - Removed these two routes from static template mappings so titles can be resolved from game data.

- **Server-side title resolution**
  - **PvP**:
    - Always renders **red player first**.
    - If `inviterColor` is still `null` (colors not picked yet), title is `new game by <inviter>`.
  - **PvB**: orders players by color and renders engine as `EngineName (depth)`.
  - On game fetch failure, falls back to previous defaults:
    - PvP: `Game`
    - PvB: `Play vs. Bot`

- **Template changes**
  - `player_vs_player_game.html` and `player_vs_bot.html` now use `{{page_title}}` in `<title>`.

- **Focused coverage**
  - Added/updated `GamePageRendererTest` for:
    - red-first PvP ordering
    - pre-color-selection PvP title (`new game by <inviter>`)
    - PvP/PvB formatting and fallback constants

```kotlin
internal fun formatPvpPageTitle(inviterUsername: String, inviteeUsername: String?, inviterColor: Color?): String {
    if (inviterColor == null) {
        return "new game by $inviterUsername"
    }

    val invitee = inviteeUsername ?: "opponent"
    return when (inviterColor) {
        Color.RED -> "$inviterUsername vs $invitee"
        Color.BLACK -> "$invitee vs $inviterUsername"
    }
}
```

author: drumfiend21
body:
## Summary

Brings cloud-session eval suite from **2151/2259 → 2253/2259 passing (+102)** so that Claude Code on the web can run the same workflow loop as local Macs. Three coordinated portability fixes plus a `.gitignore` narrowing.

## Motivation

Cloud sessions were running ruby 3.3.6 (vs local 2.6.10) and a sandbox `~/.gitconfig` with `commit.gpgsign=true` pointing at a server-side signing helper. Two failure classes resulted:
- **87 specs** failing with `Psych::DisallowedClass: Tried to load unspecified class: Time/Date` — Ruby 3.1+ ships Psych 4, which defaults to safe-load semantics that reject `Time`, `Date`, `Symbol`.
- **48 specs** failing during setup with `signing failed: signing server returned status 400: missing source` — test setups that run `git commit` triggered the host signing helper.

## Changes

### 1. `.ruby-version` → `3.3.6`
Pins the repo to the cloud base image's ruby. Local clones on ruby 2.6 should `rbenv install 3.3.6 && rbenv local 3.3.6` (or `asdf install ruby 3.3.6`).

### 2. `YAML.load_file` → `YAML.unsafe_load_file` across 32 substrate files
`unsafe_load_file` is the documented Psych 4 drop-in for prior `YAML.load` behavior — it accepts arbitrary classes (which we control, since these files are project-owned YAML). Files: `commands/`, `generated-code-quality-standards/`, `hooks/scripts/`, `pr-corpus/`, `profiles/`, `rubric/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, `standards/`, `workflow/`.

### 3. `evals/runner.sh` exports hermetic git config
```bash
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign;  export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false
export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=tag.gpgsign;     export GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=false
```
Env-level git config overrides `~/.gitconfig` but yields to per-repo `git config` set inside the workdir, so author-attribution specs (e.g. `records-author-from-git-config` which sets a local `Test User`) remain authoritative. Deliberately did **not** override `user.name` / `user.email` — initial attempt did and regressed that spec.

### 4. `.gitignore` narrowed
Removed blanket `space/` ignore that silently dropped substrate scripts from CL-137/138 commits (`space/cross-loop-emit.sh`, `space/honest-scope-validate.sh`, `space/retention-sweep.sh`, `space/README.md`). Privacy-sensitive `space/.local/` and user-data `.claude-tdd-pro/space/` remain ignored.

## Suite results (cloud: ruby 3.3.6, bash 5.2, node 22, python 3.11)

| State    | Passed   | Failed | Notes                                                 |
|----------|----------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Before   | 2151     | 108    | 87 YAML, 48 git-signing, ~10 setup-silent (overlap)   |
| After    | **2253** | 6      | All 6 blocked by gitignored local-only files          |

## Remaining 6 failures (out of scope for this PR)

The following specs assert behavior of substrate that exists on the maintainer's local Mac but never reached git (silently dropped by the old `.gitignore` `space/` line). Once the missing files are pushed from local — now possible because of change (4) above — they should go green automatically:

- `action-cards-include-rule-id-from-suppression` — needs `space/cross-loop-emit.sh`
- `friction-events-emit-rubric-loop-action-cards` — needs `space/cross-loop-emit.sh`
- `honest-scope-validator-fails-when-caveat-missing-from-readme` — needs `space/honest-scope-validate.sh`
- `readme-documents-self-observation-not-productivity-science` — needs `space/README.md`
- `retention-prunes-entries-older-than-window` — needs `space/retention-sweep.sh`
- `evals-datasets-skills-folder-exists` — needs `evals/datasets/skills/` folder

## Test plan

## Summary

- **Luxury welcome screen**: A frosted glass card fades in from blur on first launch, featuring the app logo mark, a gradient "NovaTeX" wordmark, and two animated gradient blobs behind the card that make the `backdrop-filter: blur` effect visibly rich in the macOS WebView.
- **LaTeX gate**: A new `check_latex` Rust command probes `/Library/TeX/texbin`, Homebrew paths, and system PATH for `latexmk` and `pdflatex`. The app will not proceed until at least one is found.
- **Four phases**: welcome (2.6s auto-advance) → checking (spinner) → ready (animated SVG checkmark + CTA) or missing (brew install instructions with copy buttons + retry).
- **One-time gate**: `localStorage` flag `novatex_onboarded` is set on first successful entry; all subsequent launches skip onboarding and land directly on Home.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` | Added `LatexCheckResult` struct, `check_binary` helper, `check_latex` Tauri command |

- The glass effect is subtle in a plain browser (backdrop blurs a flat colour) but pronounced in the native macOS WebView where the compositor has a real layer to blur against.

author: shanimosco47-pixel
body:
## Beeps fix
`AudioContext` was created eagerly at page load (starts `suspended` on Android), and `ctx.resume()` was called but not awaited before scheduling oscillators. Scheduled audio would burst when the context later resumed.

**Fix:**
- `ctx` is now `null` at load, created lazily on first user gesture
- `ensureAudioCtx()` awaits `ctx.resume()` — called at the top of `startRecording()`, `pauseRecording()`, `stopRecording()` before any beep
- `beep()` guards on `ctx.state === 'running'` to drop any stale schedules

## Google Docs fix
Two integration options, clearly separated:

**Option A — Apps Script** (recommended for personal use, no Cloud Console):
1. script.google.com → New project → paste the `doPost` function from the code comment

author: kayl-codes
body:
## Description

This PR introduces a massive overhaul of the TrueNAS integration, bumping the version to **v1.5.0**. It focuses on modernizing the API communication, significantly improving connection stability, adding highly requested features, and completely resolving strict static analysis (Ruff & Sourcery) warnings.

### Core & API Improvements:
* **WebSocket Protocol Update:** Fully migrated the connection handshake to the modern TrueNAS DDP protocol (`"msg": "connect"` and `"msg": "method"` via `/websocket`), ensuring robust compatibility with modern TrueNAS SCALE/CORE releases.
* **Thread Safety & Stability:** Introduced a strict dual-lock architecture (`_lock` and `_io_lock`) to eliminate race conditions, deadlocks, and overlapping I/O operations.
* **Robust Error Handling:** Replaced brittle string-matching with strict exception-type checks (`websockets`, `ssl`, `socket`) and centralized error constants. Added defensive parsing for subprotocol negotiation.
* **Smart Timeouts:** Increased WebSocket handshake timeouts to 60s and query timeouts to 30s to seamlessly accommodate TrueNAS systems under heavy load or during startups.

### Config Flow & Setup:
* **Auto-Discovery:** Automatically guesses the TrueNAS IP via DNS to speed up the initial setup process.
* **Pre-Flight Port Check:** Added an asynchronous, IPv6-ready TCP port check to fail fast (and safely) before attempting a WebSocket connection, providing precise frontend feedback.
* **Secure Reconfiguration:** Ensures the API key is not leaked in plaintext when the user re-enters the configuration flow.
* **Better Error Mapping:** Maps backend connection errors safely to frontend translation keys (e.g., `cannot_connect`, `invalid_key`, `unknown`).

### Entities & Sensors:
* **New Features:** Added entities for **TrueNAS Alerts** and **SMB Connections**.
* **Fixed Service Controls:** Updated the control payload from the deprecated `service.control` to the modern `service.start/stop/restart/reload` commands for flawless service management in HA.
* **Redundant Entities Cleanup:** Disabled the read-only `binary_sensor` for services by default, as the `switch` entities now perfectly handle state and control. Removed the redundant word "Switch" from entity names.
* **Improved Disk Temperatures:** Enhanced the temperature extraction by smartly combining Netdata graphs with a robust API fallback (`disk.temperatures`) across multiple identifiers (`name`, `devname`, `identifier`).
* **Version Parsing:** Improved TrueNAS OS version extraction using regex to prevent crashes or zero-version outputs on non-standard strings.
* **Log Reduction:** Fixed log spamming caused by transient failures in system stat graphs.

## Motivation and Context
The integration was experiencing sporadic connection drops, relying on deprecated service calls, and throwing static analysis warnings. This PR stabilizes the foundation of the integration, prepares it for future TrueNAS updates, and significantly improves both the developer and user experience.

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] 🛠️ Refactoring (code cleanup, performance improvements, resolving linter warnings)
- [x] 📚 Documentation Update (README, translations, formatting)

author: steverowley
body:
## Summary
You're right — the pop progression was still the wrong vibe. Rewrote for **actual lo-fi feel**.

### Sound design
- **Slower jazzy chords**: `Fmaj7 → Em7 → Dm7 → Cmaj7`. The maj7 + m7 voicings give it "study cafe" warmth; the descending root motion is mellow rather than driving.
- **10-second holds with 3.6s crossfade** — way slower than the pop version (6.5/1.8). Lets each chord breathe.
- Routed through a single **low-pass `BiquadFilter` at 1100Hz Q 0.6** for that muffled tape-warmth.
- Wider **±8¢ random detune** per oscillator → hazy chorus.
- A **sub-octave sine** at half the root frequency on each chord, 1.8% gain, also low-passed — gives body without thump.
- Master gain capped at **3.5%** so it stays well under SFX.

### Vinyl crackle
- White noise bursts (~40ms), high-passed at 2.4 kHz to keep them airy instead of muddy.
- Scheduled at random **180–720 ms** intervals while music is on. Capped at 0.8% gain.
- Auto-stops when music stops or sound is muted.

### No UI changes
Same Settings toggle, same start/stop pipeline. If this still isn't the vibe, easy levers:
- Chord set (`MUSIC_CHORDS`)
- Filter cutoff (lower = more muffled)
- Crackle density (`180 + Math.random() * 540`)
- Sub volume (`0.018`)

## Files
- `src/audio/sfx.js` — new `playLoFiChord`, `playCrackle`, slower chord scheduler, crackle scheduler. Old pop-chord code removed.

author: actuarialnotes
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes an issue where study plans could be generated with incomplete mastery data, causing inconsistent daily plans. The fix introduces a `masteryLoading` flag that gates plan generation until mastery records are fully loaded, and refactors the dependency tracking to prevent reactive re-generation when mastery data updates.

## Key Changes

- **Added `masteryLoading` parameter to `useStudyPlan`**: A new boolean flag (default `false`) that prevents plan generation while mastery records are still loading. This ensures plans are never cached with partial/empty mastery data.

- **Introduced `masteryRef` in `useStudyPlan`**: Uses `useRef` to maintain a stable reference to the latest mastery snapshot without making it a reactive dependency. This allows the plan to remain frozen for the day (only regenerating on config/date changes) while still using current mastery data when generation does occur.

- **Updated dependency array**: Removed `masteryRecords` from the effect dependency array and added `masteryLoading`. This prevents unnecessary plan regeneration when mastery data updates mid-day, while ensuring generation is gated until loading completes.

- **Updated `useConceptMastery` initial state**: Changed `loading` initial state from `false` to `true` to properly reflect that data is being fetched on mount.

- **Improved concept sorting stability**: Added a secondary sort by concept name (`localeCompare`) when state order is equal. This ensures deterministic ordering and prevents plan inconsistencies from sorting variations.

- **Propagated `masteryLoading` through components**: Updated `Search.tsx` and `Landing.tsx` to extract and pass the `masteryLoading` flag from `useConceptMastery` to `useStudyPlan`.

## Implementation Details

The core issue was that `masteryRecords` being a reactive dependency caused the plan to regenerate whenever mastery data arrived, even mid-day. By using a ref and gating on the `masteryLoading` flag, the plan now:
1. Waits for mastery data to fully load before generating
2. Stays stable throughout the day (same plan returned)
3. Still uses the latest mastery snapshot when generation occurs
4. Only regenerates on explicit triggers (config changes, date changes, or new day)

author: mvanhorn
body:
## The bug

`digg-pp-cli top --limit 20 --json` returned 7 distinct stories all stamped `currentRank: 1`, in an order that did not match `digg.com/ai`. The Karpathy joins-Anthropic story sat at rank 1 for 4+ days; the Cursor Composer story leaked `peakRank: 9999`.

## Root cause

`internal/diggparse/parser.go` ExtractClusters walks every JSON object containing `"clusterId":"` in the decoded RSC stream and merges occurrences by clusterId via mergeClusters. The /ai page legitimately emits the same cluster in multiple sections — main leaderboard `items[]`, plus one or more of `featuredStories`, `weeklyTop`, `sevenDaysStories`, pinned. Each section carries its own `rank` for the cluster.

mergeClusters previously used last-wins-when-nonzero for every field. Whichever section appeared last in the stream stamped the cluster's `currentRank`. Featured / weekly / pinned sections tend to assign low ranks like 1 to a small curated set, so they displaced the live leaderboard ranks of clusters that appeared in both.

`peakRank: 9999` is Digg's internal placeholder for newly-detected clusters with no tracked all-time peak; it should be normalized at the CLI's output boundary.

## The fix

Gate the four rank-bearing branches in mergeClusters (CurrentRank, PeakRank, PreviousRank, Delta) on `accumulator == 0` so first non-zero wins. The main /ai leaderboard array is emitted first in the RSC stream, so first-wins captures the canonical leaderboard rank for any cluster present in both sections. Zero accumulator still accepts a later non-zero, preserving sparse-then-full enrichment that legitimately fills missing fields from later occurrences.

Normalize `PeakRank == 9999` to 0 in ExtractClusters' output loop. The struct's `json:peakRank,omitempty` tag drops zero values, so the sentinel disappears from CLI JSON output without a schema change.

## Tests

`internal/diggparse/parser_rank_test.go` adds 5 scenarios:

- `TestMergeClustersFirstWinsForRankFields` — same clusterId twice with differing ranks; asserts first-wins for CurrentRank, PeakRank, PreviousRank, Delta.
- `TestMergeClustersStillGapFillsZeroAccumulator` — sparse first occurrence, full second; asserts later non-zero still fills the gap.
- `TestMergeClustersDistinctClustersPreserveOwnRanks` — two distinct clusters with rank 1 and rank 2; asserts no collapse.
- `TestExtractClustersNormalizesPeakRankSentinel` — peakRank=9999 in; PeakRank=0 out and json.Marshal omits the field.
- `TestExtractClustersPreservesLegitimatePeakRank` and `TestExtractClustersOmitsAbsentPeakRank` — non-sentinel values pass through unchanged; absent field stays absent.

61 of 61 diggparse tests pass. go vet clean.

## Out of scope

- Envelope-aware RSC extraction (parsing the RSC tree to scope cluster extraction to the main feed array only). Held in reserve if cross-section pollution recurs in fields the merge gate does not cover.
- Pre-existing govulncheck finding in `internal/client/digg_html.go` (golang.org/x/net@v0.43.0). Unrelated to this fix; per AGENTS.md scoped fixes do not double as dep-freshness campaigns.
- Two adjacent UX bugs in the report (`authors top --agent` returns empty objects; `author <name>` matches contributors only) deferred to follow-up.

Patches recorded in `.printing-press-patches.json`.

author: pbhopeful
body:
## Summary
Pen input was being lumped together with touch in `handleCanvasPointerDown`, setting `editorInterface.isTouchScreen = true`. This caused two related bugs:

1. A pen tap with the line/arrow tool drew a fixed-width horizontal stub and finalized immediately, instead of entering multipoint mode.
2. Since the flag was never reset, subsequent mouse clicks also finalized as 2-point lines until the page was reloaded.

The touchscreen-finalize behavior was intentionally designed for fingers, which can't precisely click multipoint. Pens are precise pointing devices and should behave like a mouse for this purpose.

## Fix
Remove `"pen"` from the condition at `App.tsx:7814-7821` that sets `isTouchScreen = true`. Touch (finger) input still gets the existing fixed-width finalize behavior.

## Related
- Fixes #9929
- Related to zsviczian/obsidian-excalidraw-plugin#2606
- Related to #11296 (that PR fixes the mouse-after-pen tail; this fixes the root cause, so the mouse-after-pen problem doesn't occur in the first place)

  - Mouse multipoint still works after a pen interaction

author: remcaro-rgb
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional Axiom HTTP sink that batches the run's structured-JSON records and POSTs them to \`https://api.axiom.co/v1/datasets/<dataset>/ingest\` at end-of-run. Replaces the Better Stack route in the original Tier 6 runbook — Better Stack was never actually provisioned, and Axiom's free tier (500GB/mo) is structurally better for our volume + cost profile.

## Design

- **Batch, don't per-record-flush** — one HTTP round-trip at end-of-run. A spec-generator run emits 10-50 records in 30s; per-record flushes would push the workflow cold-start budget.
- **Best-effort** — a failed POST writes a stderr warning and never crashes the agent. stdout JSON stays the authoritative audit trail; Axiom is a derived dashboard view.
- **No httpx dep** — \`urllib.request\` keeps the sink self-contained.
- **Composite sink** — stdout still always fires (\`stdout_and_axiom\`); Axiom is additive.
- **Activation** — \`AXIOM_TOKEN\` (secret) + \`AXIOM_DATASET\` (variable). Unset = stdout-only, no Axiom call.

## Test plan

- [x] 11 new unit tests covering buffer behaviour, HTTP failure modes, 4xx/5xx surfacing, env-driven activation
- [x] 452 tests total green
- [x] ruff + mypy clean (22 source files)
- [ ] After merge: set \`AXIOM_TOKEN\` + \`AXIOM_DATASET\` in \`GoliattCo/odoo-custom\` workflow env, fire a fresh canary, confirm records reach the Axiom dataset

author: rpgmem
body:
## Summary

Primeira tentativa de deploy end-to-end na Hostinger BR falhou silenciosamente porque o workflow `deploy-develop.yml` hardcodava porta 22, enquanto a hospedagem expõe SSH em porta alta (65002). Dois ajustes pequenos resolvem e tornam o workflow robusto pra outros provedores no futuro.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/deploy-develop.yml`**:
  - Adiciona suporte ao secret opcional `TESTES_SSH_PORT` (default `22` — VPS DigitalOcean/Linode/AWS continuam funcionando sem mudança). Tanto `ssh-keyscan` quanto o `ssh` dentro do `rsync -e` agora passam `-p $PORT`.
  - Troca `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` por `accept-new` no rsync (TOFU — aceita a chave do host na primeira conexão, exige match nas subsequentes). Mais seguro que `no` (que seria vulnerável a MITM); recupera de cenários em que o `ssh-keyscan` falha silenciosamente por causa de firewall/CDN.
  - Marca o `ssh-keyscan` como best-effort (`|| true`) — antes, falha dele com `set -e` derrubava o deploy inteiro sem log útil.

- **`CLAUDE.md`** (seção "Deploy to testes"): adiciona linha pra `TESTES_SSH_PORT` na tabela de secrets, com nota explicando que hospedagem gerenciada (Hostinger, KingHost, Locaweb) costuma usar portas não-padrão.

## Required manual actions (paralelas a este PR)

Pra que o próximo deploy funcione, o secret novo precisa estar cadastrado **antes** do merge deste PR ou o deploy disparado por ele vai falhar de novo:

1. Em https://github.com/rpgmem/ffcertificate/settings/secrets/actions adicionar `TESTES_SSH_PORT` = `65002`.
2. Garantir que `TESTES_SSH_KEY` tem a chave privada nova (gerada com `ssh-keygen` no servidor, sem passphrase).
3. Garantir que a pública correspondente foi appendada em `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` no servidor.
4. Confirmar `TESTES_REMOTE_PATH` (path absoluto até `wp-content/plugins/ffcertificate` no Hostinger, tipicamente sob `/home/u690874273/domains/<dominio>/public_html/...`).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: PHPStan, WPCS, PHPUnit, coverage, Vitest, ESLint, Stylelint, CodeQL, asset build verify.
- [ ] Após merge, o push em develop dispara `deploy-develop.yml` automaticamente.
- [ ] Validar no run: step "Configure SSH" deve completar sem erro; step "Rsync to testes" deve listar os arquivos enviados e terminar com `total size is …  speedup is …`.
- [ ] No servidor: `ls -lah $TESTES_REMOTE_PATH | head` deve mostrar `ffcertificate.php`, `includes/`, `assets/`, `templates/` com mtime de agora.

body:
💡 What:
Added dynamic `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` attributes to the reusable `<Input />` component, linking the input field to its helper text via a generated ID.

🎯 Why:
To ensure that screen reader users are properly notified of validation errors and can easily hear the associated helper text when interacting with form inputs throughout the application.

♿ Accessibility:
- Screen readers will now announce error states immediately when the field is focused via `aria-invalid`.

author: filiperomero2
body:
# fix: unblock first-run conda env creation + add `viralunity setup`

## The problem

On fresh installs with the latest conda stack (conda 26.x + conda-libmamba-solver 26.x), every ViralUnity pipeline run aborts on its very first sub-environment with `CreateCondaEnvironmentException`. The solver tries to fetch a `repodata_shards.msgpack.zst` index from bioconda — bioconda doesn't publish one — and conda crashes inside its own error handler instead of falling back. This blocks **every new user** on a modern conda stack.

## The fix

Two complementary layers:

**1. Pin the conda toolchain.** `environment.yml` now caps `conda` and `conda-libmamba-solver` to `<26`. An inline comment explains when it's safe to lift. One-line change, fully revertable.

**2. Pre-build envs into a shared cache.** New `viralunity setup` command materializes every per-rule conda env once, into a cache directory that every later run reuses:

```bash
viralunity setup --pipelines all
```

Default cache is `~/.cache/viralunity/conda-envs/` (override with `--conda-prefix` or `$VIRALUNITY_CONDA_PREFIX`). The same `--conda-prefix` flag is now also accepted by `viralunity consensus` and `viralunity meta`, so subsequent runs pick up the cache automatically. **Result: env creation only ever happens during an explicit `setup` step — never in the middle of a real analysis.**

The new subcommand also supports `--dry-run` to preview what would be built, and `--pipelines` is repeatable (`consensus-illumina`, `consensus-nanopore`, `meta-illumina`, `meta-nanopore`, `all`).

## Behaviour change

The default `--conda-prefix` is shared across working directories, so existing users' per-workdir `.snakemake/conda/` envs become orphaned on first post-upgrade run and rebuild once into the shared cache. After that, runs are faster and survive across workdirs.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit suite: 138 tests pass (+13 new for `--conda-prefix` and `setup`).
- [x] Snakemake dry-run regression: 6/6 workflows pass.
- [x] Lint clean on every file touched.
- [x] Manual end-to-end: ran the consensus-illumina tutorial on the bundled SARS-CoV-2 test data (`my_test_data/illumina_data/`) — `viralunity setup` materialized envs without error, the pipeline completed all 21 rules, both samples produced valid consensus FASTAs (≥97% horizontal coverage, ≥2000× mean depth), and the multi-sample alignment was built correctly.

### Suggested reviewer checks

- [ ] On a clean machine with conda 26.x, rebuild the env from this branch's `environment.yml` and confirm `conda list conda-libmamba-solver` reports `<26`.
- [ ] Run `viralunity setup --pipelines consensus-illumina --dry-run` and confirm the env list looks right.
- [ ] In a fresh working directory, run any `viralunity consensus` / `viralunity meta` invocation and confirm `.snakemake/conda/` stays empty (the shared cache is being used).

## Commits

1. `fix(conda): pin conda toolchain to <26 to avoid bioconda shards 404`
2. `feat(cli): thread --conda-prefix through orchestrator + consensus/meta CLIs`
3. `feat(setup): add viralunity setup subcommand to pre-build per-rule conda envs`
4. `docs: document viralunity setup, --conda-prefix, and first-time env build`

Kept separate so the conda pin can be reverted on its own if it ever causes an unrelated regression.

## Out of scope

- Container image (a future option that would let us lift the pin).

## Summary

Updates the query parameter in the `AniSkipApi` interface from `types` to `types[]`. While the primary cause of yesterday's loading failure was a temporary outage of the `arm.haglund.dev` mapping service (which is now back online), this change officially aligns Nuvio's AniSkip API integration with the official AniSkip API specification and ensures clean, correct array serialization.

## PR type

- [ ] Translation/localization only
- [x] Critical bug fix

## Why

The primary cause of the total failure to fetch skip times yesterday was a temporary outage of the `https://arm.haglund.dev/` mapping service. Because the mapping service was down, Nuvio could not resolve the IMDb ID to the MyAnimeList (MAL) ID needed to query AniSkip. Today, `arm.haglund.dev` is back online, restoring normal mapping and query flows.

However, during investigation, we identified that Nuvio's `AniSkipApi` was using `@Query("types")` instead of `@Query("types[]")` in its Retrofit declaration. While the backend occasionally tolerates the non-standard `types` parameter under relaxed parsing environments, the official API specification, the official browser extension, and other community integrations explicitly define and expect array parameters in the `types[]` format.

Updating the query key to `types[]` officially aligns Nuvio's client implementation with the AniSkip API schema, standardizes query serialization, and mitigates any potential parser mismatches or strict parameter validation issues.

### Sources & References
- **Official AniSkip API Documentation**: [api.aniskip.com/api-docs](https://api.aniskip.com/api-docs)
- **Official AniSkip Browser Extension Source Code**: [lexesjan/typescript-aniskip-extension](https://github.com/lexesjan/typescript-aniskip-extension)
- **Community Implementation Example**: [Greasy Fork AniSkip Integration Script](https://greasyfork.org/tr/scripts/474147-aniskip/code)

## Issue or approval

Reported by the user via DM

## Reproduction steps

1. Play an anime episode (e.g., *Black Summoner* S1:E2, MAL ID: 47790).
2. Observe that the "Skip Opening" or "Skip Ending" buttons do not appear in the player because the AniSkip query fails.
3. Observe the network request targeting `https://api.aniskip.com/v2/skip-times/...` and verify that parameter keys are set to `types` instead of `types[]`.

- [ ] No UI change
- [ ] No behavior change
- [ ] UI changed only to fix a documented glitch/bug
- [x] Behavior changed only to fix a documented bug/regression
- [ ] UI change has explicit maintainer approval

- [x] This PR includes a linked issue, reproduction steps, and testing notes if it is a critical bug fix.
- [x] I listed the testing performed below.

## Scope boundaries

This PR is strictly focused on modifying the `@Query("types")` parameter to `@Query("types[]")` inside `SkipIntroApi.kt`. It does not contain any unrelated formatting, UI tweaks, or library upgrades.

## Testing

Tested successfully both locally and using live server requests:
1. **Automated Unit Testing**:
   - Created a local test suite `SkipIntroRepositoryTest.kt` to mock and verify that `getSkipIntervals` correctly formats and executes queries on `AniSkipApi`. Tests executed and passed successfully (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).
2. **Live Server Integration (curl)**:
   - Queried the live `api.aniskip.com` endpoint using `curl` with standard array brackets (`types[]`) for *Black Summoner* S1:E2:

     curl "https://api.aniskip.com/v2/skip-times/47790/2?types[]=op&types[]=ed&types[]=recap&types[]=mixed-op&types[]=mixed-ed&episodeLength=0"

## Summary

Resolves the three architectural items deferred from PR #44 because they touch files held by that cluster. Two parallel worktree agents, both running TDD + 100% coverage on changes.

### A1 — `LaunchOptions.to_pool_kwargs()` consolidation
Launch kwargs (~20 keys) were independently reconstructed at four sites; adding a new launch option required editing all four. New `LaunchOptions.to_pool_kwargs()` is the canonical producer and `LaunchOptions.from_launch_record()` translates a JSONL relaunch record. All four sites now funnel through it:
- `server/browser/lifecycle.py::browser_launch`
- `server/browser/lifecycle.py::browser_quick_launch` (4th site discovered with the same ~20-key dict — folded in)
- `http/routes/sessions.py::session_launch` (22 lines → 4)
- `http/routes/sessions.py::_relaunch_kwargs_from_record` (35 lines → 1: `LaunchOptions.from_launch_record(launch).with_har_rotated().to_pool_kwargs()`)

### A6 — HAR rotation dedup
`next_har_path(x) if x else None` was open-coded at three sites. New `rotate_har_path(current)` helper in `launch_helpers.py` and `LaunchOptions.with_har_rotated()` method cover them: `pool.relaunch_fluid`, `lifecycle.handoff_browser`, `_relaunch_kwargs_from_record`.

### A7 — `bind_context` simplification
The launch-task-only contextvar binding in `BrowserSession.__post_init__` did less than the doc claimed — it only set context on the task that called `__post_init__`, and every subsequent tool call had to pass `instance_id=` explicitly anyway. Spans already carry the same info via attributes.

- Eviction-path unbind from `browser_pool/listeners.py`

Discovered three log sites that **were** implicitly relying on the binding (the AGENTS.md claim "the existing call sites already do" wasn't fully accurate). Added explicit `instance_id=` to:

author: icellan
body:
## Summary

The `cleanupExcessStack()` helper (emits `OP_NIP` to balance the stack at the end of a public method) was gated behind a `hasDeserializeState` check, so it only ran for stateful methods that read **mutable** fields. A `StatefulSmartContract` subclass with **zero mutable fields** whose terminal method binds a readonly field leaves an excess stack item below the top-of-stack boolean → violates BSV CLEANSTACK → ARC rejects the spend with *"Script did not clean its stack"*.

This drops the `hasDeserializeState` term from the gate in **all seven compilers**, keeping the inner `depth > 1` guard so already-clean methods are byte-for-byte untouched.

Credit to external contributor **Elis Jackson** (`elisjackson@icloud.com`), whose draft **PR #45** (TypeScript source only) identified and fixed the bug. This PR supersedes #45 by porting the same fix to the remaining six tiers and adding the conformance fixture.

## Per-compiler status

| Tier | File | Change | Build | Conformance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TypeScript | `packages/runar-compiler/src/passes/05-stack-lower.ts` | drop `hasDeserializeState`, keep helper's inner `depth > 1` guard | ✅ | ✅ |
| Go | `compilers/go/codegen/stack.go` (×2 call sites) | drop `hasDeserializeState`, keep call-site `depth() > 1` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Rust | `compilers/rust/src/codegen/stack.rs` | drop `has_deserialize_state`, keep `depth() > 1` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Python | `compilers/python/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.py` (×2) | drop `has_deserialize_state`, keep `depth() > 1` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Zig | `compilers/zig/src/passes/stack_lower.zig` (×3) | drop `methodUsesDeserializeState` gate (helper keeps inner `depth <= 1` no-op); removed now-dead helper fn | ✅ | ✅ |
| Ruby | `compilers/ruby/lib/runar_compiler/codegen/stack.rb` (×2) | drop `has_deserialize_state`, keep `depth > 1` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Java | `compilers/java/src/main/java/runar/compiler/passes/StackLower.java` | drop `hasDeserializeState`, keep `depth() > 1` | ✅ | ✅ |

(Note: CLAUDE.md lists `compilers/zig/src/codegen/stack.zig`; the actual Zig stack-lowering file is `compilers/zig/src/passes/stack_lower.zig`.)

## New conformance fixture

`conformance/tests/all-readonly-cleanstack/` — the "all-readonly stateful" CLEANSTACK repro: a `StatefulSmartContract` with one readonly `owner: PubKey` and a terminal `claim(sig)` that binds the readonly field (`ownerCopy = this.owner`) and asserts `checkSig(sig, this.owner)`. The unconsumed binding leaves a residual stack item; the fix emits the trailing `OP_NIP`.

- Source files added for all 9 formats (`ts/sol/move/go/rust/py/zig/rb/java`).
- Goldens (`expected-ir.json`, `expected-script.hex`) generated with the patched compiler.
- All **7 tiers produce byte-identical Stack-IR + script hex** (hex: `ab7b21…ad69007c00ac77`).
- All 7 parsers parse all 9 formats cleanly (parser-only matrix: 9/9 per tier).

## Existing goldens — IMPORTANT deviation from the issue's expectation

The issue states the fix should be a no-op for the existing corpus. That turned out to be **not quite true**: two existing fixtures carried the **same latent CLEANSTACK bug** and their goldens were regenerated:

- `conformance/tests/if-else/expected-script.hex` — `…00a0` → `…00a077` (gains one `OP_NIP`)
- `conformance/tests/if-without-else-multi-temp/expected-script.hex` — gains `OP_NIP`s inside branches

Both are stateless `SmartContract` methods whose old bytecode ended with stack depth > 1 (e.g. `if-else` ended on `OP_GREATERTHAN` with a leftover param underneath) — i.e. they would have been rejected on mainnet for the **identical** reason as #44. The previous goldens were therefore **incorrect** (emitting CLEANSTACK-violating bytecode); the fix repairs them. All 7 tiers agree on the new goldens, in both fold-OFF and fold-ON modes. PR #45's "byte-identical for the example corpus" claim was based on informal artifact checks, not a conformance golden regeneration.

Every **other** existing fixture is byte-identical (no leftover stack → `depth > 1` guard makes the new code a no-op).

## Verification

- **Full multi-format conformance (fold-OFF):** `549 passed, 0 failed` (60 fixtures × 9 formats × 7 tiers), against regenerated goldens.
- **Fold-ON cross-tier parity** for `if-else`, `if-without-else-multi-temp`, `all-readonly-cleanstack`: 9/9 each, all 7 tiers.
- **Parser-only matrix** for the new fixture: 9/9 per tier.
- All 7 compilers build clean; Go + Rust compiler unit tests pass.

## Divergences / notes

- **No tier diverges.** All 7 produce byte-identical output for the new fixture and the two repaired fixtures. No faked goldens.
- The Rust DSL frontend infers `StatefulSmartContract` from `#[runar::stateful_contract]` (or a non-readonly field). An all-readonly contract using `#[runar::contract]` is parsed as **stateless** — so the Rust fixture uses `#[runar::stateful_contract]` to match the other tiers. (Pre-existing frontend behavior, not changed by this PR.)

Closes #44
