## Summary

Second of four Stage 3 headline features. Adds customer and
vendor credit notes — the audit-trail-preserving way to reverse
part or all of a posted invoice without rewriting history. The
posting direction reverses at post time (XOR over is_bill +
is_credit_note); a new ``apply_credit_note`` tool nets posted
credit notes against posted invoices/bills from the same owner
without moving cash.

**Five commits, themed:**

1. **Copilot PR #86 follow-up fixes** (commit 0, ``306852e``) —
   the six actionable findings from Copilot's post-merge review:
   ``_gate_owner_type`` fails fast on typos instead of silently
   coercing; new test for ``_gate_owner_type('employee')``
   rejection; two stale "all 87 tools" docstrings refreshed; a
   ``_doc_label_for(owner_type)`` helper replaces the binary
   "Bill if is_bill else Invoice" pattern that mislabeled
   vouchers as bills; "Invoice/bill not found" → "Document not
   found" before the lookup tells us which type.
2. **Slot infrastructure + conventions** (``37b4aab``) — slot
   helpers for ``credit-note`` (GnuCash native) and ``gnc-mcp/
   applies-to-invoice`` (our namespaced linkage); ``_slot_value_
   str`` hoisted to ``_base.py`` so business and admin both pull
   from the shared utility; ``_invoice_to_dict`` extended to
   surface ``is_credit_note`` and ``applies_to`` keys when set;
   CLAUDE.md documents the bare-vs-namespaced slot key principle
3. **Create / add entry / delete** (``d3c5d39``) — three new
   tools (``create_credit_note``, ``add_credit_note_entry``,
   ``delete_credit_note``) with explicit ``is-a-credit-note``
   validation. Employee credit notes deliberately excluded
   (GnuCash desktop has no UI for them — supporting them at
   the MCP layer would create documents desktop users can't
   view). Source linking validates customer/vendor + currency
   match against the source invoice.
4. **Posting reversal + apply netting** (``2a8a6b9``) — XOR
   sign flip in ``post_invoice`` / ``pay_invoice`` so customer
   credit notes post like vendor bills and vice versa. New
   ``apply_credit_note`` tool books a two-split netting
   transaction on the shared A/R or A/P account (no cash
   moves) — GnuCash desktop's "Process Payment with both
   checked" workflow factored into a dedicated LLM-facing tool.
   Audit log polymorphism handler swaps entity_type for
   credit-note responses.
5. **Display polish** (``3650771``) — ``(CN)`` tags in
   ``list_invoices`` / ``get_outstanding_invoices``; "credit
   available" replaces "X days past due" in the action column
   for credit notes; ``is_credit_note`` surfaces in verbose
   output. Dashboard A/R / A/P totals already netted credit
   notes correctly (raw balance arithmetic does the right
   thing); locked with a regression test.

**Tool count:** 95 (was 91; +4 credit-note tools).

author: jpoley
body:
Supersedes closed #34.

## Problem
Closed PR #34 (multi-tool transcripts: Claude + Codex + Copilot) received Copilot review feedback:
1. `findCopilotSessionFile()` builds a path from a request-provided session id — possible path traversal.
2. `listCodexSessions()` reads every `rollout-*.jsonl` fully into memory to extract a few metadata fields and a message count.
3. `listCopilotSessions()` reads each session JSONL entirely to compute `messageCount` / `firstPrompt`.

## Approach
**Comment #1 (path traversal): already covered.** `findCopilotSessionFile()` already calls `isSafeSessionId(sessionId)` (added in commit `1d3ac8b`), which rejects path separators and `..`. Regression tests exist at `tests/lib/transcripts.test.ts` (finders return null for unsafe ids). No change made.

**Comments #2 / #3 (eager full-file reads): fixed by streaming.** Both listers now read each session file line-by-line via `readline.createInterface(createReadStream(...))` instead of `readFile` + `split("\n")`. This is the "read incrementally" option from the review. The two other suggested options were considered and rejected as out of scope:
- *Stop early once `firstPrompt` is found* — incompatible with counting all messages.
- *Defer `messageCount` to the detail view* — `messageCount` is rendered in the list UI (`app/analytics/transcripts/page.tsx`), so deferring it would change the UI contract.

Observable output (`firstPrompt`, `messageCount`, metadata) is unchanged; the parsers (`parseCodexJsonl` / `parseCopilotJsonl`) and the Codex `findCodexSessionFile` fallback are untouched. Honest scope note: peak per-file memory drops, but wall-clock listing time is roughly unchanged for typical-size JSONLs — the dominant cost for a large session store is the file count, not bytes per file.

Diff is 28 insertions / 12 deletions across the two provider files; every changed line traces to a Copilot comment.

## Test evidence
Run in a fresh worktree after `git merge origin/main` (trivial add/add conflicts in `docs/building/transcript-formats.md` and the task-006 backlog file resolved in favor of this branch's current state).

- **Unit (`bun run test`)**: transcripts suite 7/7 pass.
- **Build (`bun run build`)**: passes (both-mode compile; no Dockerfile/runtime change).
- **E2E (`bun run test:e2e`)**: 30 pass serially; 2 pre-existing failures (`navigation → settings page`, `terminal → component exists`) confirmed identical with this PR's edits stashed — unrelated to `lib/transcripts/*`. The transcripts/API specs pass.
- **Typecheck (`bun run typecheck`)**: 42 errors — all in `tests/testcontainers/*` (missing `@testcontainers/*` modules), pre-existing on `origin/main`. Zero in transcript files.
- **Lint (`bun run lint`)**: 11 errors, all in unrelated UI files, pre-existing on `origin/main`. Zero in transcript files.
- **Format (`bun run format:check`)**: 170 files flagged including these two (which were already prettier-dirty on `origin/main` — verified by stash). The added lines are prettier-clean; reformatting the rest would be an out-of-scope drive-by across 168 unrelated files.

The lint / typecheck / format / e2e baseline failures pre-date this PR (verified by stashing this PR's edits and re-running). This PR introduces zero new violations or test failures.

## Validation
Producer: Claude Opus 4.7. Validator: pending cross-provider (Codex) review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---
## Follow-up (this fresh PR)
- Commit `3b62d01`: added a non-object guard (`if (!entry || typeof entry !== "object") continue;`) after `JSON.parse` in both streaming listers, so a valid-JSON-but-non-object line (literal `null`, number, string) is skipped per-line instead of throwing and dropping the entire session. Transcript unit tests 7/7.

## Validation
- Producer: Claude Opus 4.7. Validator: Codex (GPT-5.x, cross-provider, read-only).
- Codex verdict: initial CONCERNS on malformed-line handling; resolved by `3b62d01`. Streaming + path-traversal guard PASS.
- Note: opened fresh (prior fresh PR #36 closed) because the branch received a follow-up commit — per operator policy a changed branch gets a new PR, not an update.


---
## Round 2 (Copilot review fixes) — commit de9eec1
- `lib/transcripts/codex.ts` — exact session-id match (`endsWith(`-${sessionId}.jsonl`)`, rejects substrings); `readFirstLine()` stream helper on the fallback path (no more full-file read).
- `lib/transcripts/copilot.ts` — `messageCount` now mirrors `parseCopilotJsonl` (assistant non-empty + tool requests + tool results); test asserts list count === detail message count.
- `docs/building/transcript-formats.md` — rewritten to the actual `TranscriptSession`/`TranscriptMessage` model and detail-route wrapper.
- backlog `task-006` final-summary corrected via `backlog task edit` (no hand-edit) — removes the "Shipped in PR #34" wording, notes #34 superseded.
- Transcripts unit tests 9/9; gates clean on changed files. Opened fresh (prior PR closed) per policy.
- Known separate item (not raised by Copilot, deferred to avoid scope creep): a smaller Codex list-vs-parser messageCount mismatch.


---
## Round 3 (Copilot review) — commit ca0e670
- `lib/transcripts/codex.ts` — session id now derives from the rollout filename uuid (`uuidFromRolloutName`) when `session_meta` is missing, so detail links resolve via the round-2 exact-suffix match; uuid-less filenames are skipped rather than listed with a broken link.
- `messageCount` aligned to `parseCodexJsonl` (role user/assistant + non-empty text), matching the detail view; test asserts list count === parsed messages length.
- Transcripts unit tests 12/12; gates clean on changed files. Opened fresh (prior PR closed) per policy.


---
## Round 4 (Copilot review) — commit a725d79d
- `lib/transcripts/copilot.ts` + `codex.ts` — wrapped `createReadStream`+`readline` iteration in try/finally with `rl.close()` + `stream.destroy()` (no fd leak on stream/parse exception) in both listers.
- `copilot.ts` — validate the filename-derived uuid with `isSafeSessionId()` before the `workspace.yaml` path join (traversal guard); skip unsafe entries. Codex side: untrusted `session_meta.payload.id` override accepted only if it passes `isSafeSessionId()`. Test added for the unsafe-filename skip.
- Transcripts unit tests 13/13; gates clean on changed files. Opened fresh per policy.

body:
This pull request introduces a new local Room schema for "Goals" and "Goal Allocations" and removes legacy Notification and Savings tables and related DAOs from the codebase. It also updates the Gradle configuration to address Kotlin compatibility and removes some unused dependencies. The changes modernize the database layer, streamline dependency injection, and prepare the app for new goal-tracking features.

**Database schema and DAO changes:**

* Added new entities `GoalEntity` and `GoalAllocationEntity` for local Room storage, along with their DAOs (`GoalDao`, `GoalAllocationDao`), enabling local CRUD operations and reactive flows for goals and their allocations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d441a20ea491670123cc103771c073290e74cf093589ce06b07d3f3e0a5d735eR1-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e54d7bf81faf1dcb1de0f1177e499cdf4874fd1a0c72efc8c751c036c8422eb4R1-R16) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5909309adce81f017ffc98e9dfe7ec1e1ce06d0d3b2f7a1be28651412e2f3743R1-R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-025550f511bb9f283d622adbb3eee0d55d6f2a5d19398ccd17d8ec7549ab949eR1-R17)
* Updated `AppDatabase` to register the new entities and DAOs, and removed all Notification and Savings-related entities and DAOs from the schema.
* Refactored `DatabaseModule` to provide the new DAOs and removed all Notification and Savings DAO providers and migration logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f55585e8dc60edcbfd71335a82359720ac23d32408f0c24599c1f8263898dd3eL5-L12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f55585e8dc60edcbfd71335a82359720ac23d32408f0c24599c1f8263898dd3eL28-L140) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f55585e8dc60edcbfd71335a82359720ac23d32408f0c24599c1f8263898dd3eL151-R47)

**Remote data and model improvements:**

* Added `GoalFirebaseService` for managing goals and allocations in Firestore, supporting CRUD operations and real-time flows for allocations.
* Updated the `Expense` model to use Firestore property names for boolean fields and clarified its domain context. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d3db590a21f78339d6b6b3cdd118b985f15cbfc348222477cf14512632e0b3b8R6-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d3db590a21f78339d6b6b3cdd118b985f15cbfc348222477cf14512632e0b3b8L17-R21)
* Improved type references in `ExpenseUiState` for clarity and maintainability.

**Build configuration updates:**

* Added a workaround in `build.gradle.kts` to force Kotlin language/api version to 1.9, preventing KAPT issues with Kotlin 2.0, and removed unused dependencies (WorkManager, Firebase Storage, Hilt Work, Coil). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-84f2c14f998c89e8d843a06d997c3c8672c63da7560902b9b3fee0aca6f917fbR70-R76) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-84f2c14f998c89e8d843a06d997c3c8672c63da7560902b9b3fee0aca6f917fbL123-L125) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-84f2c14f998c89e8d843a06d997c3c8672c63da7560902b9b3fee0aca6f917fbL143-L151) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-84f2c14f998c89e8d843a06d997c3c8672c63da7560902b9b3fee0aca6f917fbL197) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-84f2c14f998c89e8d843a06d997c3c8672c63da7560902b9b3fee0aca6f917fbL12)

These changes lay the foundation for robust local and remote goal management, clean up unused legacy code, and ensure compatibility with the latest Kotlin tooling.

author: vaibhav701161
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing create/edit UI for VK-level blocked models and fixes runtime enforcement for provider-prefixed model names.

The previous VK blocked-model support had backend storage, API handling, runtime hooks, and read-only display, but the create/edit sheet did not expose the `Blocked Models` editor. This PR adds that missing UI field and also fixes an enforcement issue found during E2E testing: the UI stores selected models as `provider/model`, while the governance resolver could compare against bare model names. Because of that mismatch, blocked models could bypass the VK blacklist in some request paths.

## Changes

* Added editable `Blocked Models` field in the VK create/edit provider config section.

  * Placed between `Allowed Models` and `Allowed Keys`.
  * Uses the same `ModelMultiselect` pattern as the allowed models field.
  * Adds `blacklisted_models` to the zod schema.
  * Initializes edit mode with `config.blacklisted_models || []`.
  * Defaults new provider configs to `blacklisted_models: []`.

* Added prefix-aware blocked-model matching in governance.

  * Added `isModelBlockedByList()` to handle both bare and provider-prefixed model names.
  * This prevents bypasses where the UI stores `ollama/mistral:latest`, but the runtime request is evaluated as `mistral:latest`, or the other way around.

* Updated VK runtime enforcement paths to use the prefix-aware matcher:

  * `plugins/governance/resolver.go`
  * `plugins/governance/main.go`
  * `plugins/governance/utils.go`

Design decision:

* The fix keeps the existing `schemas.BlackList` behavior intact and adds a small VK-specific helper for prefix-aware comparison.
* Provider-key behavior is unchanged.

## Type of change

* [x] Bug fix
* [x] Feature
* [ ] Refactor
* [ ] Documentation
* [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

* [ ] Core (Go)
* [ ] Transports (HTTP)
* [ ] Providers/Integrations
* [x] Plugins
* [x] UI (React)
* [ ] Docs

## How to test

Build checks:

```sh
go build -o ./tmp/bifrost-http ./transports/bifrost-http

cd ui
npm run build
```

Local server:

```sh
./tmp/bifrost-http -port 9090
```

Open:

```sh
http://localhost:9090/workspace/governance/virtual-keys
```

UI validation:

1. Open Governance → Virtual Keys.
2. Create or edit a virtual key.
3. Expand a provider config.
4. Confirm the field order is:

   * Allowed Models
   * Blocked Models
   * Allowed Keys
5. Select a blocked model and save.
6. Reopen the virtual key and confirm the blocked model is still selected.
7. Open the details sheet and confirm the blocked model is displayed.

E2E validation with local Ollama:

* Blocked bare model: `403 model_blocked`
* Blocked provider-prefixed model: `403 model_blocked`
* Allowed bare model: `200 OK`
* Allowed provider-prefixed model: `200 OK`
* Same model in allowlist and blocklist: `403 model_blocked`
* Empty blocklist: `200 OK`
* Wildcard blocklist `["*"]`: all tested models return `403 model_blocked`
* UI-created VK also works end-to-end with the same blocked/allowed behavior

## Screenshots/Recordings

Added/available recording showing the `Blocked Models` field in the VK provider config create/edit flow.



Uploading Screen Recording 2026-05-25 003101.mp4…

* [x] No

BF-896

## Security considerations

This improves VK-level governance by ensuring blocked models are actually enforced for both bare and provider-prefixed model strings.

No secrets, provider keys, auth tokens, or PII are exposed or stored by this change. Provider-key behavior is unchanged.

## PROFIT-PRIORS-003 — pin existing behavior for two series surfaced by audit

The v0.30.10 miss-pattern audit (goal "build upon PR #42 to identify additional areas...") found 39 historical fail-safe-mode BDs across 5 series. Of those:

- **3 series** (KXTXRUNOFFENDORSE / KXUSAIRANAGREEMENT / KXNEWTARIFFS) already have explicit priors from PR #40 / v0.30.8.
- **2 series** (KXCHINAANNOUNCE / KXNEWDEAL) have NO explicit prior. They fall through to PR #41's `_time_prior` default, which already produces the correct (0.65, 0.25, 0.10) shape.

This PR makes the 2 series explicit. Same shape as the existing event-driven political cluster.

## Why pin behavior that's already correct?

1. **Pinned in tests.** `test_event_driven_political_priors_are_fast_dominant` + `test_new_categorical_priors_clear_g4_threshold` now include both series. A future refactor that changes `_time_prior` default cannot silently regress these markets.
2. **Operator visibility.** The `_SERIES_PRIORS` table is the canonical "markets we trade." Implicit defaults aren't discoverable.
3. **Drift protection.** If the default ever changes (e.g. tightened back to interpretation-dominant), these series stay anchored.

## Markets affected

| Series | Currently active | Sample market |
|---|---:|---|
| KXCHINAANNOUNCE | 0 (cycle retired today) | historical: announcement events |
| KXNEWDEAL | 1 | "When will Trump announce a new trade deal?" |

## Audit closure note (full goal table)

| PR | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| A — widen fallback heuristic | ❌ no PR | Sweep `\|p-0.5\| < 0.10` yielded only +1 G1-flip across 151 historical BDs. Conditional clause ("If 23 normal-mode failures decrease meaningfully") not met. |
| **B — fail-safe-mode prior audit** | ✅ **this PR** | 5 series surfaced. 3 already pinned. 2 added explicit. |
| C — MATCH_SUPPRESSED audit | ❌ no PR | 8,647 events are 100% legitimate noise rejection. 82% single-token "china" → macro markets. MATCH-001 B' working as designed. |
| D — no_keywords audit | ❌ no PR (different workstream) | 992 rejections trace to LLM returning `magnitude='none'` 91% of analyzed news. Analyzer code is correct. The lever is the LLM prompt — T2 scope per IC §16, requires replay-CI gate before deploy. |

## Risk

- **Pure pinning change.** Runtime behavior identical (default fallback already produces same shape).
- No env mutation. No threshold changes. No G1-G6 changes.
- Bot picks up changes on next launchd restart but doesn't NEED a restart — behavior is unchanged from operator's perspective.

## Tests

\`pytest tests/\`: **2259 passed** / 4 skipped / 71 xfailed. Ruff: clean.

Phase 3 framework activation remains paused. (Recommendation deferred until operator-prompted; not opening a Phase 3 PR off this goal.)

author: r3beam
body:
### Motivation
- Añadir un pipeline de selección de variables tipo Wrapper sobre el dataset one-hot (`final_dataset_ohe`) para generar un dataset derivado sin alterar el original.
- Evaluar variables numéricas relevantes para el target proxy `sales_drop_risk` mediante una selección automática con validación cruzada.
- Proveer trazabilidad y evidencia en el notebook sobre el modelo y la métrica usadas para la selección.

### Description
- Se agregó una nueva celda en `Evaluacion_2.ipynb` que crea una copia de trabajo `wrapper_base = final_dataset_ohe.copy()` y construye `X`/`y` a partir de las columnas numéricas y el target `sales_drop_risk`.
- Se implementó `RFECV` (Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation) usando `LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=42)` como estimador y `StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)` para el CV, con `scoring='f1'` y `min_features_to_select=5`.
- El resultado es el nuevo dataset `final_dataset_ohe_wrapper` que contiene únicamente las variables seleccionadas por RFECV más la columna target `sales_drop_risk`, y se imprimen: el nombre del modelo, la métrica y la cantidad final de variables.
- Además se incluyeron en el notebook pasos de preprocesado/EDA y filtros estadísticos (p. ej. `VarianceThreshold`) y análisis de asociaciones categóricas (Cramér's V), manteniendo `final_dataset_ohe` sin modificaciones directas.

### Testing
- Se ejecutó el script que añadió la nueva celda al notebook (`python` one-liner que inserta el bloque de código) y la ejecución del script finalizó correctamente. (éxito)
- Se verificó la presencia del bloque insertado buscando referencias claves (`RFECV`, `final_dataset_ohe_wrapper`, `Modelo utilizado`, `scoring='f1'`) dentro de `Evaluacion_2.ipynb` y se localizaron las líneas esperadas. (éxito)

author: anchapin
body:
## Summary

Implement night ventilation for high-mass (6R2C) model path, fixing Issue #824.

### Problem
- Night ventilation was correctly implemented in step_physics_5r1c for low-mass cases (600FF/650FF)
- But the same logic was **missing** from step_physics_6r2c for high-mass cases (900FF/950FF)
- This caused 950FF to show +9C higher max temperature than 900FF (ventilation was heating the zone instead of cooling it)

### Fix
Added h_ve_night calculation to step_physics_6r2c:
- When night ventilation is active (18:00-07:00), adds ~571 W/K to derived_h_ext
- This makes the zone air temperature track outdoor conditions during ventilation hours
- Night ventilation now works consistently across both 5R1C and 6R2C model paths

### Test Results
- All 13 ASHRAE 140 free-floating tests pass
- test_night_ventilation_effect now passes (950FF max temp is within 2C of 900FF)

### Notes
- Case 195 test failure is **pre-existing** and unrelated to these changes

**FINAL PR of the canonical-pivot sprint.** P.1.B SHIP-LIFT-ONLY: 6 new citizen-facing canonical indicators land on `datasets/energy/` plus +12 catalogue rows, +5 source ledger rows, +2 facet axes. Renderers continue to resolve the affected indicators via the legacy shard path; canonical rows are **additive** and only become citizen-visible when the frontend allowlist is extended (deferred to subsequent P.1.B Phase B PR, mirroring the P.1.A C5+C6 strangler-fig pattern).

## What lands

**`energy_distribution_performance.parquet`** (700 → 2889 rows):

author: raphaelfh
body:
## Summary

Adds two finer-grained coverage gates on top of the existing global ratchet (`--cov-fail-under=62`), so we catch regressions the ratchet alone can't see — without ever lowering the existing floor.

**1. Diff coverage gate** (PR only, hard fail)
- Lines a PR introduces must be ≥ `PRUMO_DIFF_COVERAGE_MIN` (default 80).
- Catches the "ship 500 LOC of new code with 200 covered" case the 62% global gate would let through.
- Runs `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/\${base_ref}`.
- Renders markdown summary into `\$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

**2. Critical-path coverage gate** (every run, hard fail)
- Modules in [`backend/.coverage_critical`](backend/.coverage_critical) aggregate to ≥ `PRUMO_CRITICAL_COVERAGE_MIN` (default 85).
- "Critical" = bug there means data loss, BOLA, or HITL state corruption.
- Today's list: TOCTOU lock helper (100%), HITL session opener (95%), run lifecycle (92%), review service (89%), coord coherence (88%), proposal repo (83%), proposal service (81%), auth deps (64%). Aggregate: **89%** (snapshot 2026-05-24).
- `extraction_consensus_service.py` (34%) **excluded** with explicit TODO — needs a dedicated test PR before joining the list, otherwise it would crater the aggregate.

**3. Global ratchet preserved** (`--cov-fail-under=62`, hard rule "never lower once raised"). Diff and critical-path coexist with it, not replace it.

Pattern follows 2026 industry default ("Clean as You Code" — SonarCloud, Codecov, GitHub Code Coverage Action).

## What this unblocks

The Railway "Wait for CI" gate currently SKIPS deploys when coverage dips below the global ratchet on \`main\`. Diff coverage now catches the dip on the PR (where it can be fixed) before it lands. Once merged, fewer false-SKIPs on the Railway side — no more \`railway up\` manual fallback for coverage-related blocks.

## Test plan

- [x] `coverage report --include=\$(.coverage_critical) --fail-under=85` → exit 0 (aggregate 89%).
- [x] Same gate with `--fail-under=92` → exit 2 (correctly fails when threshold above current).
- [x] `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/main` against empty diff → exit 0 ("No lines with coverage information in this diff").
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit -q` → 454 passed, 5 xfailed.
- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` → valid YAML.
- [ ] On this PR's first CI run, verify: (a) the diff coverage step appears in the PR view's \`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\`, (b) the critical-path step prints the aggregate report, (c) both gates exit cleanly because this PR doesn't add executable Python.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — two new steps in `backend-test` job; explanatory comment block above the existing ratchet.
- `backend/pyproject.toml` — `diff-cover>=10.0` added to `[project.optional-dependencies].dev`.
- `backend/.coverage_critical` — curated list + per-file rationale.
- `docs/architecture/deployment.md` — "What CI gates the deploy on" replaces stale "Current constraint" block.
- `.gitignore` — `coverage.json` + `diff-coverage.md` excluded from version control.

## Out of scope (separate PRs)

1. Raise `extraction_consensus_service.py` coverage from 34% to ≥80%, then add to `.coverage_critical`.
2. Next global ratchet bump (62 → 70%) once F4 (repos/services unit tests) lands. After F4, evaluate adopting `--cov-branch`.

author: edwallitt
body:
Two rounds of work on the job board, folded into one branch.

## Round 1 — simplification

Collapsed redundant signals on the row: dropped the Min-class column, the separate Pay column, the Flags letters (F/W/U/M/S/X/P/C), and the FitLegend strip. Result is **8 columns instead of 11**, with `$/hr` as the primary number and contract pay as a caption underneath. Class + Payload merged into a single Load cell (payload · class · optional unpaved pill). Fit-column header gets a tooltip carrying the legend so removing the strip didn't strand the glossary. The grouping/batching heuristic is gone — clever solution to a flooding problem that doesn't happen in practice.

Filters: `flyableOnly` + `atMyLocationOnly` + `classFilter` collapsed into a single 3-way **Origin segmented control** (At <ICAO> / Flyable / All). Ferry dropped from the role filter — it's a job type, not a career role, and shows inline with its own visual tag. Header urgency tally chips removed (urgency was already on every row and on the recommendation pill). Last-tick + Force-tick readouts hidden behind `?dev=1`.

New `RecommendedJobCard` surfaces the server's `recommendedJobId` pick above the table so the answer to "what should I fly next?" lands before the alternatives.

## Round 2 — make the recommendation honest and aware

**Net pay/hour.** `computeJobFit` now takes fuel prices + per-aircraft fuel burn + rental rate, computes `(pay − fuel − rental) / hours`, and returns `netPayHourCents` alongside `payHourCents` on every fit. Rentals charge wet-rate × hours and zero fuel (it's included in the rate); owned aircraft charge fuel-at-player-airport × burn × hours. Falls back to gross when the fuel-price map is cold-started. `priceFerryLeg` in `shared/jobs` handles the ferry branch with the same pricing definition. Sort uses net (with gross fallback). Cell tooltip shows the cost breakdown so the player can see why net is below gross.

**Active-job awareness.** `listWithReachability` now returns an `activeJob` summary when the player is mid-flight, and `pickRecommendedJobId` pivots to the destination airport so the recommendation answers "what should I take when I land?" instead of pretending the player is free. New `ActiveJobBanner` renders above the recommendation card with the active job's id, route, client, ETA, and a link to `/current`. Card caption switches to "best $/hr from CYQM (after arrival)" and — importantly — shows **gross** $/hr under pivot, because the fit's `netPayHourCents` bakes in a phantom reposition leg the player isn't actually paying for (they're flying it as the active job).

**URL-persisted filters.** `?origin=`, `?role=`, `?sort=key:dir` survive reloads, are shareable, and let the Atlas deep-link land on a pre-filtered view. URL is the source of truth; React state is derived via `useMemo`. Defaults are stripped from the URL to keep it short.

**Visual trims.** Urgency column folded into Window text color (one signal, one place). "to expire" sub-caption removed (header already says Window). Fit-reason caption hidden when the row is `ready` (no actionable signal there).

## Verification

- `pnpm test`: **832 passed** (shared 248 / server 259 / web 325). New unit suites for `RecommendedJobCard` and `ActiveJobBanner`; new `computeJobFit` cases for net pay/hr (rental vs owned, fuel-price cold-start fallback, $0/hr floor, wont_fit / locked); new `pickRecommendedJobId` pivot test; new `jobBoard.ts` test that splices an in-flight career row and asserts the pivot picks the CYQM job over a higher-paying CYHZ one.
- `pnpm build`: server `tsc --noEmit` clean, web `tsc -b` clean, vite build clean.

## What's not in this PR

- Browser pass for the new strip stack — eyeballing how the ActiveJobBanner (sky/emerald) sits above the amber-tinted RecommendedJobCard above the amber-tinted FuelShockBanner when all three are present at once.
- ETA in the banner currently formats as `Mon 24 May 14:30`; relative time (`in 1h 23m`) would match the Window column's idiom but felt outside this scope.

body:
## Summary
First protection layer for this fork. Mirrors the generic-hooks subset of [yotamleo/himmel](https://github.com/yotamleo/himmel)'s `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — drops himmel-specific guards (HIMMEL-N validation, Atlassian MCP plugin enforcement) since they don't apply here.

Tracker: yotamleo/himmel HIMMEL-120 (protection-parity sweep).

## What's wired
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — pre-commit-hooks v5.0.0, shellcheck-py v0.10.0.1 (severity=error), gitleaks v8.21.2, plus 3 local hooks:
  - `worktree-isolation` (pre-commit) — refuses commits on `main`
  - `conventional-commit-msg` (commit-msg) — enforces `type(scope?): subject` format; allows `Merge`/`Revert` passthrough
  - `no-push-to-main` (pre-push) — refuses any push whose remote ref is `refs/heads/main`
- `scripts/hooks/check-*.sh` — three inline hook scripts (no external guardrails-lib dependency; each fail-closed on internal errors)
- `.gitattributes` — forces LF on `*.sh|*.bash|*.md|*.yml|*.yaml|*.json|*.js`. CRLF in bash scripts breaks Linux/macOS (literal `\r` in variable values, ANSI escapes, etc.)
- `.gitignore` — adds `/.claude/worktrees`, `/.claude/settings.local.json`, `.env`, `.env.*`
- `CLAUDE.md` — workflow rules + install steps + `core.autocrlf=false` instruction for Windows operators

## CRLF fix
`bin/statusline.sh` had Windows line endings; converted to LF via `sed -i 's/\r$//'`. With `.gitattributes` + `mixed-line-ending` hook in place, this can't regress without the pre-commit framework catching it.

## CR hardening (2nd commit, post-review)
Heavy CR (4 parallel reviewers) caught three real silent-failure issues:
1. `check-conventional-commit-msg.sh` didn't strip trailing `\r` from CRLF commit messages — would have wrongly rejected `Merge branch 'main'\r` subjects produced by Windows editors with `--cleanup=verbatim`. Fixed.
2. Same script didn't strip `#`-prefixed comments — would have validated a comment as the subject under `--cleanup=verbatim`. Added `git stripspace --strip-comments`.
3. `check-push-target.sh` silently passed malformed pre-push stdin lines (fewer than 4 fields) because `remote_ref` ended up empty. Now fail-closed with the offending values logged.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv tool run pre-commit run --all-files` — all 8 pre-commit-stage hooks pass on the full file tree (mixed-line-ending also auto-fixed `install.js`/`LICENSE`/`package.json`/`README.md` to LF)
- [x] `shellcheck --severity=error` on all hook scripts AND on `bin/statusline.sh` + `test/test_cache.sh` post-CRLF-fix: clean
- [x] All 3 hooks smoke-tested with happy path + edge cases (CRLF subject, Merge passthrough w/ CRLF, comment-on-line-1, malformed pre-push line, empty stdin, main-push refusal)
- [ ] Run `bin/statusline.sh` post-conversion on Linux to confirm CRLF strip didn't break runtime (CR flagged as verification gap — manual smoke test deferred to post-merge; statusline output unchanged on Windows)

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The app returns 404 at the root path despite a successful React build. Express is silently failing to serve the static files, and the catch-all route calls `res.sendFile` on `index.html` without checking whether the file actually exists, so there is no signal in the logs about what is going wrong.

## Solution

Added `fs` import and two startup log lines that print the resolved `clientDist` path and whether the directory exists on disk. The catch-all route now checks for `index.html` before calling `sendFile` — if the file is missing it logs the full path via `console.error` and returns a 404 with a descriptive message showing the resolved `clientDist` value, making the root cause immediately visible in the deploy logs.

### Changes
- **Modified** `server/src/index.js`

author: danmestas
body:
## Summary

One-line operator note in the migrating-to-synadia skill: the channel-loading flag named in the "Why" bullet is hidden from `claude --help` output, but is still accepted by claude's parser. Without this note, anyone debugging the orch-spawn → channel-plugin path who greps the help output will find nothing and assume the flag was removed.

## Empirical validation (2026-05-24, claude 2.1.150)

```sh
# 1. Flag is missing from --help
$ claude --help 2>&1 | grep -c 'dangerously-load-development-channels'
0

# 2. Flag is still accepted by the parser
$ claude --dangerously-load-channels-TYPO foo --print --bare 'x'
error: unknown option '--dangerously-load-channels-TYPO'

$ claude --dangerously-load-development-channels foo --print --bare 'x'
Not logged in · Please run /login         # auth failure, NOT a flag-parse failure

# 3. orch-spawn passes it internally
$ grep -n 'dangerously-load-development-channels' cmd/orch/
cmd/orch/spawn_tmux.go:87:    wrap += ` --dangerously-load-development-channels 'plugin:nats-channel@synadia-plugins'`
```

## Backstory

I was originally going to ship a stale branch (`docs/skills-synadia-plugin-validated`) with two unrelated doc commits, but during validation discovered both commits were already on main via #183. While re-confirming the doc against current claude, I noticed the flag wasn't surfaced in `--help` and wrote this note. PR #218 closed in favor of this clean single-commit branch off current main.

## Test plan

- [x] `claude --help` output checked for the flag (verified absent)
- [x] Parser-accepts vs parser-rejects behavior differentiated (real flag passes through, typo errors)
- [x] orch-spawn source-line reference resolves to the current code
- [x] Version + date stamped in the note for future readers

author: jscott3201
body:
## Summary

CI spend triage 2026-05-24 — cuts per-PR billed minutes from ~75 to ~12 (~84% reduction; back inside Team free tier). No coverage loss.

| Change | Saves | Wall-clock | Risk |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Drop `macos-latest` from PR matrix → nightly + push:main + workflow_dispatch | ~55 billed-min/PR | 0 (off critical path) | Low — dev-host validation via local `cargo` pre-PR; nightly catches Linux-pass/macOS-fail drift inside 24h |
| Move `parse-fuzz` to nightly with 1h soak (vs 60s/PR floor) | ~5 billed-min/PR | -5 min from PR job graph | Low — same fuzz workload class, longer soak = better coverage |
| Path-gate `cargo-deny` / `cargo-audit` / `third-party-current` to dep-manifest changes | ~3 billed-min on ~90% of PRs | 0 | Low — these gates only matter when deps change |
| Swap `cargo test` → `cargo nextest run` (+ separate `cargo test --doc` for the 2 crates with doctests) | ~1.5 billed-min/PR | **~2 min off the slowest PR job** | Low — drop-in scheduler swap, faster failure reporting |
| Fix `parse-fuzz` cache key: `${{ github.run_id }}` → `hashFiles('corpus/positive/**/*.gql')` | trivial | trivial | Trivial — old key never hit exact, only restore-keys |

## PR-side topology (after)

| Job | Status |
|---|---|
| `changes` (paths-filter detection) | NEW — feeds `if:` of deps-gated jobs |
| `fmt`, `file-size-cap`, `no-secret-scan`, `bench-invocation-lint` | unchanged |
| `clippy (ubuntu-latest)` | macOS dropped |
| `test (ubuntu-latest)` | macOS dropped + nextest swap |
| `deny`, `audit`, `thirdparty-current` | skip unless `Cargo.lock` / `Cargo.toml` / `crates/*/Cargo.toml` / `deny.toml` / `about.{hbs,toml}` changed |
| ~~`parse-fuzz`~~ | moved to `nightly.yml` |

## Nightly workflow (`nightly.yml`, new)

- Triggers: `cron '30 6 * * *'` (06:30 UTC daily), `push: branches: [main]`, `workflow_dispatch`
- Jobs: `clippy-macos`, `test-macos` (mirrors PR test shape with nextest), `parse-fuzz` (1h soak, content-addressed cache key)

## Test plan

- [x] Both YAMLs parse cleanly (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`).
- [x] `bash .github/scripts/check-bench-invocation.sh .` clean (no false positive on `cargo nextest`).
- [x] No branch-protection rules on `main` (verified via `gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection`) → skipped jobs from path-gating don't block merge.
- [ ] First post-merge PR runs the new shape end-to-end — true validation lands when the next BRIEF opens its PR. Expect ~5-min wall-clock vs current ~7:30, ~12 billed-min vs current ~75.
- [ ] First nightly fires next morning (06:30 UTC); manual `workflow_dispatch` from Actions tab can verify immediately.

## Decision notes / open questions

- **macOS coverage policy:** moving macOS to nightly trades same-PR signal for ~24h nightly cadence + on-merge-to-main signal. Dev work runs `cargo clippy / test` locally on macOS pre-PR, so the local validation is the primary gate. If a Linux-pass/macOS-fail regression slips, nightly catches within hours.
- **nextest + doctests:** nextest doesn't run doctests; the separate `cargo test --workspace --locked --all-features --doc` pass preserves coverage. Only 2 crates (`selene-vector`, `selene-pack`) currently ship doctests so this is fast.
- **Path-filter scope:** the `deps` filter intentionally includes `crates/*/fuzz/Cargo.toml` and `about.{hbs,toml}` (the cargo-about config), not just the top-level lock. Catches dep-changes that wouldn't touch the root Cargo.toml.

## Summary

`claude plugin marketplace add jackson-video-resources/markov-hedge-fund-method` currently fails with:

```
Failed to parse marketplace file: plugins.0.source: Invalid input
```

The cause is `"source": "."` in [.claude-plugin/marketplace.json](.claude-plugin/marketplace.json). Per the [Claude Code plugin-marketplaces docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces.md#relative-paths), relative-path sources must start with `./`. Changing `"."` to `"./"` is the minimal fix and unblocks the marketplace for everyone trying to install via the documented flow.

Validated locally with `claude plugin validate .` — passes.

body:
## What
Add a public `register_model()` API plus the missing README usage docs, so users can add support for a device without forking the library.

## Why
Issue #34 asks "What is the process to add more lights to led_ble?" — today the only path is editing `model_db.py`/`const.py` and forking. Unrecognised devices fall back to the generic unknown-model protocol with no way to override the protocol, color modes, or description. There were also no usage examples in the README at all.

## How
- `register_model(model: LEDBLEModel) -> LEDBLEModel | None` adds or overrides an entry in `MODEL_MAP`/`MODELS` and returns the previously registered model (or `None`). Keeps both the lookup map and the ordered list consistent so `get_model()` resolves the custom entry.
- Exported `register_model`, `LEDBLEModel`, and `get_model` from the package root.
- README gains a **Usage** section (connect, on/off, set_rgb, brightness, effects, callbacks) and an **Adding support for a new device** section showing `register_model`, which directly answers #34.

Scope is intentionally narrow: this covers devices that speak a flux_led protocol. Devices needing a non-flux_led protocol or different GATT characteristics still aren't supported by registration alone — noted in the README.

Fixes four error-message contract inconsistencies surfaced by an E2E black-box sweep of the GitHub provider. All production changes are in `src/lib_python_projects/providers/github.py`; regression tests added/updated in `tests/test_github_errors.py`.

1. **`get_ticket` bare 404** — the ticket fetch now catches a 404 and re-raises `GitHubError(404, "ticket '<project>#<id>' not found")`, matching the `update_ticket` pattern. The comments sub-fetch is intentionally left unwrapped.

4. **Terse 422 in `create_pr`** — the `PullRequest.head (invalid)` 422 is now intercepted and re-raised naming the offending head branch with a "push it first" hint. All other 422s (e.g. "a pull request already exists") propagate unchanged.

body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @onyema3 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro autonomous agent](https://kiro.dev/autonomous-agent)</sub>

---
Fixes audit finding **H15 (High)**.

## Threat model

`Matrix_MLM_Core::process_ticket()` sanitises the incoming priority field with `sanitize_text_field()`, which strips HTML tags but **does not escape quotes**. A payload like

```
medium" onclick="alert(1)
```

survives the sanitiser intact, lands in `matrix_tickets.priority`, and fires on every admin page load — the admin ticket list iterates every row and emits the value into both a `class` attribute and text content (twice per row, once for priority, once for status). Stored XSS, member-to-admin, no foothold required beyond the ability to submit a support ticket. From there an attacker can pivot to admin session theft or CSRF against admin-only endpoints (deposit approval, balance adjustments, etc).

## Fix — two layers

**1. Render-side escaping (the universal fix).** Every echo of `$ticket->priority` / `$ticket->status` now goes through `esc_attr` in attribute contexts and `esc_html` in text contexts. `$ticket->id` is cast to `(int)` at every echo site. `home_url` / `admin_url` hrefs are wrapped in `esc_url`. `date()` output is wrapped in `esc_html` for consistency.

Sites covered:
- `includes/user/class-matrix-user-tickets.php` — user ticket list table
- `includes/admin/class-matrix-admin-tickets.php` — admin ticket list table + per-ticket meta header

**2. Write-side allow-listing (defense-in-depth).** Two chokepoints now coerce priority to `{low, medium, high, urgent}`:
- `Matrix_MLM_Core::process_ticket` (HTTP entry)
- `Matrix_MLM_Support::create_ticket` (DB chokepoint — protects every future caller including REST, programmatic, and importer reuse)

Unknown values fall back to `'medium'` rather than rejecting the submission, so a copy-pasted old form payload never surfaces as a user-facing error.

## What's not in this PR

- **Status is not allow-listed at write time.** It's set entirely server-side (`open` at create, `customer_reply` / `answered` at reply, `closed` at close), and the CSV importer (`process_tickets` in `class-matrix-admin-import.php`) already uses a cast-int allow-list. Render-side escape on status is sufficient defence against any historical garbage from pre-allow-list import paths.
- **No DB sweep of existing `priority` values.** Anything currently in the DB that's outside the allow-list would still render safely (escaped) but display as the literal string in the badge text. Existing rows are presumed clean (this is the first time process_ticket has been exploitable in this way) — but a one-shot `UPDATE matrix_tickets SET priority = 'medium' WHERE priority NOT IN ('low','medium','high','urgent')` is the right belt-and-braces if you want a clean slate, and is left as an operator decision.

## Tested

- `php -l` clean on all four modified files.
- Repo-wide grep for `echo $ticket->priority|status` and `echo $ticket` — zero remaining unescaped echo sites.
- Walk-through of the three render sites: user list, admin list, admin meta header. All field types (id, subject, priority, status, dates, hrefs) now go through the appropriate escaper.

## Files

- `includes/user/class-matrix-user-tickets.php`
- `includes/admin/class-matrix-admin-tickets.php`
- `includes/class-matrix-core.php`
- `includes/class-matrix-support.php`

author: bhurpeau
body:
## Résumé

Portage du simulateur UVA/Padova T1D de S2013 vers S2017, d'après :
> Visentin et al. (2018), *The UVA/Padova Type 1 Diabetes Simulator Goes From Single Meal to Single Day*, J Diabetes Sci Technol 12(2):273-281.

Le flag par défaut `model_version="S2013"` garantit une **rétrocompatibilité totale** — aucune simulation existante n'est impactée.

---

## Ce qui change

### Étape 1 — Variabilité SI intra-journalière (éq. A5, A10)

`kp3(t)` et `Vmx(t)` deviennent time-varying selon 7 classes de variabilité circadienne (Visentin 2015) :

| Classe | Pattern | Proba | si_B | si_L | si_D |
|--------|---------|-------|------|------|------|
| 1 | h-h-h | 10 % | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| 5 | l-h-h | 20 % | 0.4 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| 7 | l-l-h | 30 % | 0.4 | 0.4 | 1.0 |
| … | … | … | … | … | … |

- α=0.4, σ=0.2, transitions à **04:00 / 11:00 / 17:00** — données réelles (Visentin 2015)
- Nouveau fichier : `simglucose/params/si_variability_params.csv`

### Étape 2 — Phénomène de l'aube (éq. A5, A10)

- `kp1(t)` : +**1.5 mg/kg/min** linéairement sur 03:00–07:00 (Mallad et al., réf. 29 — valeur réelle)
- `Vmx(t)` réduit par `delta_kir_max` sur la même fenêtre (éq. A10)
  - **⚠ TODO** : calibrer `delta_kir_max=0.3` sur Mallad et al. (réf. 29) — valeur placeholder
- Nouveau fichier : `simglucose/params/dawn_params.csv`

### Étape 3 — Glucagon mis à jour (éq. A8, A23-A26)

Le modèle S2013 de ce repo ne contenait aucun état glucagon. S2017 ajoute **3 états ODE** (vecteur 13 → 16 états) :

| Index | État | Éq. | Description |
|-------|------|-----|-------------|
| 13 | `X_H` | A8 | Action du glucagon sur l'EGP |
| 14 | `H` | A23 | Glucagon plasmatique |
| 15 | `SR_Hs` | A25 | Sécrétion statique du glucagon |

`SR_Hd` (éq. A26) est algébrique : `δ · max(−dG/dt, 0)`.

**EGP S2017 :** `EGP(t) = kp1(t) − kp2·G − kp3(t)·X_L + ξ·X_H` (éq. A5)

Corrections vs S2013 :
1. Clairance glucagon **fractionnaire** `n` (mL/kg/min) — éq. A23
2. **Pas de sécrétion statique** quand G ≥ G_b — éq. A25 (évite les oscillations)

**⚠ 8 paramètres glucagon sont des placeholders (`TODO: calibrer`)** — structure correcte, valeurs à calibrer sur Dalla Man 2014 / données S2017.

---

## Utilisation

```python
# Mode S2013 (défaut, rétrocompatible)
p = T1DPatient.withName("adult#001")

# Mode S2017
p = T1DPatient.withName(
    "adult#001",
    model_version="S2017",
    start_time=360,   # 06:00 au démarrage
    si_class=5,       # classe SI 1-7 (None = tirage aléatoire pondéré)
    seed=42,
)
```

```bash
python examples/run_s2017.py --compare    # S2017 vs S2013 côte-à-côte
python tests/make_baseline.py --check     # non-régression S2013
python -m pytest tests/test_s2017_plausibility.py -v
```

---

## Plan de test

- [x] Non-régression S2013 : BG identique à 1e-6 mg/dL près
- [x] BG physiologique en mode S2017 (40–400 mg/dL)
- [x] Pas de NaN / inf
- [x] Pas d'états négatifs persistants
- [x] Effet dawn : BG à 7h ≥ BG à 3h
- [x] Différence breakfast vs dîner (classe 5 SI)
- [x] États glucagon H, SR_Hs ≥ 0

`7 passed in 124.66s`

---

## Fichiers clés

| Fichier | Rôle |
|---------|------|
| `simglucose/patient/t1dpatient.py` | Cœur ODE — toutes les extensions S2017 |
| `simglucose/params/si_variability_params.csv` | 7 classes SI (données Visentin 2015) |
| `simglucose/params/dawn_params.csv` | Paramètres phénomène de l'aube |
| `tests/test_s2017_plausibility.py` | 7 tests de plausibilité S2017 |
| `tests/baseline_s2013.csv` + `tests/make_baseline.py` | Non-régression S2013 |
| `examples/run_s2017.py` | Script de démonstration |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Documentation des changements et TODO calibration |

> **Note :** Les PDFs de référence (Visentin 2018, Visentin 2015) ne sont pas versionnés (copyright). Les équations implémentées sont référencées par numéro dans les commentaires du code.

body:
## Summary

  Closes all four Critical issues and the highest-priority Technical Debt
  items from `docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md`. The platform was previously
  unsuitable for any deployment beyond a trusted local network. After this
  PR, all C-level items are resolved and the system is safe for trusted
  local network deployment.

  ## Security issues resolved

  - **C-001** — bcrypt password verification: `verify_user()` now uses
    `pwd_context.verify()` against a stored bcrypt hash. Plaintext
    comparison eliminated.
  - **C-002** — CORS hardened: `allow_origins=["*"]` replaced with
    `settings.CORS_ORIGINS` (env var, defaults to localhost only). The
    dangerous wildcard + `allow_credentials=True` combination is gone.
  - **C-003** — Hardcoded defaults removed: `API_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET`,
    `DASH_PASS`, and `FEED_SALT` have no fallback values anywhere in code.
    Startup raises `ValueError` if any required secret is unset.
    `.env.example` documents all variables with format guidance.
  - **C-004** — Login rate limiting: `slowapi` added; `/api/login` capped
    at 5 requests/minute per IP (configurable via `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT` env
    var). Returns HTTP 429 when exceeded.
  - **FEED_SALT regression** — `iocs_pf.py` contained inline `"change-me"`
    fallback in both IOC export routes. Replaced with `settings.FEED_SALT`,
    consistent with all other secret handling.

  ## Infrastructure

  - **T-01** — `.env.example` added and tracked. Documents all required
    env vars with format guidance and generation commands.
  - **T-02** — `.gitignore` updated: `*.jsonl`, `*.db`, `*.log` patterns
    added; `!.env.example` negation ensures the template is not silenced.
  - **Events route** — `/api/events` was entirely unprotected; API key
    enforcement added.
  - **Stats route** — hardcoded `api_key = "dev-123"` replaced with
    `os.environ.get("API_KEY")`.
  - **TD-002** — CI now runs `pip-audit` and `bandit -r app/ -ll` on every
    push. Both steps use `continue-on-error: true` pending initial baseline
    triage (greppable TODO comments in `ci.yml`).
  - **H-003** — Confirmed already resolved: `app/utils/auth.py` uses
    `datetime.now(UTC)` throughout. Audit doc corrected.

  ## Deferred (explicitly out of scope)

  - **H-001** — JWT `localStorage` / CSP headers: requires UI branch;
    httpOnly migration is a coordinated backend + frontend change
  - **H-002** — TLS termination in Docker Compose: infrastructure concern,
    separate engineering cycle
  - **JWT route wiring** — `require_jwt_or_api_key` is implemented but
    wired to zero routes; deferred to Phase 1B, bundled with router
    migration
  - **TD-001** — `passlib` crypt deprecation: Python 3.11 in use; deferred
    to Python version upgrade cycle

  ## Test coverage

  24 tests, all passing. New tests added this branch:

  - `test_login_success_returns_token` — bcrypt verification, happy path
  - `test_login_wrong_password_returns_401`
  - `test_login_wrong_username_returns_401`
  - `test_login_missing_fields_returns_422`
  - `test_login_rate_limited_after_threshold` — 5 attempts exhaust bucket;
    6th returns 429
  - `test_login_token_is_valid_jwt` — decodes HS256 token, asserts correct
    subject and expiry
  - `test_api_smoke_*` — CORS configuration, key endpoint health checks

  ## Reviewer checklist

  - [ ] `DASH_PASS` in `pytest.ini` is a bcrypt hash, not plaintext
  - [ ] No hardcoded secrets in `app/` — `grep -r "change-me\|dev-123\|devsecret" app/`
  - [ ] `CORS_ORIGINS` in `config.py` has no wildcard default
  - [ ] Rate limit decorator present on `/api/login` in `auth_router.py`
  - [ ] `app/limiter.py` uses `get_remote_address`, not `X-Forwarded-For`
  - [ ] `reset_rate_limiter` fixture in `conftest.py` is `autouse=True`
  - [ ] CI has `pip-audit` and `bandit` steps with `continue-on-error: true`
    and TODO comments
  - [ ] `.env.example` is tracked and readable
  - [ ] 24 tests pass on the branch

## Summary

Resolves audit Pain rows **P8** (SIP UUID wraps push label off-row), **P10** (CHP copy button misses on touch), and **P11** (Admin 6-col table overflows 360px) per Q2 mobile audit, G5 grouping.

### What changed

Empty/error rows special-cased so they read as centered messages, not labelled cards.

**Agent**: Gyarados
**Issue**: Closes #97

- [ ] Manual iPhone Safari + iPad portrait check -- pending CI green

## Post-deploy watch

Watch for any reports about admin-panel keyboard navigation regressing (the `td -> block` flatten changes default keyboard tab order). The button stays focusable + the `data-label` pseudo-elements don't affect focus, so the impact should be visual-only.

- **elrond (codex/gpt-5.5)**: Position D-equivalent for G5: SIP stacks rows, CHP full-row tap-to-copy with shared copy helper + button stopPropagation, Admin uses CSS-only `data-label` reflow (no second render path). Don't ellipsize SIP values — UUIDs need to remain inspectable. Don't use horizontal scroll for the admin table.

author: martsokha
body:
## Summary

Splits `nvisy-codec` into two crates:

- **`nvisy-codec`** — modality-keyed handler traits + supporting
  infrastructure (`Handler`, `TextHandler`, `TabularHandler`,
  `ImageHandler`, `AudioHandler`, `RichHandler`, `ContentHandle`,
  boxed wrappers, redaction shapes, `apply_*_redaction` helpers,
  span/location plumbing, `impl_image_handler!` macro).
- **`nvisy-formats`** (new) — every concrete per-format
  implementation (TXT, JSON, Markdown, HTML, CSV, XLSX, PNG, JPEG,
  TIFF, WAV, MP3, PDF, DOCX) plus the `decode` entry point that
  dispatches a `Content` to the right loader.

Engine no longer references concrete format types; the 4 `ContentHandle::decode` call sites become `nvisy_formats::decode(content)`.

## Feature shape

Per-modality features in codec (`text`, `tabular`, `image`, `audio`, `rich`) gate the corresponding trait surface and boxed wrapper. `tabular` pulls `text` (cell values are `TextData`). `rich` pulls `text + image` (rich documents are multi-modal).

Per-format features in formats (`txt`, `json`, `markdown`, `html`, `csv`, `xlsx`, `png`, `jpeg`, `tiff`, `wav`, `mp3`, `pdf`, `docx`) — each enables the matching codec modality plus that format's specific deps. Per-modality umbrellas (`text`, `tabular`, `image`, `audio`, `rich`) bundle every format in that modality.

Engine has its own modality features (`tabular`, `image`, `audio`, `rich`) that forward to both codec and formats. Text is always on at the engine layer (and above) — every recognizer, the detection engine, and redaction strategies use text unconditionally. `rich` implicitly pulls `image` because codec's rich trait surface requires both. Defaults = all four optional modalities.

Server and cli expose the same four modality features, each forwarding to engine. Defaults = all four.

Workspace declares `default-features = false` on every internal crate so every consumer opts into features explicitly — no surprise inheritance of upstream defaults.

## Other notes

- `RichHandler` trait promoted from `pub(crate)` to `pub` and `apply_*_redaction` helpers from `pub(crate)` to `pub` so formats can implement / call them.
- `ContentHandle::decode` is gone — replaced by the free `nvisy_formats::decode(content)`. Breaking change for any external consumer; only engine consumed it internally.
- `BoxedXxxHandler::from(handler)` `From` impls are gone (orphan-rule blocked across the new crate boundary). Call sites use `BoxedXxxHandler::new(handler)` instead.
- `impl_image_handler!` macro rewritten with absolute `::nvisy_codec::…` paths so it expands correctly when invoked from `nvisy-formats`.
- `envelope/document.rs` in engine split into a folder; modality-specific accessors (`text.rs`, `tabular.rs`, `image.rs`, `audio.rs`) live in sibling files gated by the matching engine feature.
- New tests in `nvisy-formats`: `tests/decode.rs` exercises the `decode` entry point for txt/json/csv plus the no-MIME failure path; `tests/image_macro.rs` is a smoke test for the macro re-export.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-features`
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features` (engine compiles with no optional modalities)
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --features "nvisy-engine/rich"` (rich auto-enables image)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` (0 warnings)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --lib --tests` (all green)
- [x] `cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps -D warnings` (no broken links)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Closes the second of the four blocked-on-Triton explorer gaps. The Audit page was a static explainer because Triton had no in-process retrieval — only stdout. This PR adds a bounded ring buffer that captures every audit record, an authenticated REST endpoint to read the recent slice, and wires the explorer's page to render a live table.

## Triton side

- `triton-core::audit::AuditBuffer` — global, mutex-protected `VecDeque` capped at `AUDIT_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 1024` entries. Ring semantics; `emit()` pushes after every stdout write so stdout stays the source of truth.
- `GET /v1/audit?limit=N&trace_id=X` — authenticated like `/v1/tools`. Server caps `limit` to [1, 500]; `trace_id` is an exact-match filter.
- Axum `query` feature added to the workspace dep.

## Explorer side

- New `auditTailProvider` (family) + `RestClient.auditTail()`.
- Audit page renders a live table: phase dot, tool, trace_id (monospace), latency, result, timestamp. Tap row to expand the full JSON. Filter-by-trace_id + limit dropdown + refresh button.

## Tests

Rust (no mocks, real spawned triton-bin):
```
test audit_endpoint_returns_dispatch_and_rejected_records ... ok
test audit_endpoint_requires_auth ... ok
test audit_endpoint_caps_limit_server_side ... ok
```

The first test fires a successful echo, a bogus-token call, asserts both appear newest-first, and that the trace_id filter only returns the matching entry.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test` (21 widget tests), `flutter build web --release` — all clean.

## Summary

Removes the bulk "🤖 Hand off N unresolved references to a Claude Code session" banner above the References list and replaces it with a per-entry pill on each bib-entry card.

### Before
- One blue banner above the entire list with a mega-prompt covering every unresolved entry.
- Click → expand → "Copy prompt" → paste a wall of text covering papers you may or may not want to triage now.

### After
- No banner.
- Each unresolved entry (no PDF / no OA link / no publisher URL / no DOI — same predicate as before) renders a small `🤖 Hand off` pill in its summary line, next to the existing PDF (OA) / Site / notes badges.
- Click → `stopPropagation` (doesn't toggle the card open/close) → copy a focused single-entry research prompt to clipboard. Briefly shows `✓ Copied` then reverts.

The per-entry prompt is built client-side from `data-bib-*` attributes on the button (no HTML-escaping in inline `onclick`). Same per-entry research procedure as before, scoped to one citation.

### Why
User feedback: the bulk banner forced an all-or-nothing handoff. Per-entry actions let users triage the bibliography one paper at a time as they're browsing.

Template-only diff (+73 / -57). No JS/CSS/Python changes outside the inline `<script>` in the references panel.

body:
pages/2_Webcam.py:
- Fix intermittent `cv2.error: vector` crash: the Haar cascade was shared across threads via @st.cache_resource, but detectMultiScale is not thread-safe — the WebRTC processor thread and the main thread corrupted each other's internal state (reproduced: ~50/960 wrong face counts under concurrency). Now uses a thread-local classifier + a lock.
- Fix maxSize passed as (height, width); OpenCV expects (width, height).
- Stop detecting trees/background as faces in snapshot & capture: those paths now use the InsightFace SCRFD CNN detector, which does not false-fire on foliage (no Haar confidence threshold separates them reliably). The live preview keeps Haar for speed (SCRFD is ~100ms/frame). SCRFD degrades to Haar if InsightFace isn't installed.

pipeline_v1.py:
- Fix the `mlp` backbone, which returned ~2-3 instead of a real BMI. Three train/inference mismatches vs notebook 15 (15_finetune_arcface):
  * activation was ReLU, model trained with GELU (loaded silently);
  * net predicts log(BMI) — now exponentiated back to BMI units;
  * fed DeepFace "ArcFace" embeddings, but the head was trained on InsightFace buffalo_l/w600k_r50. Added a dedicated InsightFace extractor for the mlp path and skip DeepFace face-prep when unused.

requirements.txt:
- Add insightface, onnxruntime (MLP backbone + SCRFD), tf-keras (deepface on Keras 3), and fastapi/uvicorn/python-multipart (the api.py FastAPI backend).

author: rickcrawford
body:
## Summary

Child of the WOR-795 epic, and the most-cited OSS AI-gateway gap (semantic cache was enterprise-only; Kong/Portkey/Bifrost/Higress ship it free). Adds an **opt-in embedding-similarity response cache**: a near-duplicate prompt is served from cache; an exact prompt still takes the existing fast path.

- **`EmbeddingCache`** (sbproxy-ai): LRU of `(L2-normalized embedding, cached response)`, brute-force cosine lookup with a configurable threshold, TTL expiry, deterministic LRU eviction. Pure + unit-tested.
- **Config** via the existing opaque `ai.semantic_cache` block: `{ enabled, threshold, ttl_secs, max_entries, embedding: { provider, model } }`. **Off by default**, so existing configs are unaffected. Built lazily on the per-origin handler (mirrors the PII redactor).
- **`compute_embedding`** posts `/v1/embeddings` to the configured provider to vectorize the prompt.
- **Wired into `handle_ai_proxy`**: on a miss, embed the prompt, cosine-scan, replay the closest match (`>= threshold`) with `x-semcache: HIT`, else remember the key+vector and store the upstream 200 response. **Gated on the enterprise `SemanticLookupHook` being absent** so the two never double-cache. Embedding failures **fail open** (proceed to upstream uncached).
- **Metrics**: reuses `sbproxy_ai_cache_results_total{cache_type=semantic}` for hit/miss and adds a `sbproxy_ai_semantic_cache_similarity` histogram.

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ Near-duplicate prompt (cosine ≥ threshold) returns a cached response; exact path runs first.
- ✅ Configurable threshold / TTL / max-entries via YAML; deterministic LRU eviction.
- ✅ Hit/miss + similarity-score metrics under the `sbproxy_*` closed label set.
- ✅ Works with a local in-memory store (no Redis required).
- ✅ Does not regress the exact path; semantic layer is opt-in.
- ✅ e2e: a paraphrased prompt hits cache; upstream call count proves the saving.

## Scope

Non-streaming + in-memory, per the blueprint on the ticket. Follow-up PRs (noted on the ticket): streaming-safe SSE replay, Redis-vector / persistent (redb/SQLite) backends, and an ANN index (this PR is brute-force, bounded by `max_entries`).

## Tests

Unit (cosine hit/miss, threshold boundary, TTL expiry, LRU eviction, opaque-config parse) + e2e (`semantic_cache_e2e.rs`): a path-routing mock returns embeddings keyed on the prompt so a paraphrased France prompt hits the cache (served without reaching the upstream, `x-semcache: HIT`, replays the first reply) while an unrelated prompt misses and forwards.

Validated through the full local gate (fmt / clippy / test / build / e2e / doc).

author: stijnvanhulle
body:
## Summary

Makes the `@kubb/ast` node vocabulary **spec-neutral** so adapters for non-OpenAPI specs (AsyncAPI, GraphQL, Prisma, Arazzo) map onto built-in nodes. The model stays **closed and fully typed** — no adapter-defined kinds, no registry. (Per the design decision: `@kubb/ast` carries all options.)

### Generalized `OperationNode`
- `method` and `path` are now **optional** (HTTP/REST only).
- New optional `protocol` (`'http'`/`'graphql'`/`'kafka'`/`'amqp'`/`'ws'`/…), `action` (`'send'`/`'receive'`/`'query'`/`'mutation'`/`'subscription'`/…), and `channel` fields cover AsyncAPI pub/sub and GraphQL roots.
- `createOperation` no longer requires `method`/`path`.

### New `Workflow` / `Step` kinds (Arazzo)
The only constructs that don't map onto Schema/Operation. Added as first-class closed kinds with `createWorkflow`/`createStep` factories, `isWorkflowNode`/`isStepNode` guards, `workflow`/`step` visitor callbacks, and an optional `workflows` collection on `InputNode`/`InputStreamNode`.

### Spec → vocabulary mapping
| Spec | Maps to |
|---|---|
| OpenAPI | `operations` (method/path) + `schemas` — unchanged |
| AsyncAPI | `operations` (`action`/`channel`) + `schemas` |
| GraphQL | `operations` (`action`) + `schemas` |
| Prisma | `schemas` only (`operations: []`) |
| Arazzo | `workflows`/`steps` + JSON-Schema `inputs` |

## Breaking (types)
`OperationNode.method`/`path` are optional now — code reading them must handle `undefined`. Within this repo only `defineResolver` needed a guard; `@kubb/adapter-oas` still sets `method`/`path`, so **OpenAPI output is byte-identical**. The plugins query/client generators are fixed in a coordinated follow-up PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `@kubb/ast` typecheck + tests (312, incl. new `workflow.test.ts`: factories, guards, walk/transform/collect over a `workflows` root, structural-sharing identity, method-less operation)
- [x] `@kubb/core` typecheck + tests (137) — resolver guards optional method/path
- [x] `@kubb/adapter-oas` typecheck + `parser.test.ts` (334) — OpenAPI output unchanged
- [x] format + lint clean
- [ ] Full CI green

> Stacked on `claude/adapter-oas-rename-schema-ctx` (PR #3377) for a clean diff; retarget to `main` once that merges. Coordinated follow-ups: plugins PR (method/path optionality) and platform-docs PR.

author: jaavila-of
body:
## Summary

Three bugs ganged up in `ridge_rt`'s HTTP client path to make every real-world HTTPS call from `Net.Http.get`/`post`/`put`/`delete` unusable. Bundled into one PR because they share the same two helper functions and the user only ever sees the failure mode (`badmap`) after stage 2 lands.

1. `application:ensure_all_started(ssl)` is now invoked alongside `inets`. Without it the first `https://` request died deep inside httpc with `{failed_connect, [{inet, [inet], ssl_not_started}]}`, wrapped in an Error the user could never inspect because of bug #2.
2. The success/error wires now return atom-keyed maps (`#{status => …, body => …}`, `#{code => …, message => …}`) that match the Ridge `Response` and built-in `Error` records. The old tagged-tuple shape (`{response_record, S, B}` / `{error_record, C, M}`) crashed any caller touching `resp.status` or `e.message` with `badmap`. Same root cause and fix as the http_listen server-side wire fix in 0.2.2; this closes the client side.
3. A default `User-Agent: ridge-lang/0.2` is sent on every request. httpc's built-in `User-Agent: httpc/X.Y` is rejected by several production APIs (GitHub returns HTTP 403 "User-Agent header required"), so the default would not get a beginner past their first real call. Custom headers remain deferred per the std.net.http scope guard.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p ridge-codegen-erl --release --test stdlib_map` — 9 tests pass including the new `stdlib_bridge_covers_http_client_surface` that locks all four client methods to RidgeStdlibLocal dispatch
- [x] End-to-end against the real `https://api.github.com/users/octocat/repos?per_page=30`: response decoded, top repos sorted by stars, output rendered without `badmap`/`ssl_not_started`/`403` (every one of these was a failure mode before)

author: maximumcats
body:
## Purpose
Add validation primitives for concrete mapping-shaped data objects.

## Boundary
This PR introduces explicit field specifications, record specifications, structured validation violations, and a validator that checks whether a concrete mapping-shaped object satisfies a declared structural contract. The record is the object being checked; the specification supplies the protocol-facing rules.

## Public Surface
- leibniz.records.FieldSpec
- leibniz.records.RecordSpec
- leibniz.records.RecordViolation
- leibniz.records.RecordValidationError
- leibniz.records.required
- leibniz.records.optional
- leibniz.records.validate_record
- leibniz.records.collect_record_violations

## Tests
- env -u PYTHONPATH python -m pytest
- env -u PYTHONPATH python -m ruff check .
- env -u PYTHONPATH python -m pyright
- env -u PYTHONPATH python -m leibniz.repository_policy .
- env -u PYTHONPATH python -m build
- installed the built wheel in a temporary virtual environment and imported leibniz.records

## Rationale
Future protocol definitions need a shared way to check concrete data objects without each definition inventing ad hoc validation. This gives later record types a small substrate for rejecting missing fields, unknown fields, invalid scalar values, invalid identifiers, and malformed nested structures.

## Design Review
The validator works on mappings and explicit field specifications. It parses identifier, name, and version fields through the identifier module, rejects non-finite numbers, reports paths for nested failures, and returns only fields the specification owns. It does not define Record as a protocol primitive, and it does not add canonical JSON, content hashing, manifests, or artifact categories.

author: ztripez
body:
Closes #182.

Adds the first real, non-trivial end-to-end scenario, built **only through the
public authoring API** — the Alpha 0 product-usage test for whether Conflux is
usable beyond isolated single-domain fixtures.

## The world (`regional_settlement_ecology`)

One bounded model combining most existing domains, all dimensionally consistent
(water / grain / people / vehicles):

- **Terrain field** (2×2): `water` runs off east with conservation; `crop` grows
  10%/tick.
- **Basins + aggregates**: north/south regions, sum-of-crop aggregates.
- **Settlement table**: `grain_store` accumulates **two** cross-scale inflows —
  north-basin crop **bridged** into a `food` signal, and south-basin crop
  **projected** up a source-authoritative scale link into a `projected_yield`
  signal — and `population` grows at a per-tick rate.
- **Herd actors**: graze the crop (sampling the field), track nearby herd-mates via
  an exact **proximity query**, and **drift** east.
- **TradeRoutes graph**: `congestion` rises with incident road `capacity`; a
  report-only `trade_congestion` **event** materializes for congested nodes.

## Acceptance (#182)

- Built only through the public API — no value computed by hand outside a declared
  Conflux API. ✓
- Runs on CPU reference execution. ✓
- In the baseline report (registered in `ALL_SCENARIOS`); it exercises every report
  surface — aggregates, bridges, flow conservation, actors, query + index
  eligibility, projection + drift, graph rule, report-only event, plus kernel
  extraction, selected-execution fallback (`grow_population` reads a param → falls
  back to reference), the planner, and a transfer advisory. ✓
- Contract tests assert the lowered domain set and the headline runtime outcomes
  with report provenance (basin totals, both bridges, flow conservation, actor
  grazing/alertness, graph congestion `[10,0,0] -> [20,15,5]`, and the report-only
  event). ✓
- API pain points captured as follow-ups: handled by the dedicated audit in
  **#186** (this PR is the usage; #186 is the audit + follow-up issues).

## Boundaries

No new domain semantics, no optimization work, no manual scans or ad-hoc vectors —
every value flows through a declared domain/report API. Doc/test-support only
(`conflux-fixtures` stays `publish = false`). Workspace green (fmt/clippy/test) and
the strict doc build passes.

author: hanielcota
body:
## Summary

Targets the teleport-family findings (back, spawn, teleport, tpa, warps, homes) from the codebase review.

### HIGH — async teleports
- `TeleportExecutor` switches to `player.teleportAsync` so the warm-up used by `/home`, `/spawn`, and `/warp` does not stall on chunk-load when the destination is far away or in another world.
- `TeleportRequestExecutor.execute` now returns `CompletableFuture<TeleportExecution>` so `/tpaccept` does not block the main thread on a cross-world target. `TeleportRequestService.accept` returns `CompletableFuture<AcceptResult>` and `TpAcceptCommand` consumes it via `thenAccept`.
- `SpawnVoidListener` uses `teleportAsync` for the void rescue (fire-and-forget) so a nether-void → overworld-spawn does not stall the damage event.
- `BackClickHandler` uses `teleportAsync` and consolidates the dual world-null check (`SqliteTeleportHistory.readEntry` already filters unloaded worlds on read).
- `HomeRenameChatListener` flips to `ignoreCancelled=false` so a chat-mute / anti-spam plugin cancelling the message earlier no longer strands the rename session waiting for input that will never arrive.

### HIGH — TPA correctness
- `TeleportRequestService.create` now notifies the previous target when a new outgoing request from the same requester replaces theirs. Previously the prior target was left staring at stale `[ACCEPT]/[DENY]` buttons whose actions silently returned `noIncoming`.

### MEDIUM
- `RequestStore.add` mutates `outgoingByRequester` through `compute` so two concurrent `add` calls for the same requester cannot leave a dangling index entry pointing at an already-removed request id.
- `WarpStore.delete` uses a single `updateCount` DELETE; the affected-row count tells us whether the warp existed, so concurrent `/delwarp` calls don't both observe-then-double-delete.

### Deferred (not in this PR)
- `SetSpawnCommand` / `SetWarpCommand` async SQL writes — would need writer plumbing; one-shot admin commands so the latency hit is bounded.
- Warp lookup cache — every `/warp <name>` hits SQL; would need a refactor of `WarpService` and `WarpStore`. Tracked for a follow-up.
- `/tphere`, `/tp <player>`, `/tp pos` sync teleport — already rare admin paths; deferred.

## Test plan
- [x] `./gradlew spotlessApply build` passes locally.
- [ ] Manual: `/tpa <player>`, accept across worlds, no main-thread stall.
- [ ] Manual: `/tpa A`, then `/tpa B` from the same requester — player A gets a "request replaced" message.
- [ ] Manual: void-fall in nether with spawn in overworld → rescue teleport works without lag spike.
- [ ] Manual: rename a home while another plugin is muting chat — rename input still consumed.
- [ ] Manual: `/setwarp foo`, two operators run `/delwarp foo` simultaneously — exactly one reports success.

author: st-adam
body:
## Summary

Three targeted performance optimizations to `_step_speculative` and `_writeback_kv_row`, reducing per-step overhead in the PLD hot path. All correctness-preserving — byte-equal output verified by 11 new unit tests + 25 existing PLD tests.

**Stacked on #173** — merge #173 first; this PR adds 1 commit on top.

Profiling showed 3-7ms/step wasted on unnecessary GPU syncs, O(B) cache concatenations, and Python↔GPU round-trips.

### Optimizations

- **Opt 1 — Remove redundant `mx.eval(predicted)`** (L6731): `tolist()` implicitly evals; explicit eval before it adds an unnecessary GPU sync point (~0.1-0.5ms)
- **Opt 2 — In-place KV row writeback** (L6310-6355): Replace O(B) `mx.concatenate` rebuild with direct slice assignment (`arr[i:j] = val`) when solo fits within existing allocation. Falls back to concat for the rare growth case. Eliminates 64 concatenate calls (keys+values × 32 layers) per replay step at B=4
- **Opt 3 — Vectorized offset rewind** (L6844-6876): Replace per-layer `.tolist()` → Python list comprehension → `mx.array()` round-trip with single `mx.maximum(offset - shortfall_arr, 0)`. Includes shape-mismatch guard for padded cache arrays (B > active batch)

### New files

- `tests/test_pld_perf_optimizations.py` — 11 unit tests covering all 3 optimizations
- `tests/benchmark/bench_pld_step_overhead.py` — Micro-benchmark harness (instant-return mock, reports median/P95)

### Benchmark results (M-series, L=32)

| Component | B=1 med(ms) | B=4 med(ms) |
|---|---|---|
| Accept/reject | 0.22 | 0.18 |
| KV rewind (vectorized) | 0.39 | 0.24 |
| KV writeback (in-place) | n/a | 0.67 |
| Total step overhead | 0.25 | 0.22 |

## Test plan

- [x] 11/11 new unit tests pass (`pytest tests/test_pld_perf_optimizations.py -v`)
- [x] 25/25 existing PLD tests pass (`pytest tests/test_mllm_step_speculative.py tests/test_mllm_pld_tq_and_invariants.py -v`)

author: michalschroeder
body:
## Why
Default render grabs the DOM at `domcontentloaded` and runs **once**. SPAs that load content afterward, and pages that serve a JS challenge, come back empty — so today you rerun by hand with stronger flags. `--auto` does that escalation for you.

## What
`--auto` tries strategies in order, stopping at the first that extracts content:

1. `default`
2. `--wait-ms 6000`
3. evasive rendering + `--wait-ms 6000`

- Escalates **only on failure** (load error / Defuddle error / empty or missing output), so simple pages keep the fast default path.
- Each retry is logged to stderr; honors explicit `--wait-ms`/`--stealth` as the base for the ladder.
- `--no-render` remains a single static attempt.

## Verified (built image, real pages)
| Case | Behavior | exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--auto` example.com | rung 1, silent fast-path | 0 |
| `--auto` Bluesky | escalates → `--wait-ms`, content extracted | 0 |
| `--auto` Reddit | exhausts ladder, clear stderr, no false success | 3 |
| `--no-render --auto` | single static attempt | 0 |

## Verification
biome clean, tsc clean, 62/62 tests pass (+3 for `--auto`).

Audit spec `tests/audit/trainer-games-browser.spec.ts` ran against prod (https://praxis.tsrun.dev/trainer/games) and recorded:

- **`outline: 'none'` on every input.** The shared `inputStyle` literal in `src/trainer/ImportGamesPage.tsx` set `outline: 'none'`, which (as an inline style) overrides the global `:focus-visible` rule from `src/index.css`. After `.focus()`:

  ECO INPUT :focus styles: { outlineStyle: 'none', ... }  // same
  ```
  Affects all six inputs on the page (Chess.com / Lichess username, Database Player, Year from, Year to, ECO, Min Elo). Sighted keyboard users get no focus indicator on any of these — versus e.g. the trainer-students-list search input which correctly shows `outlineStyle: solid, outlineWidth: 2px, outlineColor: rgb(251, 191, 36)`.
- **No programmatic `<label>` association on any of those inputs:**
  ```
  CC USERNAME INPUT a11y: { id: null, ariaLabel: null, labelsFor: 0, wrappingLabel: null, placeholder: 'e.g. Hikaru', type: 'text' }
  PLAYER INPUT      a11y: { id: null, ariaLabel: null, labelsFor: 0, wrappingLabel: null, placeholder: 'e.g. Carlsen' }
  ECO INPUT         a11y: { id: null, ariaLabel: null, labelsFor: 0, wrappingLabel: null }
  MIN ELO INPUT     a11y: { id: null, ariaLabel: null, labelsFor: 0, wrappingLabel: null, type: 'number' }
  YEAR FROM         a11y: { id: null, ariaLabel: null, labelsFor: 0, wrappingLabel: null, type: 'number' }

  SOURCE SEGMENTED container: { role: null, ariaLabel: null, ariaLabelledby: null }
  POSITION MODE SEGMENTED:    { role: null, ariaLabel: null }
