author: eshishki
body:
## Why I'm doing:

`ndv` / `approx_count_distinct` (the `HyperLogLog`-backed aggregates) spend avoidable
CPU on two per-row hot paths that have nothing to do with the actual HLL math:

1. **Merge side.** When a serialized HLL arrives at the receiver, it is materialized
   into a temporary `HyperLogLog` and then merged. For a `FULL`-format input that
   temporary `posix_memalign`s a 16 KiB register array, `memcpy`s 16 KiB into it,
   and frees it again -- per row.
2. **Serialize side.** `convert_to_serialize_format` builds a throwaway
   `HyperLogLog` for every single input value (heap-allocating a `flat_hash_set`
   for that one element) only to serialize a ~10-byte record.

The HLL wire format is already compact/adaptive, so unlike the percentile work there
is no byte bloat to recover here -- this is purely about the per-row object/allocation
churn.

## What I'm doing:

### 1. Merge a serialized HLL in place

Add `HyperLogLog::merge(const Slice&)` that merges a serialized HLL into the
destination without materializing a temporary object. Only the **FULL** payload is
merged in place: its register array is flat, so the merge is an order-independent,
duplicate-free `max` and the result is provably byte-identical. EXPLICIT, SPARSE and
invalid/empty slices delegate to the existing `merge(HyperLogLog(slice))` path,
because:

- EXPLICIT serialization depends on `phmap::flat_hash_set` iteration order, so a
  direct re-insert could reorder the serialized bytes;
- SPARSE deserialize is **last-write-wins** on duplicate indexes (not `max`), and
  `is_valid()` does not reject duplicate indexes;
- an invalid/null/truncated slice must stay a no-op (the temporary path turns it into
  an empty HLL today).

This removes the per-row 16 KiB allocate/copy/free on the `FULL` merge path while
keeping the exact same serialized state for every slice the current code accepts.

### 2. Emit the single-value record directly

In `convert_to_serialize_format`, a single hashed value is a one-element `EXPLICIT`
record (or an `EMPTY` record when the hash is 0). Emit those bytes directly instead
of constructing a `HyperLogLog` and its `flat_hash_set`. Byte-identical to
`update()` + `serialize()`.

Scope: this is the `HllNdvAggregateFunction` family (`ndv`, `approx_count_distinct`,
`hll_raw`). `hll_union*` aggregates take in-memory object columns and never
deserialize per row, so they are untouched.

## Numbers (`hll_merge_bench`, Release, single thread)

| What | Where it runs in a query | legacy | new | speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Convert** (serialize a value) | pass-through serialize before exchange; per row, independent of `GROUP BY` | 31.9M/s | 91.9M/s | **2.9x** (1024) / **2.7x** (4096) |
| **Merge FULL**, single state | global `ndv` (no `GROUP BY`) | 126k/s | 138k/s | 1.10x |
| **Merge FULL**, `GROUP BY` 64 groups | `ndv ... GROUP BY`, low cardinality | 122k/s | 134k/s | 1.10x |
| **Merge FULL**, `GROUP BY` 512 groups | `ndv ... GROUP BY`, higher cardinality | 98k/s | 105k/s | 1.06x |
| **Merge EXPLICIT/SPARSE** | low-cardinality input (any shape) | 492k/s | 492k/s | unchanged (delegates) |

The serialize side is the real win (**~2.7-2.9x**): the per-row `HyperLogLog` +
`flat_hash_set` construction is gone. The merge win is modest and only on `FULL`
inputs (**~6-10%**): the 16 KiB register `max` dominates the merge, so removing the
temporary allocate/copy/free trims a single-digit percentage, and that shrinks as
`GROUP BY` cardinality grows (more cache-cold destination registers). EXPLICIT/SPARSE
inputs are unchanged because they keep the byte-identical temp-object path.

## Safety

- **Byte-identical output.** The `FULL` fast path mirrors `merge(const HyperLogLog&)`
  operation-for-operation; EXPLICIT/SPARSE/invalid slices delegate to the existing
  path. `convert` emits exactly the one-element `EXPLICIT` / `EMPTY` record.
- **No storage-format change.** The persisted `HllDataType` enum and all on-wire
  encodings are untouched, so this is rolling-upgrade safe.
- Unit tests: `TestHll.MergeSlice` asserts byte-identity vs the temp-object path
  across the full (destination type x slice type) matrix plus EXPLICIT->FULL
  promotion, a `hash == 0` element, a non-canonical duplicate-index SPARSE slice, and
  invalid/truncated/null slices; `TestHll.SingleValueExplicitFormat` locks the
  convert record layout.

Fixes #73767

body:
## Summary
Fourth ticket of Sprint C.0 per [design doc](https://github.com/shoaibrain/edforge/blob/main/docs/pilot-greenlight/c-epic-pdf-generation-design.md) §5.2. Pure TypeScript scope — no new external library, no runtime PDF rendering. Adds the **extensibility hinge** that lets all future doc types (invoice, receipt, report card, admit card, ID card, certs) share the editor UI and the per-domain render endpoint code path.

### Why this design

The editor UI in Shell (`/settings/pdf-templates`) needs to render a form section for every configurable field in every doc-type's template. With ~12 doc types planned over V1+V1.5, hand-writing a per-doc-type editor for each is the wrong path. Instead, **each doc type declares a `TemplateDescriptor` listing its `configurableFields[]` + its `defaults(archetype, locale)` + its `sampleData(archetype, locale)` + its React Component**. The editor reads any descriptor and generates the right form sections automatically. Adding a 13th doc type = adding one descriptor file. Zero editor code change.

This PR ships the type contract + the registry. Concrete descriptors (`invoice.ts`, `receipt.ts`, …) ship with their document components in C.1+.

## Files
- `packages/pdf-renderer/src/descriptors/types.ts` — `DocType`, `Archetype`, `PdfBranding`, `PdfLocaleSettings`, `PdfTemplateConfig`, `ConfigurableField`, `DocumentComponentProps`, `TemplateDescriptor<TData, TConfig>` — the full contract
- `packages/pdf-renderer/src/descriptors/registry.ts` — `registerDescriptor`, `getDescriptor`, `getRegisteredDocTypes`, `hasDescriptor`, `_clearRegistryForTest`
- `packages/pdf-renderer/src/descriptors/index.ts` — public re-exports
- `packages/pdf-renderer/src/descriptors/__tests__/registry.spec.ts` — 14 specs covering register/retrieve, duplicate rejection, unknown-docType errors, snapshot semantics, hasDescriptor, callability of `defaults()`/`sampleData()`, configurableFields preservation
- `packages/pdf-renderer/src/index.ts` — re-export `./descriptors` from root + bump `PDF_RENDERER_PACKAGE_VERSION` to `'0.4.0'`
- `packages/pdf-renderer/package.json` — version 0.3.0 → 0.4.0; new `./descriptors` subpath export

## Test results
```
PASS src/core/__tests__/theme.spec.ts                    (4 specs)
PASS src/core/__tests__/i18n.spec.ts                    (12 specs)
PASS src/core/__tests__/fonts.spec.ts                   (12 specs)
PASS src/core/__tests__/format.spec.ts                  (17 specs)
PASS src/components/__tests__/LineItemTable.spec.tsx    (9 specs)
PASS src/descriptors/__tests__/registry.spec.ts        (14 specs, NEW)
PASS src/__tests__/render-smoke.spec.tsx               (18 specs)
Test Suites: 7 passed, 7 total
Tests:       72 passed, 72 total
```

Public-surface smoke (post-build sanity check):
```
exports check: OK — all 19 surface names present
version: 0.4.0
```

## Notable design choices called out for review

1. **`PdfBranding` and `PdfLocaleSettings` are pdf-renderer-LOCAL shapes**, not re-exported from `@aibrains/shared-types`. The canonical `SchoolBranding` lands in shared-types in C.0.5. Render endpoints (C.1+) will map their canonical types to these shapes at the boundary. This keeps the renderer self-contained at the type level and avoids a circular publish dependency.
2. **Descriptors store internally as `TemplateDescriptor<unknown, PdfTemplateConfig>`** and cast back to the caller's `TemplateDescriptor<TData, TConfig>` at `getDescriptor`. The generic-position invariance forces a double-`unknown` cast — comments at both call sites explain why this is intentional, not a smell.
3. **`Lang` is canonical in `core/i18n.ts`** and NOT re-exported from descriptors. Avoids a `TS2308` duplicate-export collision at the package root. `PdfTemplateConfig.labelLanguages` uses the canonical type via internal import.
4. **`Archetype` accepts all 5 V1 archetypes** in the type (`PABSON | GENERIC | CBSE_IN | NAIS_US | GEMS_UAE`), but each descriptor's `defaults()` SHOULD fall back to the GENERIC profile for archetypes it doesn't explicitly handle. V1 only exercises PABSON + GENERIC; reserved archetypes are type-level future-proofing per the master plan.
5. **Registry rejects duplicate registrations rather than silently overwriting.** Duplicate registration usually indicates a double-import bug (two paths both importing `descriptors/invoice.ts`); a loud error catches it. Tests cover this — `registerDescriptor` throws AND the first registration is preserved intact.
6. **`getRegisteredDocTypes` returns a snapshot, not a live view.** Mutating the result does not affect the registry. Test asserts this.

# 👩🏻‍💻 What does this PR do?

Sync style fixes for patient- and store-scoped tables on `feature-sync`. Reassigns sync styles in `sync_style.rs` and updates each affected `generate_changelog` to populate `store_id` / `patient_id` from `&self`.

Sync style changes

- `NameInsuranceJoin` → `Patient` (was `Remote`)

- `ItemStoreJoin` → `RemoteOwned` v6 (was unassigned)
- `Clinician`, `ClinicianStoreJoin`, `InsuranceProvider` → Central (was `RemoteOwned`)

Changelog generation

Refactored `generate_changelog` from `(record_id, ...)` to `(&self, ...)` so the changelog entry can carry `store_id` / `patient_id`:

- `ClinicianStoreJoin` — added `store_id`

author: script-java
body:
**💡 What:**
Added full keyboard accessibility to the `CouponCard` interactive elements in the Valentine's Day application. The cards now feature clear visual focus rings and can be flipped using the `Enter` or `Space` keys.

**🎯 Why:**
The `CouponCard` component was originally implemented as a generic `<div>` with only an `onClick` handler. This meant users relying on keyboard navigation (like Tab) could not access or interact with the cards. This update makes the delightful coupon reveal experience accessible to all users.

**📸 Before/After:**
*Before:* Pressing Tab would skip over the love coupons entirely.
*After:* Pressing Tab successfully focuses each coupon, showing a clean, visible focus ring (`focus-visible:ring-4 focus-visible:ring-rose-400`), and pressing Enter/Space flips the card smoothly.

**♿ Accessibility:**
- Added `role="button"` to provide semantic meaning to screen readers.
- Added `tabIndex={0}` to include the cards in the document's tab sequence.
- Added `aria-expanded={isOpen}` to communicate the card's current state to assistive technologies.
- Added `onKeyDown` handler that listens for `Enter` or `Space` (and calls `e.preventDefault()` to prevent unwanted page scrolling when using Space) to trigger the `onClick` logic.
- Implemented `focus-visible` styling using existing Tailwind utility classes to ensure a clear visual focus indicator for sighted keyboard users.

author: twidtwid
body:
## Summary

Two fixes that fall out of debugging the Tim Ferriss / Sami Inkinen ingest 2026-05-21:

### 1. \`select_transcript_link\` rejects negative-scored winners

The scoring logic already penalized index/archive pages with \`-100\` but the function still returned the highest-scored candidate regardless of whether that score was negative. On a fresh episode whose per-episode transcript page hasn't been posted yet, the function silently returned the nav-menu "All Transcripts" link (score \`-50\` after the index penalty) and the pipeline ingested an index page of *every* Tim Ferriss transcript as if it were the interview. Validators happily reported success because the structure was valid; the content was just wrong.

After: if the best candidate's score is \`< 0\`, return \`None\` and let the caller raise \`"no transcript link was found"\`. Fail loud beats silently shipping the least-bad garbage.

Generalizes to every provider, not just \`tim_blog\`.

### 2. \`title_strip_prefix\` support (function renamed)

\`strip_title_suffix\` only handled trailing boilerplate. Tim's per-episode *transcript* pages prepend \`"The Tim Ferriss Show Transcripts:"\` to \`og:title\`, which leaked all the way into \`episode.short_title\` — derived by splitting the canonical title on \` — \` and taking the head. Because the prefixed head was under the 80-char limit, the split kept it as the "headline." That polluted the HTML \`<title>\`, \`og:title\`, and the og-card.

After: \`strip_title_boilerplate\` handles both ends. The manifest gets a new \`title_strip_prefix\` key (string-or-list, case-insensitive, looped until stable, symmetric with the existing \`title_strip_suffix\`). Three call sites updated; \`tim_blog.json\` declares its prefixes:

\`\`\`json
"title_strip_prefix": [
  "The Tim Ferriss Show Transcripts:",
  "The Tim Ferriss Show Transcripts —",
  "The Tim Ferriss Show:"
]
\`\`\`

Module-level \`_TITLE_EDGE_CHARS = " -–—|·:"\` hoisted so the rstrip/lstrip trim-set isn't duplicated between the two paths.

## Why these are coupled in one PR

Both came from the same debugging session and both touch \`url_ingest.py\` in adjacent functions. They also reinforce each other: #1 makes fresh-episode failures fail loud (good), and #2 means once the real transcript page DOES exist, its title is clean on the way in. Together they make the tim.blog ingest robust to the new-episode → transcript-published lifecycle.

author: jasonlovesdoggo
body:
Closes #7.

## Problem
With four Catppuccin themes registered and `defaultColor: false`, Shiki inlined **four hex colors on every token span**:

```
<span style="--shiki-mocha:#CBA6F7;--shiki-macchiato:#C6A0F6;--shiki-frappe:#CA9EE6;--shiki-latte:#8839EF">
```

Across every token in every code block, the rendered markup hit ~600KB raw.

## Fix
Add `transformerStyleToClass` to the mdsvex Shiki highlighter. Each unique color-set becomes a single content-hashed class plus a small stylesheet, instead of being repeated inline on every span:

```
<span class="tk-1j9ida">   +   .tk-1j9ida{--shiki-mocha:#CBA6F7;--shiki-macchiato:#C6A0F6;...}
```

## Exact same colors, all four flavors
The class definitions carry the same `--shiki-{flavor}` variables that `src/lib/styles/syntax.css` already consumes per flavor (`html.latte .shiki span { color: var(--shiki-latte) }`, etc.), so output is byte-for-byte identical in appearance and theme switching is unchanged. No CSS changes needed.

## Measured
- Largest content chunk `tutorials.js`: **762KB → 405KB (50% smaller)**
- Inline `style="--shiki..."` spans remaining: **0** (6083 spans now reference shared classes)
- `bun run check`: 0 errors. `bun run build`: clean.

Class names are content hashes, so blocks sharing token styles share definitions and any duplicate `<style>` rules across blocks gzip away.

body:
## Correccion implementada

Se corrige una vulnerabilidad de control de acceso y explotacion de confianza en la ruta `POST /api/ofertas`.

Antes del cambio, el backend aceptaba directamente el campo `cliente_id` enviado en el cuerpo de la solicitud. Un usuario podia modificar ese valor y publicar una oferta asociada a otra persona.

## Solucion aplicada

- Se agrego un token de sesion firmado emitido por el backend al iniciar sesion o registrarse.
- Se agrego middleware para validar autenticacion y rol.
- La ruta `POST /api/ofertas` ahora requiere un usuario autenticado con rol `cliente`.
- El backend ignora el `cliente_id` enviado desde el cliente y utiliza el identificador obtenido de la sesion firmada.
- Se actualizaron los clientes web y movil para guardar el token y enviarlo al publicar ofertas.
- La respuesta de autenticacion ya no expone la contrasena almacenada del usuario.
- Se documento la correccion en `docs/security/NESA-01-control-acceso-ofertas.md`.

## Vulnerabilidad reproducida

Para la demostracion se utilizo una solicitud que intentaba crear una oferta usando el identificador de otra cliente:

- Usuario autenticado: Pablo Gutierrez  
  `32cc0909-d949-xxxx-adc2-xxxxxx`

- Identificador enviado maliciosamente: Gabriela Salazar  
  `52be19bf-0eb1-xxxx-a366-xxxxxx`

### Version vulnerable

En la rama `evidencia/version-vulnerable-base`, la oferta creada con id `55` fue almacenada con el identificador manipulado de Gabriela:

cliente_id = 52be19bf-0eb1-xxxx-a366-xxxxx

author: hherb
body:
## Summary

- Closes #126 via option (b) from the issue body: document at the call site why `SynthesisSession::push_text` / `finalize` are deliberately not wrapped in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, and what would have to change for the wrap to matter.
- No behaviour change. Comment-only edit in [`primer-speech/src/voice_loop/state_machine.rs`](src/crates/primer-speech/src/voice_loop/state_machine.rs).

## Why option (b), not option (a)

The issue body and the [`NEXT_SESSION.md`](NEXT_SESSION.md) brief sketched option (a) (actually wrap in `spawn_blocking`) as the "safer choice", but a careful reread of the macOS-native CLI architecture shows option (a) would deadlock that build:

- `primer-cli` is wired to `Builder::new_current_thread()` on the OS main thread when built with `macos-native` or `macos-native-26` (see [primer-cli/src/main.rs#L480-L498](src/crates/primer-cli/src/main.rs#L480-L498)). That is the only configuration in which `AVSpeechSynthesizer`'s main-thread contract is satisfied for the streaming path.
- `spawn_blocking` would hop synthesis off the OS main thread to a tokio blocking-pool worker; `synthesize_streaming` then sees `is_main_thread() == false` and takes the background-thread branch, which bounces work onto GCD main via `dispatch2::DispatchQueue::main().exec_async(...)`.
- Per the macOS-native bullet in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), the GCD-main bounce **only drains when the OS main thread is owned by `NSApplicationMain` or `dispatch_main()`**. The CLI's main thread is running tokio, not AppKit — so the bounced work is queued on GCD main but nothing dequeues it, and synthesis never returns.

The other two production backends (macOS-native GUI, Piper Linux) tolerate the direct sync call: one worker is blocked for the synth duration, other workers keep running, and the GUI's GCD bounce drains because Tauri owns main via `NSApplicationMain`.

The new comment block documents all three cases and the explicit conditions under which the wrap would become correct (multi-tenant non-Apple runtime starving background tasks during SPEAK; new backend that doesn't require main-thread access; macOS-native CLI moving off `new_current_thread`).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` → 858/0/3 (matches brief baseline)
- [x] `cargo test -p primer-speech --features macos-native` → 49/0/3
- [x] `cargo test -p primer-cli --features speech,macos-native` → 12/0/0
- [x] `cargo test -p primer-cli --features speech` → 12/0/0
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p primer-speech --features macos-native --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean
- [x] `cargo build -p primer-gui --features speech` → clean
- [ ] Optional manual: voice-mode mic round-trip on macOS-native CLI (no code path changed; smoke is purely confirmatory)

author: realroc
body:
## Summary
- Default MyCalFix's fix session to `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions <prompt>` so the user isn't pelted with Approve/Deny prompts mid-session
- Add `mycalfix_interactive_claude` knob in `~/.config/my-calendar/config.json` (strict JSON-bool, default `false`) as the safety valve for PRs the user wants to babysit
- Knob lives in a new `scripts/mycalfix_config.py` (doesn't pull pyobjc into the launch path) and is shelled out from `launch_fix.sh` via a `claude-flag` subcommand
- Doc + design-tradeoffs section in `AGENTS.md` updated with the security argument (worktree isolation + Terminal-side remote validation + prompt hard constraints) and the residual prompt-injection risk that the knob exists to mitigate

## Follow-up fixes folded into this PR

### `mycalfix_config.py` not bundled into `MyCalFix.app` (codex review on this PR)
`launch_fix.sh` resolves the helper via `$HERE/mycalfix_config.py`, but `install_app.sh` only copied launcher + parser + prompt. Real installs missed `Contents/Resources/mycalfix_config.py`; the helper call failed and `launch_fix.sh`'s fail-safe silently fell back to `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, nullifying the `mycalfix_interactive_claude: true` safety valve. `install_app.sh` now copies the helper and smoke-tests it (`claude-flag` under a clean HOME must emit `--dangerously-skip-permissions`); `InstallAppBundleManifestTests` statically verifies every `$HERE/<helper>` reference is in the copy manifest. Commit `f58143c`.

### `launch_fix.sh` python heredoc quoting regression — also fixes #25 (P0)
PR #19 rewrote the `cmd=$(python3 -c '<source>')` block into a python f-string with many literal single quotes (`printf '%s'`, `sed -E 's|...|'`). bash's outer `'...'` closed early, leaving `s|(\.git)?/*$||` as bare shell tokens and aborting the command substitution with `syntax error near unexpected token ?/*$'`. The .command file was never written, Terminal never launched, and every codex review with verdict ⚠️/❌ produced a dead `mycalfix://` URL from the day PR #19 merged. `bash -n` did not catch this — the static parser doesn't descend into `$(...)` bodies. Switched to a `python3 - <<'PYEOF'` heredoc so literal `'` inside the python source no longer matter, and added `LaunchFixCommandFileRenderTests` that drives `launch_fix.sh` end-to-end with a stubbed `open` and asserts the `.command` file parses + contains the renderer's marker strings. Without this fix, the manual smoke below cannot be performed at all. Commit `c5b50d3`.

## Why this is safe by default
1. Worktree is disposable: `~/.cache/my-calendar/worktrees/<repo>__<branch>__<ts>` — wrong outcome means `git worktree remove`, main checkout untouched
2. User-triggered: every session starts from a click on a `mycalfix://` URL (informed consent each time)
3. `fix_prompt.md` has the hard caps: diff >200 lines abort, only touch what review names, no `--force` push
4. Terminal-side validation (PR #19) verifies `git remote get-url origin` matches URL's `repo=` **before** fetch/worktree-add, so a wrong path can't push to the wrong remote
5. Knob lets users dial back to per-tool approvals when reviewing a PR they're unsure about

## Residual risk

author: matiasjrossi
body:
## Summary

Fixes a startup-time race where the integration permanently fails to load if the OIDC discovery endpoint (`configure_url`) is briefly unreachable when Home Assistant boots — only a manual HA restart recovers it. Common on reboots where HA shares a host with its IdP (Authentik, Authelia, Pocket-ID, etc.) and DNS/the IdP container come up just after HA.

Same user-facing symptom as upstream [cavefire/hass-openid#62](https://github.com/cavefire/hass-openid/issues/62), via a different code path post-refactor — `_async_prepare_config` raising in the YAML setup path rather than `fetch_urls` silently swallowing the exception.

## What it does

- `async_setup_entry`: wrap the `_async_prepare_config` call and raise `ConfigEntryNotReady` on failure, so HA retries with its standard exponential backoff instead of marking the entry dead.
- `async_setup` (YAML path): on initial discovery failure, log a warning and forward the raw YAML data to the import flow without the discovered fields. The created config entry then goes through the `ConfigEntryNotReady` retry path above, so once the IdP is reachable the entry loads cleanly. On the next HA start, if YAML discovery succeeds, the import flow updates the entry with the full data as before.

## Symptom this fixes

```
ERROR (MainThread) [custom_components.openid] Failed to prepare YAML OpenID configuration: Configuration endpoint returned 404
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.setup] Setup failed for custom integration 'openid': Integration failed to initialize.
```

After the patch, this becomes a `WARNING` and the config entry is then retried automatically until the IdP is reachable.

## Who actually benefits

Worth being explicit, because it's narrower than "everyone who's ever had a startup race" — `_async_prepare_config` short-circuits discovery if `authorize_url`/`token_url`/`user_info_url`/`use_pkce` are already cached on the entry:

```python
needs_discovery = (
    any(key not in config for key in (CONF_AUTHORIZE_URL, CONF_TOKEN_URL, CONF_USER_INFO_URL))
    or CONF_USE_PKCE not in config
)
if not needs_discovery:
    return config
```

So the bug only manifests for:

- **Fresh installs** — no cached endpoints, discovery is required. **Primary impact**; matches the symptom in #62 and the incident this PR was written for.
- **Entries that lost their cache** somehow (partial `.storage` reset, manual cleanup, etc.).
- **The first YAML-import discovery on each HA start** — `async_setup` operates on raw YAML, not entry data, so it always hits the network even when the entry would have otherwise skipped discovery. This was the failing path in my incident: integration was returning `False` from `async_setup`, so the (working) entry-data cache never got a chance to load.

Existing entries with a healthy previous cache are not affected by the boot race because discovery isn't attempted.

## Manual verification

Reproduced and fixed on Home Assistant 2026.4.4 + Authentik. Procedure:

1. Stopped HA. In `.storage/core.config_entries`, stripped `authorize_url`, `token_url`, `user_info_url`, `logout_url`, `use_pkce` from the existing openid entry to simulate a fresh-install state where discovery is required.
2. Pointed `configure_url` at a path Authentik returns `404` on (`/application/o/nonexistent/.well-known/openid-configuration`).
3. Started HA.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| **Without patch** | `state=not_loaded`. Integration dead until manual HA restart. |
| **With patch** | `state=setup_retry`  `reason="Failed to prepare OpenID configuration: Configuration endpoint returned 404"`. HA's exponential-backoff retry loop engaged. |

4. Restored `configure_url` to the working URL, restarted HA. Integration loaded cleanly and entry data was re-populated by fresh discovery.

A simpler initial test (broken `configure_url` without stripping cached fields) found the integration still loaded — useful surfacing of the `needs_discovery` short-circuit behavior above, even though it doesn't exercise the patched path.

## Scope notes

- Behavior on a *configuration* error (bad client_id/secret, malformed YAML, etc.) is unchanged — those still propagate from the import flow / entry setup as before.
- Behavior when discovery succeeds is unchanged — happy path takes the same branch it always did.
- The `Exception` catches are intentionally broad to match the existing style in `async_setup` and because `_async_prepare_config` can raise anything aiohttp throws (`ClientError`, `asyncio.TimeoutError`, custom `RuntimeError`, etc.) — all of which deserve the same retry treatment.

author: art3m4ik3
body:
## Summary

- **BrowserPool** — держит N браузеров Camoufox живыми, раздаёт через `asyncio.Queue`. Поддерживает async context manager и ручной `start()`/`stop()`. Устраняет overhead холодного старта браузера на каждый запрос.
- **ChallengeCache** — TTL-кэш результатов по ключу `(domain, challenge_type)`. Для Challenge-типа TTL автоматически вычисляется из времени истечения cookie `cf_clearance`. API: `get`, `set`, `invalidate`, `clear`.
- **`solve_batch(links, concurrency=None)`** — параллельное решение списка URL через `asyncio.gather` с опциональным ограничением через `asyncio.Semaphore`. Результаты возвращаются в том же порядке.
- **`on_success` / `on_failure` callbacks** — принимают sync и async callable, вызываются после каждого solve (включая cache hit) и при каждой ошибке.
- **`timeout`** — ограничение времени на один вызов `solve` через `asyncio.wait_for`.
- **Cookie isolation** — переключено на `browser.new_context()` per solve, чтобы pooled браузеры не протекали cookies между параллельными запросами.

Все фичи opt-in и полностью совместимы с оригинальным API.

## Test plan

- [ ] `solve()` без pool и cache работает как раньше
- [ ] `BrowserPool` корректно стартует/останавливается как context manager
- [ ] `ChallengeCache` возвращает результат из кэша на второй вызов для того же домена
- [ ] `solve_batch()` возвращает результаты в порядке входного списка
- [ ] `on_success` и `on_failure` вызываются для sync и async callables
- [ ] `timeout` прерывает зависший solve и вызывает `on_failure`

author: uotw
body:
## Summary
Three small, independent UX improvements that emerged while testing the scheduler fix in #51 on a large image:

1. **Progress gauge in the status bar.** Adds a fixed-width third status bar field with an embedded `wxGauge`. Driven from the existing progress-text events, filtered to only show during the slow L-R deconvolution step (whose text contains "deconvolution"). Tone curve / unsharp mask events complete in milliseconds and were noisy and useless as gauge drivers.

2. **Quieter status text.** Previously the status text would flicker through `Applying tone curve: 0%` → `100%` → `Idle` for every curve drag — pure noise. Now the text field only updates for the slow step and the terminal `Idle` state.

3. **Default to fit-in-window on every image open.** A freshly opened image is much more useful framed than at 100% with only one corner visible. Extracted the existing fit-in-window toggle logic into a `SetFitImageInWindow` helper and call it at the end of `OpenFile`. Users can still toggle fit off afterwards. Subsequent opens also pick up the right fit ratio because the helper unconditionally recomputes.

## Notes
Independent of PR #51 (scheduler fix). They can land in either order.

If you would prefer any of the three as a separate PR, happy to split.

## Test plan
- [x] Build + run on macOS Tahoe (Apple Silicon, wxWidgets 3.3.2)
- [x] Gauge visible during slow whole-image L-R, hidden during rapid curve drags
- [x] Status text reads `L-R deconvolution: X%` during slow step, `Idle` otherwise; no flicker on curve drag
- [x] Opening a new image fits it to the window; subsequent opens re-fit to the new image dimensions; manual zoom still works and toggles fit off
